title: Fermented Shrimp
steps: Put the shrimp into a bowl, cover with the fish sauce, then add the salt, ground rice, and galangal, and mix until thoroughly combined. Cover with plastic wrap (clingfilm) and let ferment for 3-5 days until the taste becomes sour.

title: Fermented Soybeans
prepTime: 10 minutes, plus soaking and fermenting time
steps: Rinse the soybeans several times with cold water. Soak overnight in a bowl of water, then drain. Bring a pan of water to a boil, add the soybeans, reduce the heat, and simmer for 4-6 hours until soft. Drain.

Divide the soybeans into 8-10 portions. Put each portion in the center of a banana leaf, fold the sides and ends over the soybeans, and secure with string. Put a plate or another firm weight on top and ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days.
The fermented soybeans are then ready to use. To make dried soybean sheets, remove the beans from the leaves, shape them into balls, flatten into thin circles, and sun-dry for 2-3 days.

title: Chili Jam
ingredients: 5 dried red bird's eye chiles, seeded
2½ tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Dry-fry both kinds of dried chile in a wok over medium heat for 3-4 minutes until fragrant and toasted. Transfer to a plate. Add the garlic and shallots to the wok and dry-fry for 5-6 minutes until softened and the garlic skins are slightly burned. Set aside.
Pound the toasted chiles with the salt in a mortar until finely flaked. Add the garlic and shallots and pound until smooth. Add the dried shrimp and shrimp paste and pound until thoroughly combined.

Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the paste and cook for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Add the tamarind, fish sauce, and sugar and stir for about 4 minutes. Transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving 1 cm headspace. Cool, cover, and seal. Refrigerate for up to 2 weeks.

title: Cucumber Relish
ingredients: 1 small cucumber (50 g), halved lengthwise and thinly sliced
steps: Put the vinegar, sugar, and salt into a small pan over low-medium heat and stir until the sugar has dissolved. Bring to a boil and cook for about 4 minutes or until the mixture turns slightly syrupy. Remove from the heat and let cool completely. Add the cucumber, shallots and chile and serve. Alternatively, transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving 1 cm head space, cover, and seal. Store in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

title: Kaeng Som Chili Paste
ingredients: 10 dried red bird's eye chiles, seeded
steps: Soak the dried chiles in a bowl of hot water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop. Pound the chiles and salt in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Gradually add the lemongrass, fingerroot, galangal, garlic, and shallots and continue to pound until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and pound until smooth and thoroughly combined. Use the paste immediately. About 100 ml chili paste is needed for 1 kg of meat. Alternatively, transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving 1 cm head space, cover, and seal. Store in the refrigerator for up to 2-3 weeks.

title: Roasted Shrimp Paste
steps: Lay the banana leaf on a work surface, spoon the shrimp paste into the center of the leaf, and gently press to flatten the shrimp paste. Cover the paste with the sides of the leaf, fold over the ends, and secure with a toothpick.

Hold the banana-leaf package over a low gas flame for about 5 minutes, turning it from time to time until the leaf is charred and the shrimp paste is fragrant,. Alternatively, preheat the oven to 400°F/200°C/Gas Mark 6 and roast the banana leaf package for about 10 minutes or until fragrant.

title: Green Curry Paste
ingredients: 1 tablespoon finely chopped kaffir lime zest
steps: Dry-fry the coriander and cumin in a small pan over medium heat for 1 minute until fragrant and lightly toasted. Transfer to a mortar, add the peppercorns, and pound with a pestle until a fine powder. Set aside. Pound both chiles and the salt together in the mortar with the pestle until smooth. Gradually add the galangal, cilantro (coriander) root, kaffir lime zest, lemongrass, garlic, and shallots and pound until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and spice mix and pound again until smooth and thoroughly combined. Use the paste immediately. Alternatively, transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving 1 cm head space, cover, and seal. Store in the refrigerator for up to 2-3 weeks.

title: Spicy Chili Paste
ingredients: 250 g catfish or another firm-fleshed white fish, cleaned
2 small garlic bulbs, cloves separated and chopped
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
steps: Heat the broiler (grill) to medium-high. Place the fish on the broiler (grill) rack and broil (grill) on both sides for about 15 minutes until dry and cooked. Remove from the broiler, let cool, and then remove and discard the bones and shred the flesh. Set aside.

Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the shallots and garlic, and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes or until golden brown. Transfer to a plate and set aside. Add the chiles to the wok and stir-fry for about 5 minutes or until they start to blacken. Remove from the heat.
Pound the shallot, garlic, chiles, sugar, tamarind, and salt in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the grilled (broiled) fish and pound again until thoroughly combined. Serve with rice.

title: Red Curry Paste
ingredients: 10 dried red bird's eye chiles, seeded
1 tablespoon finely chopped kaffir lime zest
steps: Soak both kinds of dried chile in a bowl of hot water for 15 minutes, then drain and chop. Toast the coriander and cumin in a small pan over medium heat for 1 minute until fragrant. Transfer to a mortar, add the white peppercorns, and pound until finely ground. Set aside.

Pound the chiles and salt in the mortar until smooth. Gradually add the galangal, cilantro (coriander) root, kaffir lime zest, lemongrass, shallots, and garlic and continue to pound until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and toasted spices and pound until thoroughly combined. Use immediately, or transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving 1 cm headspace. Cover, seal, and refrigerate for up to 2-3 weeks.

title: Southern Chili Paste
ingredients: 10-15 dried red bird's eye chiles, seeded
steps: Soak the chiles in a bowl of hot water for 20 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop. Transfer to a mortar with the salt and pound with a pestle until it forms fine flakes. Gradually add the lemongrass, galangal, peppercorns, turmeric, garlic, and shallots and pound until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and pound until smooth and thoroughly combined Use the paste immediately. Alternatively, transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving 1 cm head space, cover, and seal. Store in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 weeks.

title: Massaman Curry Paste
steps: Soak the dried chiles in a bowl of hot water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain, chop, and set aside.

Dry-fry the star anise, cinnamon, cardamom, black peppercorns, coriander, and cumin in a pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes, or until brown and fragrant. Transfer to a mortar, grind to a powder, and set aside.
In the same pan, dry-fry the garlic, shallots, lemongrass, and galangal over medium heat for 2-3 minutes, or until brown and fragrant. Transfer to a mortar and pound.
Add the soaked chiles, ground spices, salt, and shrimp paste and pound until thoroughly combined and smooth.
Use immediately, or transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving 1 cm headspace. Cover, seal, and refrigerate for up to 2-3 weeks.

title: Spicy Curry Paste
ingredients: 10 dried red bird's eye chiles, seeded
1 tablespoon finely chopped kaffir lime zest
steps: Soak both the dried chiles in a bowl of hot water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop. Transfer to a mortar with the salt and pound thoroughly with a pestle. Gradually add the lemongrass, galangal, lime zest, fingerroots, peppercorns, garlic, cilantro (coriander) root, and shallots and pound until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and pound until thoroughly combined. Use the paste immediately. About 100 ml chili paste is needed for 1 kg of meat. Alternatively, transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving ½ inch/1 cm headspace, cover, and seal. Store in the refrigerator for up to 2-3 weeks.

title: Larb Chili Paste
steps: Dry-fry the bird's-eye chiles in a wok over medium heat for 2-3 minutes, until fragrant, then set aside.
Dry-fry the shallots, garlic, and long red peppers in the same wok for about 2 minutes, until softened and golden, then set aside.
Dry-fry the lemongrass, dill seeds, fennel seeds, peppercorns, nutmeg, cardamom pods, cloves, and cumin seeds for 3-4 minutes, until fragrant and toasted. Let cool.
Pound the dried chiles and salt in a mortar to fine flakes. Add the garlic and pound until smooth, then gradually add the remaining toasted ingredients and continue pounding to a smooth paste.
Use immediately, or transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving 1 cm headspace. Cover, seal, and refrigerate for up to 2-3 weeks.

title: Northern-Style Chili Paste
ingredients: 1 garlic bulb, cloves separated and chopped
steps: Pound the garlic and chiles together in a mortar with a pestle to make a coarse paste.
Add the salt, lime juice, and oil and stir until thoroughly combined.
Use immediately, or transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving 1 cm headspace. Cover, seal, and refrigerate for up to 2-3 weeks.

title: Saam-gler
steps: Pound the cilantro (coriander) root briefly in a mortar with a pestle. Add the garlic and continue to pound until a coarse paste. Add the peppercorns and pound to a fine paste. Use the paste immediately. Alternatively, transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving 1 cm head space, cover, and seal. Store in the refrigerator for up to 3 weeks.

title: Fermented Soybean Chili Dip
ingredients: 2 small banana-leaf packages Fermented Soybeans (see p. 34)
2 garlic bulbs, cloves separated and chopped
Raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumbers and round eggplants, to serve
steps: Preheat a charcoal or gas grill to 160°C, or preheat an indoor broiler to medium-low.
Grill the fermented soybean packages for 4-5 minutes on each side. Remove them from the heat, unwrap, and discard the banana leaves.
Pound the dried chiles, garlic, salt, and grilled fermented soybeans in a mortar until combined. Mix in the fermented fish sauce and serve with raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Yellow Curry Paste
ingredients: 1 x ⅝-inch/1½ cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and sliced
steps: Soak the dried chiles in a bowl of hot water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Dry-fry the garlic and ginger in a wok over medium heat for 5 minutes, until fragrant and browned. Set aside.
Pound the chiles and salt in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the lemongrass and galangal and continue pounding until thoroughly combined.
Add the roasted garlic and ginger and pound until well mixed. Add the shallots, then the coriander, curry powder, turmeric, cumin, and shrimp paste, and pound to a smooth paste.

title: Fermented Vegetable Chili Dip
prepTime: 10 minutes plus fermenting and cooling time
ingredients: 2 tablespoons cooled Glutinous Rice (see p. 378). cooking water reserved
steps: Mix the lettuce and sea salt together in a large bowl. Add the cooked rice and 120 ml reserved rice water and mix well. Put the mixture into a stainless steel container, cover with a tight-fitting lid, and let ferment for 2-3 days.
Put the fermented mixture in a large pan and simmer for 5-10 minutes until soft. Remove from the heat and let cool.

For the chili paste, pound the chiles, garlic, salt, and peppercorns together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the mackerel to the chili paste and pound again until thoroughly combined. Mix with the fermented mixture. Transfer to a serving bowl, garnish with the chopped scallions (spring onions) and cilantro (coriander), and serve with roasted fish.

title: Spicy Mushroom Dip
ingredients: 1 x 200 g tilapia or sea bass fillet
1 handful of mint, chopped, to garnish
raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumber, Chinese greens (leaves), yard-long beans, and lettuce
steps: Bring a pan of water to a boil over medium heat, add the beans and mushrooms, and boil for 5 minutes. Drain, chop into small pieces, and set aside.

Bring 350 ml water to a boil in a large pan enough over medium heat. Add the salt. Gently put the fish in the pan, reduce the heat to low, and simmer for 6-7 minutes until cooked. Drain, let cool slightly, then remove and discard the skin. Set aside.
Grind the sesame seeds in a mortar with a pestle until a very fine powder. Remove and set aside.

Toast the chiles and shallots in a wok over medium heat until softened and slightly burned. Transfer to the mortar and pound to a paste, then add the ground sesame seeds and pound again. Add the mushrooms, beans, and fish and pound until thoroughly combined. Season with the fish sauce, and the scallion and both kinds of cilantro. and stir until well mixed. Transfer to a bowl and garnish with mint leaves. Serve with rice and raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Dried Spicy Fried Tilapia Dip
ingredients: 250 g dried catfish or snakehead, finely pounded
raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumber, Chinese greens (leaves), carrots, and yard-long beans, to serve
steps: Heat the tamarind in a wok over medium heat. Add the sugar, salt, and vinegar and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring continuously until the mixture starts to become sticky. Remove from the heat and set aside.

Put the pounded dried fish, the fried garlic, chili flakes, and fried fish flesh in a large bowl and stir until combined. Pour in the tamarind mixture and mix again thoroughly, then process in a food processor until ground and crumbly. Serve in a bowl with raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Fermented Catfish Chili Dip
ingredients: 1 x 300 g fermented catfish, finely chopped
raw vegetables, such as white turmeric, cucumbers, round eggplants (aubergines), wing beans, lotus stems, and yard-long beans, to serve
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat, add the fish, and cook for 3-4 minutes. Add the lemongrass, shallots, and fingerroots and stir-fry for 5 minutes. Add the chiles, sawtooth cilantro (coriander), and kaffir lime leaves and cook for another 5 minutes. Serve in a bowl with raw vegetables.

title: Broiled Mackerel Dip
ingredients: 3 × 275 g horse mackerel (or 130 g smoked mackerel fillet)
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p.378), to serve
raw vegetables such as cucumber, Chinese greens (leaves), wing beans, or carrots
steps: Preheat the boiler (grill) to medium-high. Individually wrap the mackerel in a banana leaf and secure with a toothpick. Place the packages on the boiler (grill) rack and broil (grill) for 5-6 minutes on each side, until cooked. Unwrap the fish from the banana leaves and discard the skin, bones, and the leaves. Set aside the fish flesh.

Toast the chiles in a wok over medium heat for 4 minutes or until soft and the skin slightly burned. Transfer to a plate. Add the garlic and shallots to the wok and toast for 6-7 minutes or until soft and slightly burned. Put the chiles, shallots, and garlic in a mortar and pound with a pestle until smooth. Add the fish and pound until smooth, then add the salt, sugar, fish sauce, lime juice, and 4 tablespoons warm water. Gently mix together. Serve in a bowl with rice and raw vegetables.

title: Spicy Fermented Fish Dip
ingredients: 65 g peeled and seeded sour tamarind pods
6 Kaffir lime leaves, finely sliced, plus extra to garnish
raw vegetables, such as mustard greens, Chinese greens (leaves), and cucumbers, to serve
steps: Preheat the broiler (grill) to medium. Wrap the fermented fish in a banana leaf, place on the broiler (grill) pan, and broil (grill) for 3-4 minutes until the banana leaf is brown and fragrant. Alternatively, cook the wrapped fish in a pan. Unwrap the fermented fish, remove and discard the fish bone, and set aside.

Dry-fry the lemongrass, shallots, galangal, and garlic in a wok over medium heat for 5-6 minutes until brown and fragrant. Remove and pound thoroughly in a mortar with a pestle. Set aside in the mortar.
Toast the chili flakes in the wok over medium heat for about 1 minute or until fragrant. Remove and set aside.

Chop the fermented fish and tamarind on a cutting (chopping) board until a smooth chopped mixture forms. Add to the mortar and pound until combined. Add the sugar, chili flakes, and kaffir lime leaves and pound again until thoroughly combined. Transfer to a bowl and garnish with the remaining lime leaves. Serve with raw vegetables.

title: Spicy Fermented Shrimp Dip
ingredients: 1 tablespoon sliced red and green bird's eye chiles
1 × 2 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and sliced
2 tablespoons thinly sliced round yellow eggplants
raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumbers and round eggplants (aubergines)
steps: Put the fermented shrimp in a pan and cook over low heat for 3-4 minutes. Bring to a boil, then remove from the heat, add the remaining ingredients, and mix together until thoroughly combined. Serve in a bowl with rice and raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Spicy Shrimp Dip
ingredients: 2.5 cm piece galangal, peeled and sliced
raw or steamed vegetables, such as carrots, cucumber, napa (Chinese) cabbage, and round eggplants (aubergines), to serve
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the shrimp and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until cooked. Set aside.

Finely pound the chiles, garlic, and galangal in a mortar with a pestle. Add the shrimp, toasted rice, fish sauce, lime juice, and fermented fish sauce and mix thoroughly. Add the scallions (spring onions), both cilantro (coriander), dill, and peppermint leaves and mix well. Serve in a bowl with raw vegetables.

title: Fresh Shrimp Chili Dip
ingredients: 100 g uncooked jumbo shrimp (king prawns), peeled, deveined, and diced
2 red spur chiles, cut into 2 cm pieces
2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
raw or steamed vegetables, such as carrots, cucumber, napa (Chinese) cabbage, and round eggplants (aubergines), to serve
steps: Bring 4 tablespoons water to a boil in a small pan. Add the shrimp and stir for 1 minute. When the shrimp start to turn pink, remove from the heat and keep stirring until fully cooked. Set aside and reserve the cooking liquid.
Heat the oil in a wok over low-medium heat. Add the garlic, both kinds of chile, and shallots and stir continuously for 5-6 minutes, or until the shallots turn dark brown.
Pound the shallot mixture in a mortar with a pestle. Add the shrimp paste and salt and continue pounding to a fine paste.
Season with the sugar, lime juice, tamarind, fish sauce, and 1¼ tablespoons of the reserved cooking liquid and stir. Add the cooked shrimp.
Serve in a bowl with steamed rice and raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Shrimp Chili Dip
ingredients: 4-5 red or orange spur chiles, chopped
4-6 red or green bird's-eye chiles, chopped, plus extra whole chiles to garnish
3 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1 handful of pea eggplants (aubergines), to garnish
raw and steamed vegetables, such as carrots, cucumber, napa (Chinese) cabbage, and round eggplants (aubergines), to serve
steps: Pound the garlic and both chiles together in a mortar with a pestle. Add the eggplant (aubergine) and pound to a smooth paste. Add the shrimp paste and mix until thoroughly combined. Season with the lime juice, fish sauce, and sugar. Transfer to a bowl and garnish with pea eggplants (aubergines) and extra bird's eye chiles. Serve with grilled fish and raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Fermented Fish Chili Dip
ingredients: 1 x 2 cm piece fingerroot, peeled and sliced
3-5 green, red, and yellow finger chiles, sliced
1-2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
120 g bamboo shoots, boiled and finely chopped
185 g yard-long beans, cut into 2.5 cm pieces
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
Raw or steamed vegetables, such as bamboo shoots, cabbage, carrots, and cucumber, to serve
steps: Heat the fermented fish sauce and coconut milk in a wok over low heat and simmer for 3-4 minutes, until any pieces of fish melt.
Strain through cheesecloth (muslin) into a heatproof bowl, then return the liquid to the wok.
Add the shallots, fingerroot, kaffir lime leaves, chiles, sugar, and fish sauce and bring to a boil. Add the pork and boil for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until cooked.
Add the bamboo shoots and eggplants, pour in the coconut cream, and add the yard-long beans. Stir, then remove from the heat. Serve with rice and raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Shrimp Paste and Coconut Milk Dip
ingredients: 1½ tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
50 g shrimp (prawns), peeled, deveined, and ground (minced)
4-6 dried red bird's eye chiles, seeded
1 x Y 1 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped
raw or steamed vegetables, such as pumpkin, wing beans, round eggplants (aubergines), cucumber, and yard long beans
steps: To make the chili paste, pound the chiles and garlic in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Gradually add the lemongrass, galangal. fingerroots, and shallot and pound thoroughly until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and pound to a smooth paste. Set aside. Heat the coconut milk in a wok over medium heat for 3-4 minutes until the oil separates from the coconut milk. Add the chili paste and stir for 1-2 minutes until fragrant and the paste and coconut milk are mixed well Simmer for 1-2 minutes, then add the sugar, fish sauce, and tamarind and mix well until the sugar has dissolved. Add the shrimp (prawns), kaffir lime, and green chiles. Cook for another 2 minutes or until thickened. Serve in a bowl with raw or steamed vegetables and the boiled egg.

title: Eggplant Dip with Pork
ingredients: 400 g long green eggplants, quartered crosswise
Raw or steamed vegetables, such as Chinese greens, cucumber, carrots, and yard-long beans, to serve
1 tablespoon Fried Garlic (see p. 64), to garnish
1 small handful mint leaves, to garnish
steps: Brush a griddle or stove-top grill pan with the oil. Grill the eggplants over medium heat for 10-13 minutes, until softened and their skins are charred. Let cool, peel, and set aside.
Dry-fry the chiles in a wok or pan over medium-high heat for 15 minutes, until softened and charred. Let cool, peel, and set aside.
In the same wok, dry-fry the garlic and shallots for 5-6 minutes, until softened and lightly charred.
Bring 75 ml water to a boil in a small pan. Add the pork and blanch for 1-2 minutes, until cooked, then drain.
Pound the garlic, shallots, and shrimp paste in a mortar. Add the chiles, eggplant, pork, salt, and fish sauce and mix gently with a spoon. Fold in the chopped eggs.
Garnish with fried garlic and mint leaves and serve with raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Spicy Tamarind Dip
ingredients: 200 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumber, round eggplants (aubergines), and yard-long beans, to serve
steps: To make the chili paste, finely pound the chiles, tamarind, garlic, and shallots in a mortar with a pestle. Add the shrimp paste and pound until smooth and thoroughly combined.

Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the chili paste, and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Add the pork and sugar and cook for about 7 minutes or until the pork is cooked. Serve in a bowl with raw or steamed vegetables. Alternatively, transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving 1 cm head space, cover, and seal. Store in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

title: Pork and Tomato Chili Dip
ingredients: raw or steamed vegetables, such as carrots, mustard greens, Chinese greens (leaves), and cucumbers, to serve
steps: Soak the dried chiles in a bowl of hot water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.

Pound the chiles, shallots, garlic, and half the salt in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the pork and pound again until well mixed. Add the tomatoes and gently press into the mixture, then coarsely pound until combined. Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the pounded tomato mixture and stir-fry for about 4 minutes or until fragrant. Add a small amount of water and season with the fish sauce, sugar, and the remaining salt. Stir until well mixed Cook for another 6-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes are cooked and the dip is fully flavored.
Transfer to a bowl and garnish with the cilantro (coriander) and scallions (spring onions). Serve with raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Spicy Dip with Rice Crackers
ingredients: 8 uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled, deveined, and finely chopped
steps: Finely pound the cilantro (coriander) root garlic, and peppercorns in a mortar with a pestle, then set aside.

Heat 200 ml coconut milk in a wok over low heat. Add the pounded cilantro root mixture and stir until the coconut oil separates and becomes fragrant. Add the pork and shrimp (prawns) and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until nearly cooked. Add the shallots and remaining coconut milk and stir- fry for 3-4 minutes. Season with the sugar, fish sauce, and tamarind. Add the peanuts and stir thoroughly. Serve in a bowl with rice crackers.

title: Pickled Bamboo Shoot Dip
ingredients: 120 g pickled bamboo shoots (sour and salty version)
raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumber, cabbage, and lettuce
steps: Blanch the ground (minced) pork in a pan of boiling water for 1 minute or until cooked. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the bamboo shoots in another pan of boiling water for about 2 minutes to reduce their sourness and saltiness. Drain and set aside.

Dry-fry the garlic and chiles in a wok over medium heat for 4-5 minutes, until softened and slightly burned. Transfer to a mortar and pound thoroughly. Add the bamboo shoots and pound until just before they break into small pieces. Add the blanched pork and pound coarsely until thoroughly combined. Season to taste.
Transfer to a bowl and garnish with the scallions and cilantro. Serve with the pork cracklings and raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Spicy Frog Dip
ingredients: 2 lemongrass stalks, cut into 2.5 cm pieces
100 g young tamarind leaves or sorrel leaves
raw or steamed vegetables, such as yard-long beans, round eggplants (aubergines), and winged beans
steps: Dry-fry the chiles in a wok over medium heat for 3-4 minutes until fragrant and toasted, then transfer to a plate and set aside.

Bring 475 ml water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the galangal, lemongrass, fermented fish sauce, and frog meat and cook for 5 minutes or until the meat is cooked. Add the young tamarind leaves stir, and remove from the heat. Remove the frog meat with a slotted spoon and set aside. Reserve the broth (stock).

Pound the chiles in a mortar with a pestle to form fine Flakes, then add the boiled frog meat and pound coarsely. Add 2-3 tablespoons of the frog broth and the fish sauce and mix well. Transfer to a bowl and garnish with the cilantro (coriander), scallion (spring onion), and Vietnamese cilantro leaves. Serve with raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Galangal Chili Dip
ingredients: 4 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped
raw or steamed vegetables, such as mushrooms, cucumber, and napa cabbage
steps: Preheat the broiler (grill) to high.
Crush the galangal and garlic in a mortar with a pestle, then remove and set aside.
Put the dried chiles on the broiler rack and broil for a few minutes until slightly burned. Transfer to the mortar, add the crushed galangal and garlic, and pound until thoroughly combined.
Season with the salt and serve in a bowl with raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Spicy Tomato Dip
ingredients: Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p.378), to serve
raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumber and round eggplants (aubergines)
steps: Heat the broiler (grill) to medium-high, Put the tomatoes onto the broiler (grill) rack and grill (broil) for 5-6 minutes until softened and the skins are charred.

Dry-fry the lemongrass, chiles, shallots, galangal, and garlic in a wok over medium heat for 4-5 minutes until fragrant and lightly toasted. Transfer to a mortar and pound with a pestle until smooth. Add the broiled (grilled) tomatoes and gently press with the pestle until combined. Add the fermented fish flesh, tamarind, lime juice, and kaffir lime leaves and stir until well mixed. Serve in a bowl with rice and raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Roasted Chili Dip
ingredients: 50 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
5 bitter orange leaves, coarsely sliced, to garnish
Raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumber and round eggplants (aubergines), to serve
1 x 10 cm piece red galangal, peeled and finely chopped
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of hot water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain.
Pound the chiles, garlic, shallots, lemongrass, red galangal, and cardamom leaves in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the dried shrimp and shrimp paste and pound again until combined.
Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a wok over medium heat and boil for 4-5 minutes, until it develops a grainy texture.
Add the chili paste, sugar, salt, and kaffir lime leaves and simmer for 3-4 minutes. Transfer to a bowl, garnish with the bitter orange leaves, and serve with raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Spicy Green Mango Dip
ingredients: 1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
80 g shredded unripe green (sour) mango or green apple, plus extra to garnish
Raw vegetables, such as cauliflower and cucumber, to serve
steps: Pound the chiles and garlic in a mortar with a pestle until smooth.
Add the sugar and shrimp paste and continue to pound until combined.
Add the mango or apple, dried shrimp, fish sauce, lime juice, and 2 tablespoons warm water and gently mix.
Garnish with shredded mango or apple and serve with raw vegetables.

title: Spicy Salacca Dip
ingredients: 10 red and green bird's eye chiles, chopped
2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
raw or steamed vegetables, such as carrots and cucumber to serve
steps: Pound the garlic, shallots, chiles, and shrimp paste in a mortar with a pestle. Add the snake fruit and pound again until combined. Add the sugar, and fish sauce, and mix well. Serve in a bowl with raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Seafood Dipping Sauce
ingredients: 10 red and green bird's eye chiles
2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
Broiled (grilled) or steamed seafood, to serve
steps: Pound the garlic in a mortar with a pestle, add the chiles, and pound into fine pieces.
Add the cilantro and pound until smooth.
Add the fish sauce, sugar, lime juice, and 1 tablespoon water and stir with a spoon until the sugar has dissolved. The sauce should be sweet, sour, salty, and hot.
Serve with broiled or steamed seafood. Alternatively, transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving 1 cm headspace, cover, seal, and refrigerate for up to 2 weeks.

title: Shrimp Paste Dipping Sauce
ingredients: 1 x 2 cm piece fingerroot, peeled and julienned
2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
Raw or steamed vegetables, such as carrots, napa cabbage, cucumbers, and yard-long beans, to serve
1 red bird's eye chile, seeded and finely sliced lengthwise
steps: Pound the curry paste with the lemongrass, fingerroot, shallot, shrimp paste, and salted mackerel in a mortar with a pestle until smooth.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the pounded paste, and stir-fry for about 3 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk and stir continuously until thickened.
Add the sugar, fish sauce, and tamarind to taste and stir until thoroughly combined.
Add the crushed chiles and kaffir lime leaves, stir, and remove from the heat.
Transfer to a bowl, garnish with the green chile, cilantro sprig, and sliced red chile, and serve with raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Peanut Chili Sauce
ingredients: 10 red and green bird's eye chiles, chopped
120 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumbers, round eggplants (aubergines), and yard-long beans, to serve
steps: Pound the garlic, chiles, and peanuts in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Season with the lemon juice, fish sauce, and sugar. Serve in a bowl with raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Sweet Chili Dipping Sauce
ingredients: Grilled Chicken or Fried Spring Rolls, to serve (see p. 276 and p. 95)
steps: Mix the vinegar, sugar, salt, 4 tablespoons water, and the chile in a pan. Bring to a boil and boil for 2 minutes. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 3-5 minutes, or until syrupy. Remove from the heat and cool.
Garnish with the peanuts, if using, and serve immediately. Alternatively, transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving 1 cm headspace. Cool, cover, seal, and refrigerate for up to 1 week.

title: Thai-Style Satay Sauce
ingredients: 3 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the curry paste and sauté for 30 seconds, or until it sizzles and becomes fragrant.
Gradually add the coconut milk, stir, and boil for 2-3 minutes. Add the peanuts, sugar, salt, and tamarind and stir for 3-4 minutes. Remove from the heat, transfer to a bowl, and serve.

title: Very Spicy Thai Dipping Sauce
ingredients: grilled meat or fish, to serve
steps: Pound the garlic and chiles together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Transfer to a bowl, add the fish sauce and lime juice, and mix until thoroughly combined. Serve with grilled meat or fish.

title: Barbecue Sauce
ingredients: 1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Mix the fish sauce, lime juice, tamarind puree, sugar, and chili flakes in a bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Transfer to a serving bowl and sprinkle with the ground toasted rice, shallot, and scallion. Serve with grilled meat.
Alternatively, transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving 1 cm headspace. Cover, seal, and refrigerate for up to 2-3 weeks.

title: Pandan Extract
steps: Put the pandan leaves and 475 ml water into a food processor and blend. Pour the mixture through a fine strainer (sieve) or cheesecloth (muslin) into a bowl Use the extract immediately. Alternatively, transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving ½ inch (1 cm) head space, cover, and seal. Store in the refrigerator for up 1o 1-2 weeks.

title: Spicy Sauce with Boiled Eggs
ingredients: 2 hard-boiled eggs, cut into quarters, to garnish
raw or steamed vegetables, such as yard long beans, cucumber, and ferns, to serve
steps: Soak the chiles in a bowl of hot water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop. Transfer to a mortar with the garlic and pound thoroughly with a pestle until smooth. Season with the lemon juice and fish sauce, sprinkle with the shallots, and mix well until combined. Transfer to a bowl, season to taste, and garnish with the boiled eggs. Serve with raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Tamarind Puree
ingredients: 500 g sour tamarind pods. peeled and seeded
steps: Mix 475 ml Warm water with the tamarind pods in a large bowl, then knead together by hand. Strain the mixture through cheesecloth (muslin) into a large bowl. Use immediately,. Alternatively, transfer to a sterilized jar, leaving ½ inch (1 cm) head space, let cool, cover, and seal. Store in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

title: Fried Garlic
ingredients: 2 garlic bulbs, cloves separated, peeled, and sliced
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the garlic, and stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until golden brown. Remove from the heat, drain the garlic, and pat dry on kitchen paper. Use as an ingredient or a garnish.

title: Fried Shallots
ingredients: 5 shallots, peeled and finely sliced lengthwise
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the shallots, and stir-fry for 10-11 minutes until golden brown. Remove from the heat, drain the shallots, and pat dry on kitchen paper. Use as an ingredient or a garnish.

title: Ground Toasted Rice
steps: Dry-fry the rice in a wok over medium heat for about 8-10 minutes, stirring continuously, until golden brown and fragrant. Let cool, then pound in a mortar with a pestle until a fine powder: Use immediately. Alternatively, transfer to an airtight container and store for up to 1-2 months.

title: Tomato Chili Sauce
ingredients: raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumber, napa (Chinese) cabbage, and small bitter melon, to serve
steps: Dry-fry the chiles, shallots, and garlic in a wok over medium heat for 3-4 minutes until softened and slightly burned. Remove from the heat and set aside.

Heat a broiler (grill) to medium-high heat. Put the tomatoes onto the broiler (grill) rack and broil (grill) for 6-7 minutes until softened and the skin slightly burned. Pound the chiles, shallots, and garlic in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the lemongrass and pound again until smooth. Add the broiled (grilled) tomatoes and salt, and gently press with the pestle until combined. Serve with raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Deep-Fried Tofu with Dipping Sauce
ingredients: 100 g tofu, cut into triangles 5 cm long and 1 cm thick
2 red bird's eye chiles, coarsely pounded
steps: To make the sauce, put the vinegar, sugar, and salt in a small pan and mix until combined. Bring to a boil over medium heat, then remove from the heat and set aside. Add the chiles and mix well, then add the peanuts and transfer to a small serving bowl.
Heat the oil for deep-frying to 180°C (350°F), or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the tofu for 10 minutes, or until crisp and golden brown.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Serve immediately with the dipping sauce.

title: Roasted Fermented Soybean Dip
ingredients: 3 red and green long chiles, chopped
steps: Pound the shallots, lemongrass, chiles, and galangal in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add garlic and the pounded paste and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Pour in the beaten eggs, add the fermented soybeans with the dill, if using, and stir-fry for another 2-3 minutes until the eggs are cooked. Serve with rice.

title: Old-Style Rice Crust
steps: Put a wok or a pan over medium heat, add the oil, and spread across the pan, making sure that the inside surfaces are fully coated. Add the rice to the wok and spread over the whole surface to make a thin layer. Gradually move the wok around to let the rice cook evenly for 20-25 minutes until the rice becomes golden brown and crispy. Be sure to keep moving the wok to prevent the rice at the bottom of the wok from burning. Remove from the heat.

Mix the garlic, fish sauce, and sugar together thoroughly in a bowl, then stir in the cilantro (coriander) Dip a brush into the sauce and spread it over the rice crust, then let dry. Gently remove the rice crust from the wok or pan and serve.

title: Roasted Rice with Spicy Paste
ingredients: 200 g fermented fish, rinsed and ground (minced)
steps: Soak several 12-15 cm bamboo skewers in cold water for 30 minutes. Prepare a charcoal grill with white-hot coals, or heat a gas grill to 190°C.
Whisk the eggs and salt together in a small bowl.
Shape the glutinous rice into oval patties, thread them onto the soaked skewers, and grill for 4-5 minutes on each side, until crisp.
Brush one side with the egg mixture and grill for 1-2 minutes, until the egg dries. Turn and repeat on the other side. Repeat 5-6 times to build a thick, crisp egg coating.
For the spicy paste, cook the garlic, shallots, galangal, lemongrass, chile flakes, and kaffir lime leaves in a pan over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Transfer to a mortar and pound thoroughly. Add the fermented fish and mix well, then season with the lime juice.
Serve the grilled rice with the spicy paste.

title: Basic Puff Pastry
steps: To make the outer pastry, sift the flour into a large bowl. Dissolve the sugar and salt in 150 ml cold water and add to the flour. Add the vegetable oil and butter and knead until a dough forms. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, to make the inner pastry, sift the flour into another large bowl, add the oil, and knead until a dough forms.
Divide the inner and outer doughs into 20 small pieces.
On a lightly dusted work surface, roll the outer dough balls into rectangles. Put an inner dough ball in the middle of each and cover it with the outer layer.

Lightly dust the work surface again. Roll each dough ball into a 12-15 cm rectangle, working from the middle toward the top and bottom. Roll it into a tube and place it lengthwise on the work surface.
Roll each tube into another rectangle 18-20 cm long, again working from the middle toward the ends. Roll it tightly into a tube and cut it in half.
Place each half vertically on the work surface, press down with a rolling pin, and roll into a thin, flat disk. The pastry is now ready to use.

title: Chicken Curry Puffs
ingredients: 400 g boneless, stainless chicken breast, diced
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat add the cilantro (coriander) root, garlic, and white peppercorns, and sauté for 30 seconds. Add the diced chicken and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes. Add the curry powder, onions, potatoes, soy sauce, sugar, salt, and a little water and stir-fry for another 3-4 minutes until the potatoes have softened and are cooked. Let cool.

Place the filling on the pastry disks, brush the edges of the pastry with a little water, and fold the bottom edge of the pastry over to enclose the filling. Press down to seal, then crimp the edge. Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C, or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the pastry packages in batches for 8-10 minutes or until golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Serve.

title: Mung Bean Puffs
steps: Soak the mung beans in a bowl of water for 30 minutes, then drain.
Bring a pan of water to a boil over medium heat, add the mung beans, and cook for 30 minutes until cooked, then drain. Transfer to a mortar and pound with a pestle until a smooth paste.

Put the mung bean paste, coconut cream, sugar, and salt in a pan and heat over medium heat. Cook, stirring occasionally, for about 5 minutes until thick and sticky. Let cool, then form the mung bean filling into small balls. Place the filling on the pastry disks, brush the edges of the pastry with a little water and fold the bottom edge of the pastry over to enclose the filling. Press down to seal, then crimp the edge. Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C, or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the pastry packages in batches for 8-10 minutes or until golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Serve.

title: Taro Puffs
ingredients: 400 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Bring a pan of water to a boil over medium heat, add the taro, then reduce the heat and simmer for 10-15 minutes until cooked. Drain, let cool, then peel and dice. Transfer to a mortar and pound with a pestle until a smooth paste.

Put the taro paste, coconut cream, sugar, and salt into a pan and heat over medium heat. Cook, stirring occasionally, for about 5 minutes until thick and sticky. Let cool, then form the taro filling into small balls. Put the filling on the pastry disks, brush the edges of the pastry with a little water, and fold the bottom edge of the pastry over to enclose the filling. Press down to seal, then crimp the edge.

Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C, or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the pastry packages in batches for 10 minutes or until golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Serve.

title: Egg in Tamarind Sauce
ingredients: 6 hard boiled chicken or duck eggs
150 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1 red spur chile, seeded and finely sliced
1 handful of cilantro (coriander), chopped, to garnish
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over low-medium heat, add the shallot, and saute for 8-10 minutes until golden brown. Remove the shallot with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Set aside.
Saute the whole eggs in the same oil in the wok over medium heat for 6-8 minutes until the eggs are evenly golden brown. Remove from the wok and set aside. Reserve 1 tablespoon of oil in the wok.

And the tamarind, sugar, fish sauce, and about 4 tablespoons water to the wok and stir until the sugar has dissolved, then cook for 5 minutes or until the mixture turns syrupy. Remove from the heat and set aside.

Halve the eggs lengthwise. Place on a serving plate with the egg yolks facing up, then gently pour the sauce over the eggs and sprinkle with the crispy shallots, chile, and cilantro (coriander). Serve with cooked jasmine rice.

title: Hard-Boiled Eggs with Spicy Sauce
ingredients: 4 red and green finger chiles, chopped
steps: Mix the lime juice, fish sauce, and sugar together in a small bowl. Place the halved eggs on a serving plate with the egg yolks facing up. Top with the shallot and chiles and serve with the sauce on the side.

title: Grilled Eggs in Banana Leaves
ingredients: 1 kg banana leaves, cut into 6-inch 15 cm-diameter circles
steps: Prepare the banana-leaf cups. For each cup, place 2 banana leaf circles back to back with the shiny surface face outward on both sides. From the outside of the circle, fold up 3 cm of banana leaf and then fold in on itself to create a corner. Secure with a toothpick or use a stapler. Repeat until there are 4 corners. Set aside.

Heat the broiler (grill) to low. Put the eggs, chiles, soy sauce, cilantro (coriander), and salt into a large bowl and mix well until combined. Add 1-3 tablespoons water while mixing the eggs to make the texture softer. Carefully pour the egg mixture into the banana leaf cups.
Put the containers on the broiler (grill) rack and broil (grill) for 15 minutes or until the eggs are cooked through.

title: Pineapple Stuffed Omelet
ingredients: ½ carrot, cut into 8 mm dice
steps: Break the eggs into a bowl and add half the salt. Beat with a fork and set aside.
For the stuffing, heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the ground pork and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.

Add the onions, carrot, tomato, and chiles and stir-fry for another minute. Add 2-3 tablespoons water, then season with the sugar, oyster sauce, soy sauce, and remaining salt. Stir for 1-2 minutes, add the pineapple, and stir-fry for 1 minute. Set aside.

For the omelet, heat another wok over medium heat, add the remaining 1½ tablespoons oil, and roll the oil around the wok. Reduce the heat to low, then add the beaten eggs. Roll the eggs around the wok to create a thin omelet. Move and roll the wok for 3-4 minutes until the omelet is cooked and starts to come away from the wok.
Spoon the stuffing into the center of the omelet. Fold the bottom edge up, fold the left and right sides into the middle, and finish by folding the top side down to create a square package.

Place a serving plate upside down over the package, press firmly, and carefully turn the wok upside down to transfer the omelet to the plate. Cut across the middle of the omelet and serve with cucumber slices.

title: Herb Omelet
ingredients: Steamed Jasmine Rice (sec p 378), to serve
steps: Whisk the eggs with all the ingredients, except the oil, in a large bowl until combined.

Heat the oil in a skillet or frying pan over medium-low heat. Add the egg mixture and cook for 3-4 minutes or until the underside starts to set and the meat is browned. When almost cooked, carefully flip the omelet over and cook for 1-2 minutes to quickly color the other side. Serve on its own or with rice.

title: Pan-Fried Eggs
ingredients: 4 tablespoons julienned cooled white pork sausage
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F/180°C/Gas Mark.

4. Heat the oil in a large skillet or frying pan over medium heat. Add the ground (minced) pork and cook for 3-4 minutes until browned. Remove from the pan with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.

Break the eggs into the pan, then add the scallions (spring onions), Chinese sausage white pork sausage, garlic, tomato, and sliced onion and cook for 2-3 minutes or until the egg is cooked as desired.

Slice the baguette in half lengthwise and fill with the egg, sausages, scallions (spring onions), garlic, tomato, onions, and the fried pork. Toast in the oven for 2 minutes, then serve with the dipping sauces.

title: Fried Mussels
steps: For the sauce, mix the chili sauce, sugar, salt, vinegar, and 1-2 tablespoons water together in a pan over low heat. Heat for 1 minute or until the mixture starts to boil, then remove from the heat and let cool.

Clean the mussels in cold water. Blanch them in a pan of boiling water for 1 minute or until the mussels open and are cooked halfway through. Drain and discard the shells as well as any mussels that haven't opened and set aside.
Mix the arrowroot flour, rice flour, all-purpose (plain) flour, salt, baking powder, and 50 ml water together thoroughly in a bowl. Add the mussels and set aside.

Heat 3½ tablespoons oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the mussel and flour mixture to the pan, separate the mussels, and cook for 1 minute. Pour the beaten egg over the mussel mixture. Use a spatula to spread it evenly across the surface of the mixture. Divide the resulting "egg pancake" and mussel mixture underneath into portions and cook for another 4-5 minutes until the bottom of the mussel mixture starts to turn golden brown. Turn the portions over and cook for another 3-4 minutes until golden brown. Transfer to a serving plate and set aside. Heat ½ tablespoon oil in the same wok over medium heat. Add the chopped garlic and quickly sauté for about 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the bean sprouts, sugar, and soy sauce and stir-fry for about 30 seconds. Remove from the heat and place on top of the mussels.
Sprinkle with finely sliced scallions (spring onions) and pepper and serve with the sauce.

title: Grilled Fish Patties
ingredients: 2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
500 g king mackerel fillets, skin removed
steps: Soak 8-10 bamboo skewers in a bowl of cold water for 30 minutes to prevent them from burning during cooking.
Prepare a charcoal grill with glowing white-hot coals, preheat a gas grill to 200°C, or heat a conventional broiler to medium.
Mix the coconut milk and sugar in a bowl until the sugar dissolves. Set aside.

Process the fish and curry paste in a food processor until smooth. Transfer to a bowl and add the coconut milk mixture, coconut, fish sauce, and basil. Knead by hand for 10 minutes, until firm and sticky.
Shape 2 tablespoons of the mixture into an oval patty and thread it onto a soaked skewer. Press firmly around the skewer. Place 3-4 patties on each skewer and repeat with the remaining mixture.
Grill for 6-7 minutes on each side, until puffed and browned. If broiling, position the rack about 10 cm from the heat and broil for 6-7 minutes on each side. Serve.

title: Mackerel Fish Balls
ingredients: 250 g Spanish mackerel or clown fish, skinned and filleted
steps: Put the fish into a food processor and process until it is a fine, smooth texture, then transfer to a large bowl. Add the black pepper, salt, and flour and knead with your hands for 5-10 minutes. While kneading, slowly add the ice cubes until the texture is sticky and firm.

Using a spoon, shape the fish mixture into sma 1 cm-diameter balls and soak in a bowl of warm water (about 110-120°F/45-50°C) for 30 minutes. To harden the fish balls, maintain the water temperature by refreshing it with warm water as needed.
Fill a large bowl with ice-cold water. Set aside.

Bring a medium pan of water to a boil over medium heat. Add the fish balls and cook for 5 minutes until they float to the surface. Remove with a slotted spoon and transfer to the bowl of ice-cold water. Transfer to an airtight container and store in the refrigerator for up to 1-2 weeks or freeze for a up to a month.

title: Taro Pyramids
ingredients: 50 g wheat starch, plus extra for dusting
50 g wheat starch, plus extra for dusting
120 ml limewater (see p. 509) or club soda (soda water)
2 tablespoons vegetable oil, plus extra for deep-frying
steps: To make the dough, steam the taro for about 30 minutes or until cooked. Drain and grind or pound in a mortar with a pestle until smooth, then let cool. When cool, put the taro in a large bowl, add the wheat starch and coconut cream, and mix until thoroughly combined.

For the batter, mix the wheat starch, rice flour, salt, sugar, and egg in a bowl. Gradually add the limewater or club soda (soda water) and 175 ml water, a small amount at a time. Mix until no lumps are left. Set aside. For the filling, pound the garlic, cilantro (coriander) root, and pepper in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the pounded paste, and stir- fry for 1 minute or until fragrant. Add the pork, shrimp, and mushrooms and stir-fry for another 3-4 minutes until well cooked. Add the sugar and soy sauce and stir until combined, then remove from the heat.

Scoop out a tablespoon of the taro mixture and flatten it with your hand. Put a teaspoon of the filling in the center and fold and pinch the edges together to enclose the filling into a pyramid shape. Repeat until all the dough and filling are used.

Heat enough oil for deep-frying in a large wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the taro pyramids in batches for 5-7 minutes or until crispy and golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Serve with cucumber relish.

title: Pork Roll
ingredients: 2 tablespoons pork liver, cut into small pieces
steps: To make the sauce, pound the chiles, garlic and pineapple in a mortar with a pestle. Heat a pan over medium heat, add the chile and pineapple mixture, sugar, vinegar, and salt and simmer, stirring, until thick and sticky. Put the pork, pork liver, crabmeat, soy sauce, onion, sesame oil, and sugar into a large bowl and mix with your hands until combined.

Place the tofu sheet on a work surface and put the filling at one end, leaving a 2 cm border. Brush the borders with a little water then roll up, tucking in the ends as you go, to form a roll Brush the end with more water and press to seal. Set aside covered in a damp dish towel to prevent it from drying out. Pour 350 ml water into a large bowl, add the tempura flour, and stir until the flour has dissolved.

Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Dip the tofu roll into the tempura batter and deep-fry for 7-10 minutes until golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Serve, cut into slices, with the dipping sauce.

title: Thai Summer Rolls
ingredients: 15 g crispy pork rind, coarsely chopped
100 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat add the jicama and oyster sauce, and saute for 30 seconds. Remove from the heat and set aside.

To make the sauce, pound all the ingredients together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Heat the sauce in a wok over medium heat. bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until thickened.

Lay a spring roll wrapper out on a work surface so that one of the corners faces you. Put a little of the lettuce, bean sprouts, pork skin, fried shallots, and jicama in the center of the wrapper and add a little sauce. Fold the bottom corner of the wrapper up and over the filling. Fold the left and right corners in to create a package. Roll the package up toward the top corner and brush a little water on the top edges of the wrapper to stick the package together. Repeat until you have used up the filling. Cut the rolls in half and serve with the remaining sauce.

title: Pork and Shrimp Golden Packages
ingredients: 1 scallion (spring onion) or baby leek, 20-30 cm long
150 g shrimp (prawns), peeled, deveined, and ground (minced)
30 spring-roll wrapper sheets, about 13 cm in diameter
Sweet Chili Dipping Sauce (see p. 60), to serve
steps: Prepare one bowl of boiling water and another of cold water.
Cut the scallion or leek lengthwise into 5-7 mm-wide strips, making one strip for each wrapper.
Blanch the strips in the boiling water for 30 seconds, transfer to the cold water, then drain and pat dry.
For the filling, combine the shrimp, pork, saam-gler, soy sauce, sugar, and water chestnuts in a large bowl.
Cover and chili for at least 10 minutes.
Place a wrapper on the work surface and put 1 teaspoon filling in the center. Lift the edges to form a package and tie securely with a blanched scallion strip. Repeat with the remaining filling.
Heat the oil in a wok or deep fryer to 180°C. Deep-fry the packages in batches for 5-7 minutes, until golden brown and crisp.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and serve with sweet chili dipping sauce.

title: Cracker Salad
ingredients: 5 large black sesame seed rice-paper crackers
steps: Break the crackers into small pieces and put them in a deep bowl.
Add the fish paste, pork crackling, garlic, shallot, carrot, and yard-long bean and gently mix until combined.
Season with the lime juice, oil, and fish sauce and serve.

title: Pork and Shrimp on Pineapple
ingredients: 150 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
100 g uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled, deveined, and ground
1 pineapple, peeled, cored, and cut into 3 x 1 cm pieces
steps: Finely pound the garlic, cilantro root, and pepper in a mortar with a pestle.
Heat the oil in a wok over low-medium heat, add the garlic paste, and sauté for 2-3 minutes, until golden and fragrant.
Add the sugar and salt and cook for another 2-3 minutes, until the sugar softens.
Add the pork and shrimp and cook for another 4 minutes. Stir in the peanuts and cook for 8-9 minutes, until the mixture becomes sticky. Remove from the heat and let cool.
Shape the cooled mixture into 2 cm balls and place each ball on a piece of pineapple. Top with a cilantro leaf and a slice of chile, then serve.

title: Thai-Style Hot Pot
prepTime: 20 minutes, plus soaking and marinating time
ingredients: 300 g tenderloin steak (beef sirloin), thinly sliced
½ head green or white cabbage, cut into chunks
120 ml Barbecue Sauce (see p. 63), to serve
steps: Soak the noodles in water for 10 minutes, or prepare according to package directions. Drain, cut, and set aside.
Put the beef in a bowl, add the oyster sauce, sugar, and soy sauce, and mix well. Cover and marinate for 10-15 minutes.
Put the beef and shrimp in a shallow serving dish and pour the beaten egg over them. Set aside.
Put the drained noodles on a serving plate with the cabbage, water spinach, and basil leaves.
For the soup, combine the chicken broth, kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, shallots, cilantro, and galangal in a large bowl. Pour into a hot pot and bring to a boil.
Bring the hot pot to the table. Use chopsticks to dip small portions of meat, shrimp, or vegetables into the broth until cooked. Remove, dip into the barbecue sauce, and eat.

title: Deep-Fried Pork with Crispy Kaffir Lime Leaves
ingredients: 80 g all-purpose (plain) flour, cornstarch (cornflour), or tapioca flour
200 g sour pork sausage, cut into bite-size pieces
selection of condiments, such as sliced ginger, shallots. garlic, roasted peanuts, red bird's eye chiles, and scallions (spring onions)
steps: Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds.
Meanwhile, spread the flour and breadcrumbs out on separate large plates. Dredge the pork sausage in the flour, then dip in the beaten egg, and coat in the breadcrumbs.
Deep-fry the coated sausage pieces for about 5 minutes or until golden brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Set aside.
Deep-fry the kaffir lime leaves for 30 seconds until crispy, then remove and drain on paper towels. Set aside.
Put the sausage on a serving plate, garnish with the deep-fried kaffir lime leaves, and serve with a selection of condiments.

title: Grilled Pork Skewers
ingredients: 2 kg pork sirloin, rinsed and sliced into 2.5 cm strips
200 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Finely pound the garlic, cilantro (coriander) roots, and peppercorns in a mortar with a pestle. Transfer to a large bowl and add the pork, salt, soy sauce, and sugar and mix well. Cover with plastic wrap (clingfilm) and let marinate in the refrigerator for 2-4 hours.
Meanwhile, soak 10-15 bamboo skewers in a bowl of cold water for 30 minutes, This prevents the skewers from burning during cooking.
Before you begin cooking, check that your charcoal is glowing white hot, or your gas grill (barbecue) is preheated to 400°F/200°C.

Using your hands, mold some of the pork mixture onto a soaked wooden skewer, making sure that the mixture is firmly attached to the skewer and molds into an oval shape. Repeat until all the mixture is used.
Brush the oil over the pork skewers, then grill for 10-12 minutes until cooked. Serve.

title: Pork Cracklings
prepTime: 5 minutes, plus drying and standing time
steps: Bring a large pan of water to a boil over medium heat. Add the pork skin and boil for 30 minutes, then drain and cut into 2.5 cm pieces.
Mix the cooked pork skin with the soy sauce and salt, then sun-dry for 4 hours, or until dry.
Heat the oil in a wok or deep fryer to 180°C. Deep-fry the pork skin for 5 minutes, remove with a slotted spoon, and drain on paper towels overnight.
The next day, reheat the oil to 180°C and deep-fry the pork skin for about 5 minutes, until puffed. Drain on paper towels, let cool, and serve.

title: Thai-style Pork Satay
ingredients: 1 teaspoon coriander seeds, ground and toasted
1 teaspoon cumin seeds, ground and toasted
Thai-Style Satay Sauce (see p. 80), to serve
steps: Slice the pork into pieces about 2.5 cm wide, 7.5 cm long, and 8 mm thick.
Mix the pork with the galangal, lemongrass, turmeric, coriander, cumin, white pepper, 100 ml coconut cream, sugar, and salt. Cover and marinate for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, soak 25 bamboo skewers in cold water for 30 minutes to prevent them from burning.
Heat a charcoal or gas grill to about 200°C, or heat an indoor broiler to medium. Thread a piece of pork onto each skewer.
Cook for 10-15 minutes, turning the skewers and basting frequently with the remaining coconut cream, until the pork is cooked. Serve with satay sauce and cucumber relish.

title: Fried Spring Rolls
ingredients: 10-12 spring roll wrappers 20 cm in diameter
Sweet Chili Dipping Sauce (see p. 60), to serve
steps: Soak the noodles in a bowl of water for 10 minutes, or prepare according to package directions, then drain and cut into 4 cm. lengths. Set aside Squeeze out the water from the mushrooms, discard the stems, and finely slice. Set aside.

Dissolve the tapioca flour in 120 ml water over low heat, then set aside. Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a skillet or frying pan over medium heat, add the pork, and cook for 3-4 minutes until browned and any liquid has evaporated. Strain and set aside. Heat another 2 tablespoons oil in a wok over medium heat, add the saam-gler, and cook for 1 minute or until fragrant. Add the shiitake mushrooms and saute for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Reduce the heat to low, add the cabbage, and stir-fry for 1½ minutes. Remove the wok from the heat, add the noodles, pork, oyster sauce, sugar, soy, and salt, and stir until thoroughly combined. Avoid overcooking, which will make the mixture soggy. Let cool Lay a spring roll wrapper on a work surface so that one of the corners faces you. Put 2 tablespoons of the filling in the center of the wrapper and fold the bottom of the wrapper up and over the filling. Fold the left and right sides in to create a package. Roll the package up toward the top corner and brush the tapioca mixture on the top edges of the wrapper to stick the package together. Repeat until all the filling is used. Cover the wrapper with a damp dish towel to stop it from drying out. Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 375°F/190°C, or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the spring rolls in batches for 7-10 minutes until golden brown, then remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Serve with sweet chili dipping sauce.

title: Sour Sausage Meat in Banana Leaf
ingredients: 2 garlic bulbs, cloves separated and finely chopped
selection of condiments, such as sliced ginger, shallots, peanuts, bird's eye chiles, and scallions (spring onions)
steps: Put the ground (minced) meat, garlic, rice, and salt in a large bowl and mix together with clean, damp hands until the mixture is sticky and can be molded. Divide the mixture into portions, place the meat in the center of a banana leaf, and top with a chile. Cover the meat with the sides of the leaf, fold over the ends, and tightly seal with string. Alternatively, and the whole chiles to the meat, then pack the meat mixture into a large plastic food bag and seal. Let ferment for 7-10 days at room temperature The meat will taste sour when ready. Serve as patties with rice and a selection of condiments. Alternatively, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

title: Steamed Spring Rolls
ingredients: 30 rice crepes or rice paper spring roll wrappers
steps: Soak the vermicelli in a bowl of cold water for 5 minutes, then drain. Put all the ingredients except the rice crepes in a large bowl and mix together until thoroughly combined.

Lay a rice crepe on a work surface. Put 1-2 tablespoons of the filling in the center of the crepe and spread out thinly. Don't overfill because it might tear. Fold the bottom of the crepe up and over the filling. Fold the left and right sides in to create a package. Roll the package up toward the top of the crepe and brush a little water on the top edges of the crepe to stick the package together. Repeat until all the filling is used Steam the rolls in a steamer for about 5 minutes or until cooked. Serve with plum sauce.

title: Stuffed Roti
ingredients: 120 ml ghee or vegetable oil, plus extra for greasing
steps: Grease a baking sheet with vegetable oil and set aside.

To make the roti pastry, put the flour in a large bowl. Whisk half the beaten egg, the milk, salt, sugar, and 120 ml water in another bowl until the sugar and salt dissolve. Pour into the flour and mix and knead until the ingredients start to combine. Add 1 tablespoon ghee or vegetable oil and continue kneading until smooth.

Divide the dough into small equal portions. Coat your fingers with ghee or oil and shape the portions into small balls. Place them on the greased baking sheet, cover with plastic wrap or cheesecloth, and let stand for 2-10 hours before cooking.

Meanwhile, prepare the stuffing. Heat the butter and 1 tablespoon oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the saam-gler and curry powder and cook for 1 minute, or until fragrant. Add the onions and sauté for 1 minute, then add the chicken and stir-fry for 2 minutes, or until cooked. Season with the salt and sugar, stir-fry until fully flavored, then remove from the heat and set aside.
Place a dough ball on an oiled work surface. Dip your hand in ghee or oil, then press and flatten the dough into a very thin, wide, almost translucent sheet.

Put 3-4 tablespoons stuffing in the center, pour about 1½ teaspoons beaten egg over it, and sprinkle with a little scallion. Fold in the sides, then the ends, to form a square package. Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.

Heat ½ tablespoon oil or ghee in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Cook the roti one at a time for about 2 minutes on each side, or until golden brown and crisp. Transfer to a serving plate and repeat with the remaining roti. Serve with cucumber relish.

title: Fried Crickets with Herbs
ingredients: 3 garlic bulbs, cloves separated and finely sliced
steps: Put the crickets in an airtight container and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes, then remove and transfer to the freezer for 30 minutes.
Blanch the crickets in a pan of boiling water for 1-2 minutes, then rinse under cold running water, drain, and set aside.

Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C, or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the ginger, galangal, lemongrass, and garlic for 1 minute or until golden brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Deep-fry the peanuts, if using, in the oil for about 1 minute or until toasted. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.

Deep-fry the kaffir lime leaves in the oil for 20-30 seconds. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Make sure the oil is at the correct temperature, then deep-fry the crickets for about 5 minutes or until golden brown and crispy, then remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Mix the crickets, ginger mixture, garlic, and peanuts together and season with the salt Garnish with the kaffir lime leaves and serve.

title: Roasted Crickets
steps: Put the crickets in an airtight container and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes, then remove and transfer to the freezer for 30 minutes. Remove the crickets from the freezer and wash 3 or 4 times in water.
Heat a wok over medium heat, add the crickets, and roast for 6-7 minutes. Add the lemongrass and pandan leaves and season with salt. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes. Serve.

title: Omelet with Red Ant Eggs
steps: Break the eggs into a bowl, add the shallots, red ant eggs, and fish sauce, and beat thoroughly with a fork.

Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the garlic, and sauté for 1 minute. Pour in the egg mixture and roll it around the wok to form an omelet. Continue moving and rolling the wok for 2-3 minutes, until the omelet is yellow and begins to come away from the wok. Carefully flip and cook for another 1-2 minutes to color the other side. Serve.

title: Pickled Cabbage
ingredients: 400 g choy sum (flowering Chinese cabbage), cut into 5 cm lengths
steps: Mix 950 ml water and the rice together in a large bowl. Stir until the water turns milky white. Strain through cheesecloth (muslin) and reserve 250 ml of the rice water. Strain the rice water again and set aside.
Put the choy sum and salt in a large bowl and rub the salt all over the cabbage. Squeeze and knead for 2-3 minutes until softened. Add the cooled glutinous rice and massage until well mixed.
Transfer to a large sterilized jar and add the reserved rice water, leaving 5 cm headspace. Add the ginger, if using, cover, and stand overnight at room temperature. Drain the next day and serve.

title: Roasted Big Red Ants
steps: Put the ants in an airtight container and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes, then remove and transfer to the freezer for 30 minutes.
Roast all the ingredients in a skillet or frying pan over medium heat for 3-5 minutes until dry. Let cool and serve.

title: Dried Mango
ingredients: 2 kg ripe mangoes, peeled, pitted, and thinly sliced
steps: Put the mango and salt in a food processor and blend until smooth. Transfer to a wok and heat over medium heat for about 20 minutes until sticky. Remove from the heat and let cool slightly, then shape the mango mixture into small balls. Flatten the balls into disks 5 cm in diameter. Put the mango disks on a tray and sun-dry for 24 hours. Turn over and let dry for another 48 hours. Store the dried mango in sterilized airtight jars. They must be stored away from moisture, so when filling the jars, make sure your hands are dry.

title: Green Mango with Sweetened Fish Sauce
ingredients: 65 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
2 sour green mangoes, peeled and thinly sliced
steps: Mix the sugar and fish sauce together in a wok, then heat over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 5-8 minutes until thick. Add the shallot, chiles, and dried shrimp and mix well. Transfer to a small serving bowl and serve with the sliced green mango.

title: Preserved Mango
prepTime: 15 minutes, plus soaking and drying time
ingredients: 1 kg sour green mango, peeled, seeded, and sliced
steps: Pour 1.2 liters water into a large bowl, add the rock salt, and stir until the salt has dissolved. Add the mango slices to the salted water, cover with plastic wrap (clingfilm), and let soak for 24 hours The next day, remove the mango from the salted water with a slotted spoon and soak in the limewater for 1 hour. Rinse under cold running water and let dry. Bring 800 ml water and 700 g sugar to a boil in a large pan and keep boiling for 3-4 minutes. Remove from the heat and let cool.

Put the sliced mango in a large bowl, pour the sugar syrup over the fruit, and cover with plastic wrap. Let soak overnight in the refrigerator. The next day, remove the mango with a slotted spoon and set aside. Bring the sugar syrup to a boil over medium heat and gradually add the remaining 100 g sugar. Boil until thick and sticky. Remove from the heat and let cool. When cool pour into an airtight container and add the mango. Cover and set aside for 2-3 days. Store in the refrigerator for up to I month.

title: Dried Bananas
ingredients: 10 small ripe bananas, peeled and sliced into circles
steps: Line a baking sheet with cheesecloth (muslin). Arrange the bananas on the lined baking sheet, cover with more cheesecloth to prevent any bugs from settling on the bananas, and let dry in the sun for 3-5 days. Turn the baking sheet once a day so the bananas dry evenly. Preheat the oven to 325°F/160°C/Gas Mark 3 and line a large baking sheet with wax (greaseproof) paper.

Mix the dried bananas with the honey in a large bowl. Transfer to the lined baking sheet and bake in the oven for about 20 minutes. Let cool, then transfer to a sterilized airtight jar and store for up to 3-4 weeks.

title: Thai-Style Chinese Cruller
ingredients: 120 g all-purpose (plain) flour, plus 50 g flour, for dusting
1 tablespoon vegetable oil, plus extra for deep-frying
coffee, hot chocolate, congee, or sweetened condensed milk
steps: Put the flour, yeast, baking powder, sugar, and salt into a large bowl and mix well. Add 5 tablespoons water and knead for 10 minutes or until the dough is mixed well. Add the 1 tablespoon oil and knead for another 2-3 minutes. Cover the dough with plastic wrap (clingfilm) and let rest for 2-10 hours. Knead the dough on a floured work surface. Roll into a tube shape and gently press with a rolling pin to create a 5 mm thick rectangle sheet. Cut the rectangle in half Lengthwise, then cut crosswise to create 2 x 8 cm strips. Take 2 dough strips. Moisten the middle of one strip with some water, then press the other strip on top where the water is. Stretch them out slightly. Repeat until all the dough strips are used.

Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the dough for 1-2 minutes on each side or until the dough has puffed up and turned golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Serve with coffee, hot chocolate, congee, or sweetened condensed milk.

title: Grilled Yuca Root with Coconut Syrup
ingredients: 700 g-1 kg yuca root (cassava), peeled and cut crosswise into 10 cm pieces
200 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Soak the yuca root in cold water for 15 minutes, then drain and set aside.

For the coconut syrup, heat the coconut milk in a pan over medium heat. When it starts to boil, add the sugar and salt and stir until dissolved. Reduce the heat slightly and boil gently for 4-5 minutes. Remove from the heat and set aside.

Heat a charcoal grill until white hot, preheat a gas grill to 350°F/180°C, or heat an indoor broiler to medium-high. Steam the yuca over high heat for about 10 minutes, or until it just starts to cook; do not overcook it.
Grill the yuca over medium heat for about 10 minutes on each side, or until brown. If broiling, place the rack about 10 cm from the heat and broil for about 10 minutes on each side.
Put the grilled yuca on a cutting board and flatten each piece by pressing it with another board or a plate.

Dip the yuca in the coconut syrup for 2-3 minutes. Return it to the grill or broiler and cook each side for 3-5 minutes, or until the coating dries. Transfer to a plate, pour over the remaining syrup, and serve.

title: Butterfly Pea Juice
steps: Bring 3 liters water to a boil in a pan over medium heat.
Add the butterfly pea flowers and boil for about 5 minutes.
Add the sugar, salt, and lemon juice and stir for about 5 minutes, until the sugar and salt dissolve.
Remove from the heat and let cool slightly. Strain through cheesecloth into a heatproof pitcher and cool completely.
Serve over ice.

title: Dragon Fruit Frappé
steps: Put the dragon fruits into a blender, add the ice cubes, honey, and lime juice and blend until smooth. Serve.

title: Water Chestnut Rubies and Emeralds in Coconut Milk
ingredients: 250 ml cream soda syrup or green
250 ml grenadine or red sugar syrup
400 g peeled and diced water chestnuts
1 pandan leaf, tied in a knot
steps: Put the cream soda syrup, grenadine, and tapioca flour in separate bowls. Divide the water chestnuts between the bowls of red and green sugar syrup and let soak for about 10 minutes or until the chestnuts absorbs the color. Remove with a slotted spoon and transfer to the bowl of tapioca flour. Shake the bowl until the water chestnuts are well coated with starch.

Have a bowl of ice water ready. Bring 1.2 liters water to a boil in a pan, add the coated water chestnuts, and let sit for 3-4 minutes until the water chestnuts float to the surface and the flour has become transparent (jellylike). Transfer to the bowl of ice water and set aside.

Bring 250 ml water and the sugar to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Boil until the mixture turns syrupy, then remove from the heat, let cool, and set aside. Heat the pandan leaf and coconut milk in a pan over low-medium heat for 3-4 minutes or until it reaches a boil. Remove from the heat, let cool, and set aside.
Drain the water chestnuts and spoon into a serving bowl. Add the sugar syrup, and infused coconut milk, and crushed ice cubes and serve.

title: Asiatic Pennywort Juice
ingredients: 20 g Asiatic pennywort leaves, washed thoroughly
steps: Put the leaves in a blender, add 250 ml recently boiled water, and process until smooth. Strain through a piece of cheesecloth (muslin) into a large heatproof pitcher (jug) to remove the residue.

Carefully pour 250 ml boiling water over the residue into the pitcher and squeeze the cheesecloth to extract the liquid Discard the residue. Add the sugar syrup to the juice, stir well, and let cool. Serve cold with ice cubes.

title: Kumquat Juice
steps: Wash the kumquats and squeeze the juice into a large pan. Pour in 2 liters water and stir until mixed. Add the sugar and salt, then bring to a boil over medium heat. Remove from the heat, strain through a piece of cheesecloth (muslin) into a large heatproof pitcher (jug), and let cool. Serve cold with ice cubes.

title: Lemongrass Juice
steps: Bring 2 liters water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the lemongrass, and simmer for 8-10 minutes. Remove from the heat and strain the lemongrass juice through a piece of cheesecloth (muslin) into a large heatproof pitcher (jug). Add the sugar and salt and stir until dissolved. Pour the lemongrass juice into a clean pan and bring to a boil over medium heat, then remove from the heat and let cool. Serve cold with ice cubes:.

title: Passion Fruit Juice
steps: Bring 350 ml water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat.
