Add the sugar and stir until dissolved and syrupy, then remove from the heat.
Strain the passion fruit pulp through cheesecloth into a large heatproof pitcher and discard the residue.
Add the salt and 120 ml of the sugar syrup and stir well.
Serve cold over ice.

title: Pandan Juice
ingredients: 5 x 30 g pandan leaves, washed and cut crosswise into 5-7.5 cm strips
steps: Bring 1.4 liters water to a boil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Add the pandan leaves, reduce the heat to medium-low, and boil for 5 minutes.
Add the sugar and salt and boil for another 2-3 minutes, until dissolved.
Remove from the heat and adjust the sweetness to taste.
Strain through a fine sieve into a heatproof pitcher. Serve hot, or cold over ice.

title: Roselle Juice
ingredients: 200 g fresh roselle (or 20 g dried roselle). cleaned
steps: Bring 2 liters of water to a boil in a large pan. Add the roselle, reduce the heat, and simmer gently until the water turns dark red. Remove the roselle with a slotted spoon, add the sugar and salt, and bring back to a boil. Boil for 10 minutes, then remove from the heat and flavor to taste. Pour into a heatproof pitcher (jug) and let cool. Serve cold with ice cubes.

title: Sweetened Soy Milk
steps: Rinse the soybeans until the water becomes clear, then soak in 750 ml water for at least 6 hours. Drain and discard the soaking water.

Finely pound the soybeans in a mortar with a pestle, then transfer to a large bowl, pour in 1.7 liters water, and stir well. Strain through a piece of cheesecloth (muslin) into a pan, discarding the residue left in the cheesecloth.

Bring the soy milk to a boil over medium heat, stirring continuously for 5 minutes. Add the sugar, reduce the heat to low, and stir for 5-10 minutes or until the sugar has dissolved. Remove from the heat and serve hot or cold.

title: Tamarind Juice
ingredients: 80 g peeled and seeded sour tamarind pods
steps: To make the tamarind puree, soak the tamarind pods in 350 ml warm water for 15-20 minutes. Use your hand to squeeze the tamarind and water to mix and remove the tamarind flesh until you have quite a thick puree. Strain the tamarind mixture through a fine strainer (sieve) into a cup. Set aside. Bring 950 ml water to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the tamarind puree, salt, and sugar and stir until the sugar has dissolved, then boil for 4-5 minutes. Remove from the heat. Serve hot or cold with ice cubes.

title: Spicy Egg Salad
ingredients: 4 hard-boiled eggs, peeled and quartered lengthwise
5 red and green bird's-eye chiles, finely chopped
steps: Arrange the eggs on a serving plate.
Stir the shallots, chiles, fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar together in a bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Pour the dressing over the eggs, garnish with the cilantro leaves, and serve.

title: Spicy Salted Egg Salad
ingredients: 1 yard-long bean, cut into 8 cm pieces
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
2 salted duck eggs, cut into quarters lengthwise
steps: Coarsely pound the chiles and garlic in a mortar with a pestle.
Add the yard-long bean, tomatoes, papaya, and dried shrimp and mix together.
Season with the lime juice, sugar, and fish sauce and mix well.
Add the eggs and gently stir with a spoon.
Transfer to a serving dish, sprinkle with the peanuts, and serve.

title: Thai Rice Salad
ingredients: 400 g jasmine rice, rinsed and drained
200 g uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined
50 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: For the dressing, bring the fish sauce and 250 ml water to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the sugar, lemongrass, lime leaves, and galangal and return to a boil. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes.

Remove from the heat and strain through cheesecloth (muslin) into a clean pan. Discard the solids. Return the liquid to the heat, bring to a boil, then simmer for another 5-7 minutes until thickened and reduced by half. Set aside.

For the rice salad, process the morinda leaves in a blender. Strain through cheesecloth into a bowl or pitcher, add 600 ml water, and stir. Put the rice in a pan, add enough morinda water to cover, bring to a boil over medium heat, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the shrimp in boiling water for 1-2 minutes until pink. Drain, pound to a smooth paste, then toast the paste in a wok for 5-7 minutes until dry. Set aside.
Dry-fry the grated coconut in a clean wok for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly, until golden brown. Remove from the heat and set aside.
Soak the vermicelli in water for 10 minutes, or according to the package directions. Drain and set aside.
Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a wok over medium heat. Add the salt, sugar, and noodles and stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until dry.
Mix all the rice-salad ingredients together and serve with the dressing and side dishes.

title: Spicy Fish Salad
ingredients: 1 kg sea bass or sea bream, cleaned and filleted
65 g pea eggplants, grilled and pounded
steps: Finely chop the fish, then cook in a large skillet or frying pan for 2-3 minutes. Set aside. Mix the chili flakes, ground rice, shallots, scallion (spring onion), cilantro (coriander), and sawtooth cilantro (coriander) together in a bowl. Add the fish sauce, fermented fish sauce, galangal, and eggplant (aubergine), and mix well. Sprinkle with the mint leaves and serve.

title: Spicy Seaweed Salad
ingredients: 500 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
100 g red and green bird's-eye chiles
steps: Soak the seaweed in a bow of water for 1 hour then drain and set aside.

Mix the coconut cream, tamarind, sugar, salt, and shrimp paste together in a large pan. Bring to a boil over medium heat, then remove from the heat and let stand until warm. Add the soaked seaweed, the peanuts, dried shrimp, coconut chiles, and shallot and mix together. Put a tablespoon of the salad into the center of a betel leaf. Repeat until all the salad s used. Serve.

title: Spicy Mackerel Salad
ingredients: 2 x 150 g steamed salted horse mackerel, or 150 g smoked mackerel
7 red and green bird's-eye chiles, chopped
1 x ⅝-inch/1½ cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and julienned
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the horse mackerel and fry for 2-3 minutes on each side. Remove and let cool.
Remove the skin and bones and put the flesh in a large bowl. Gently crumble it into small pieces.
Add the shallots, chiles, lemongrass, ginger, lime juice, and fish sauce and mix well. Transfer to a serving plate, garnish with the peppermint leaves, and serve.

title: Spicy Squid and Heart of Palm Salad
ingredients: 300 g squid, cleaned and cut into 4 cm pieces
100 g uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined, tails still intact
10 red bird's eye chiles, finely chopped
steps: Blanch the squid in a pan of boiling water for 2-3 minutes or until cooked. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the shrimp in another pan of boiling water for 1-2 minutes or until pink. Drain and set aside.
For the dressing, mix the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and chiles in a large bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Add the squid, shrimp, heart of palm, mango, carrot, onion, cilantro, and scallions. Mix well and serve.

title: Deep Fried Squid Salad
ingredients: 300 g squid, cut into 1 cm-thick rings
steps: Whisk the flour and cold water together until thoroughly combined.

Heat the oil in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C. Dip the squid in the batter, carefully add it to the oil, and deep-fry for 4-5 minutes, until golden and crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Mix the chili jam, lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, shallot, kaffir lime leaves, chiles, and lemongrass in a bowl.
Add the squid and mix well. Transfer to a serving plate, garnish with peppermint leaves, and serve.

title: Spicy Wing Bean Salad
ingredients: 12 uncooked jumbo shrimp (king prawns), peeled and deveined, with tails still intact
steps: Cook the shrimp in a pan of boiling water for 1-2 minutes, or until they turn pink, then drain and set aside.
Fill a bowl with ice-cold water and set aside.
Blanch the wing beans in a pan of boiling water for 30 seconds, then drain and transfer to the ice water for 1 minute.
Drain the beans, slice them into 5 mm-thick slices, and set aside.
To make the sauce, mix all the sauce ingredients together in a large bowl until thoroughly combined.
Add the shrimp, squid, cashew nuts, and wing beans and mix well.
Transfer to a serving plate, garnish with peppermint leaves, and serve.

title: Spicy Giant Freshwater Shrimp Salad
ingredients: 3-8 red bird's eye chiles, finely chopped
steps: Preheat the broiler (grill) to high. Put the shrimp on the broiler rack and broil for 2-3 minutes on each side, or until cooked. Let cool slightly, remove the shells, and press the juices from the heads.
Put the shrimp in a bowl, add the remaining ingredients, and mix until thoroughly combined. Serve.

title: Spicy Heart of Palm Salad
ingredients: 100 g uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined
10 red bird's eye chiles, finely chopped
1 teaspoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Blanch the pork in a pan of boiling water for 2-3 minutes or until cooked. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the squid in another pan of boiling water for 2-3 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the shrimp in a pan of boiling water for 1-2 minutes or until pink. Drain and set aside.

Mix the pork, squid, shrimp, carrots, chiles, shallots, celery, and heart of palm in a large bowl. Add the fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar and mix until the sugar dissolves. Serve on lettuce leaves.

title: Seafood Salad
ingredients: 150 g squid, sliced into 2 cm-thick rings
180 g uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined
1 tablespoon sliced red and green bird's eye chiles
1 handful cilantro (coriander), chopped, plus extra sprigs to garnish
20 g Chinese celery stalk, chopped into 3 cm lengths
steps: Blanch the squid in a pan of boiling water for 2-3 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the shrimp in another pan of boiling water for 1-2 minutes. Drain and set aside.
For the dressing, combine the lime juice, fish sauce, and sugar in a small bowl. Add the chicken broth or water and stir until the sugar dissolves.

Put the shrimp, squid, onion, mango, carrot, chiles, tomatoes, cilantro, celery, scallions, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, if using, and dressing in a large bowl. Stir 3-4 times until coated. Serve on lettuce leaves and garnish with cilantro sprigs.

title: Spicy Salad with Shrimp and Pork
ingredients: 300 g uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined, tails intact
500 g vegetable hummingbird flowers, stamens removed
10 red and green bird's eye chiles, chopped
steps: Bring a pan of water to a boil, add the shrimp, and blanch for 1-2 minutes, or until pink and cooked. Drain and set aside.

Return the water to a boil, add the pork, and blanch for 2-3 minutes, or until cooked. Drain and set aside. Return the water to a boil once more, add the vegetable hummingbird flowers, and blanch for 1 minute. Drain and set aside.

For the dressing, pound the chiles and garlic in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar and stir until the sugar dissolves. Transfer the dressing to a large serving bowl, add the shrimp, pork, and flowers, and mix well. Stir in the shallots and serve.

title: Glass Noodle Salad
ingredients: 50 g squid, sliced into 2 cm-thick rings
10 red bird's-eye chiles, very finely chopped
30 g Chinese celery stalks, sliced into 2.5 cm pieces
steps: Soak the noodles in water for 10 minutes. Drain, then blanch in boiling water for 1 minute, or cook according to the package directions. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the sliced pork in boiling water for 1-2 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Blanch the fish balls in boiling water for 1-2 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Blanch the squid in boiling water for 2-3 minutes, then drain and set aside. Blanch the ground pork in boiling water for 2-3 minutes, then drain and set aside.

Put the noodles in a large bowl. Add the sliced pork, fish balls, squid, ground pork, fried fish balls, Chinese fish cake, onion, chiles, sugar, lime juice, fish sauce, cilantro, and Chinese celery. Mix well and serve.

title: Spicy Shrimp and Mango Salad
ingredients: 2 tablespoons julienned sour green mango or shredded carrot
steps: To make the dressing, mix all the ingredients together in a bowl and set aside For the salad, mix all the ingredients together in a large bowl, add the dressing, and mix until combined. Garnish with the dried chiles and fried shallot and serve.

title: Cilantro Salad
ingredients: 90 g pork crackling, cut into small pieces
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles, garlic, ginger, shallots, galangal, lemongrass, cilantro roots, and shrimp paste thoroughly in a mortar with a pestle.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the chili paste, and stir-fry for 2 minutes, or until fragrant, then remove from the heat.
Put the cilantro and pork crackling in a bowl and mix well. Add the chili paste and a pinch of salt and mix well. Sprinkle with the fried garlic and shallots and serve.

title: Spicy Yard-Long Bean and Pork Salad
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop. Pound the chiles, shallots, garlic, salt, and shrimp paste in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Set aside.

Bring a pan of water to a boil. Add the water spinach and blanch for 30 seconds, then transfer to cold water and drain. Add the yard-long beans to the boiling water and blanch for 1 minute, then transfer to cold water and drain. Boil the eggplants and lablab beans separately for 2-3 minutes, then drain. Coarsely chop all the vegetables.

Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the garlic and chili paste and stir-fry for 1 minute. Add the pork and stir-fry for 3 minutes, then add the vegetables and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Transfer to a serving dish and garnish with the neem tree tips, shallots, cilantro, scallions, and sesame seeds, if using.

title: Spicy Dried Buffalo Skin Salad
steps: Heat the boiler (grill) to medium. Put the buffalo skin on the broiler (grill) rack and char to remove the hairs. Soak the skin in a bowl of water for 3 hours, then drain, transfer to a pan of boiling water, and boil for 20 minutes or until tender. Drain and set aside.

For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated then drain and chop. Pound the chiles, shallot, garlic, and salt in a mortar win a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and mix until combined. Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the garlic and 1½ teaspoons chili paste and cook for 1 minute or until fragrant. Add the tomatoes, buffalo skin, and 2 tablespoons water and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes. Transfer to a serving plate, sprinkle with the sesame seeds, and scallion (spring onion) and garnish with the cilantro (coriander) sprig. Serve.

title: Spicy Pork Liver Salad
ingredients: 100 g pork liver, rinsed, drained, and cut into bite-size pieces
raw or steamed vegetables, such as Chinese greens, cucumber, and napa (Chinese) cabbage, to serve
steps: Bring the broth to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the pork liver and blanch for 1-2 minutes, or until medium cooked.
Remove from the heat and add the chili flakes, lime juice, fish sauce, shallot, scallions, sawtooth cilantro, mint leaves, and ground toasted rice and mix well.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve with glutinous rice and raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Peanut Curd in Spicy Salad
prepTime: 10 minutes, plus soaking and cooling time
ingredients: 1 garlic bulb, cloves separated and finely sliced
steps: Soak the peanuts in water overnight, then drain. Grind them thoroughly in a mortar with a pestle until fine.

Bring 2 liters water and the ground peanuts to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Stir in the rice flour, then strain through cheesecloth (muslin) into a large, shallow rectangular container. Spread out the curd mixture and leave to cool until solid.

For the salad, cut the peanut curd into 2.5 cm pieces about 3-4 mm thick and place in a large bowl. Add the chili jam, salt, shallot, garlic, and pork and mix together. Add the lime juice, lemon juice, and cilantro and mix well. Sprinkle with the fried garlic and shallots and serve.

title: Spicy Beef Salad
ingredients: 300 g thin beef sirloin, tenderloin, or rump steak
1 cucumber, halved lengthwise and sliced into 1 cm-thick pieces
steps: Heat a charcoal or gas grill to 400°F/200°C, or preheat an indoor broiler to medium. Put the beef in a shallow dish, add the soy sauce, turn to coat, and marinate for about 10 minutes.
Grill or broil the beef for 4-5 minutes on each side. Remove, slice into strips, and set aside.
For the dressing, stir the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and chiles together until the sugar dissolves.
Put the beef, cucumber, tomatoes, shallots, and cilantro in a large bowl. Pour in the dressing, toss lightly, and serve.

title: Chinese Mustard Green Salad
ingredients: 60 g chopped Chinese mustard greens (with yellow flowers)
70 g white and black sesame seeds, roasted
steps: Blanch the mustard greens in a pan of boiling water for 1 minute, then drain and plunge into ice-cold water.
Mix the remaining ingredients in a large bowl. Drain the mustard greens, add them to the bowl, and mix well. Sprinkle with the fried garlic and shallots and serve.

title: Spicy Round Eggplant and Pork Salad
ingredients: 8 dried red bird's eye chiles, chopped
steps: Boil the pork for 3-4 minutes, or until cooked. Drain and pat dry, then pound thoroughly in a mortar. Tear the pork into small pieces and set aside.
Mix 475 ml water with the salt until dissolved. Halve the eggplants lengthwise, slice them lengthwise into 3 mm pieces, and soak in the salt water for 5 minutes.

For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop. Pound the chiles, shallots, garlic, galangal, and salt until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and mix thoroughly.

Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chopped garlic and chili paste and stir-fry for 1 minute, or until golden and fragrant. Add the pork and 1 tablespoon water and stir-fry for another 1-2 minutes. Remove from the heat.
Drain the eggplants and mix them with the pork and chili paste. Sprinkle with the cilantro, scallion, peppermint, and Vietnamese cilantro and serve.

title: Spicy Red Ant Salad
ingredients: 9 cm piece galangal, peeled and sliced
5 red and green bird's eye chiles, finely chopped
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
young jackfruit, peeled and seeded while wearing gloves, and cut into chunks
steps: Put the ants in an airtight container and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes, then transfer to the freezer for 30 minutes.
Roast the ants in a wok over medium heat for 6-8 minutes, or until dry. Set aside.

For the dressing, mix the tamarind, sugar, fermented fish sauce, fish sauce, shrimp paste, lime juice, and salt in a bowl. Transfer to a wok and warm over low heat for 2-3 minutes, or until the sugar dissolves. Remove from the heat and cool.
Add the ants, galangal, lemongrass, chiles, dried shrimp, and peanuts to the cooled dressing and stir until combined. Serve with the wild betel leaves, star gooseberry leaves, and young jackfruit.

title: Thai Spicy Salad with Giant Water Bug Eggs
ingredients: 5-7 red and green bird's eye chiles, finely chopped
2 scallions (spring onions), snipped into small lengths
steps: Heat the oil for deep-frying to 350°F/180°C. Deep-fry the squid and fish bladder for 5 minutes, or until crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.

Mix the fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar in a large bowl. Add the crispy fish bladder and squid, cashew nuts, onions, tomato, chiles, sweet shrimp if using, scallions, carrots, mango, celery, and giant water bug eggs. Mix well and serve.

title: Snail and Noodle Salad
ingredients: 300 g snakehead fish or catfish, cleaned
1 handful young pink mempat leaves or tamarind leaves, sliced
1 handful chayote shoots or young spinach, sliced
steps: Soak the snails in tepid water for 1-2 hours, then drain. Soak the noodles in water for 10 minutes, then drain and blanch in boiling water for 1 minute, or according to the package directions. Drain and set aside.

Fill a large bowl with water and add the vinegar. Remove and discard the outer red petals and small white flowers from the banana blossom. Cut off the tip and base, quarter the blossom lengthwise, and place it in the vinegar water. Separate and clean the layers, discard the flowers within, finely slice the leaves to 5 mm thick, and return them to the vinegar water.
Bring 750 ml water to a boil. Add the snails, reduce the heat, and simmer for 5 minutes. Drain, discard the shells, and set aside.
Bring 350 ml water to a boil in another pan. Add the fish and cook for 7-10 minutes. Drain, discard the bones and skin, and tear the flesh into small pieces.

Pound the chili flakes and shallots to a smooth paste. Transfer to a large bowl and add the snails and fish. Drain and rinse the banana blossom, add it with the remaining ingredients, and mix thoroughly. Garnish with the chiles and fried shallots and serve.

title: Pickled Vegetable Salad
ingredients: 1 x 1-inch/3.5-om piece fresh ginger, peeled and sliced
steps: Leave 3 chiles whole and finely chop the rest, then set aside.
Mix the pickled mustard greens, eggplant (aubergine), and ginger together in a large bowl. Sprinkle with the whole and finely chopped chiles. Serve.

title: Spicy Shiitake Mushroom Salad
ingredients: 230 g fresh shiitake mushrooms, stems discarded
3-5 red and green bird's eye chiles, finely chopped
raw vegetables, such as tomatoes, cucumber, lettuce, and cabbage, to serve
steps: Blanch the shiitake mushrooms in boiling water for 1 minute, or until cooked. Drain and pat dry, then slice into 5 mm strips and put in a large bowl.
Add the cilantro, shallots, kaffir lime leaves, scallions, garlic, sawtooth cilantro, ground toasted rice, chili flakes, lime juice, lemongrass, chiles, fish sauce, and chicken broth and mix well.
Garnish with the mint leaves and serve with raw vegetables.

title: Spicy Mushroom Salad
ingredients: 8-10 jumbo shrimp (king prawns), peeled and deveined
300 g mixed mushrooms, such as straw, king oyster, and shimeji mushrooms
1½ tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1 handful cilantro (coriander), coarsely chopped, to garnish
steps: Blanch the pork in a pan of boiling water for 2-3 minutes or until cooked. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the shrimp in another pan of boiling water for 1-2 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the mushrooms in another pan of boiling water for about 30 seconds. Drain and set aside.
For the dressing, stir the fish sauce, lime juice, chiles, and sugar together in a bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Put the pork, shrimp, mushrooms, scallions, shallots, and dressing in a large bowl and mix well. Transfer to a serving plate, sprinkle with cilantro, and serve.

title: Spicy Pork, Mushroom, and Seafood Salad
steps: Blanch the squid in a pan of boiling water for 2-3 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the pork in another pan of boiling water for 2-3 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the shrimp in another pan of boiling water for 1-2 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the mushrooms in another pan of boiling water for 1 minute. Drain and set aside.

Mix the pork, seafood, mushrooms, sugar, fish sauce, toasted rice, lime juice, shallots, and chili flakes in a bowl until thoroughly combined. Add the scallions and sawtooth cilantro and mix well. Sprinkle with peppermint leaves and serve.

title: Cucumber Salad
ingredients: 1 yard-long bean, cut into 4 cm lengths
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Coarsely pound the chiles, garlic, and yard-long bean in a mortar with a pestle.
Add the tomatoes, sugar, lime juice, fish sauce, and fermented fish sauce and mix well until the sugar dissolves.
Add the cucumber and crabmeat, if using, and mix gently. Serve.

title: Mixed Fruit and Vegetable Salad
ingredients: 2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Fill a large bowl with water and add the vinegar. Peel away and discard the outer red petals and small white flowers from the banana blossom. Cut off the tip and stem end, split the blossom in half lengthwise, then halve each piece again and put the quarters into the vinegar water.

Peel and clean each layer, discarding the banana flowers inside. Finely slice the blossom into 3 mm slices and return them to the vinegar water. Repeat until all the leaves have been sliced, then drain, rinse under cold running water, and drain again.

Pound the drained banana blossom, papaya, great morinda, star gooseberries, scallions, both kinds of cilantro, shallots, dried shrimp, sugar, chili flakes, fermented fish sauce, fish sauce, and lead tree seeds together in a mortar with a pestle. Serve on a bed of lettuce leaves.

title: Yard-Long Bean Salad
ingredients: 1½ teaspoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Finely pound the garlic and chiles in a mortar with a pestle.
Add the beans and pound coarsely.
Add the lime juice, sugar, salted crab, tomato, eggplant, dried shrimp, and fermented fish sauce.
Coarsely pound and mix with the pestle until thoroughly combined, then serve.

title: Spicy Pomelo Salad
ingredients: 1½ tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Cook the shrimp in a pan of boiling water for 1-2 minutes, or until pink, then drain and set aside.
Cook the pork in another pan of boiling water for 2-3 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Dry-fry the coconut in a skillet or frying pan over medium heat, stirring frequently, for 1-2 minutes, or until light brown. Transfer to a small bowl and set aside.
To make the dressing, put the sugar, salt, chili flakes, and coconut milk in a bowl and mix until the sugar has dissolved. Set aside.

Peel the pomelo and cut the flesh into segments. Remove and discard the pith and membrane, then break the flesh into small pieces and transfer to a large bowl. Add the dried shrimp, cooked shrimp, coconut, peanuts, garlic, and dressing and gently toss until well mixed.
Transfer to a serving plate, sprinkle with the cashew nuts, fried shallots, and chopped cilantro, and serve.

title: Papaya Salad
ingredients: 1 teaspoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1 yard-long bean, cut into 4 cm lengths
steps: Coarsely pound the chiles and garlic in a mortar with a pestle. Add the tomatoes, lime juice, fermented fish sauce, fish sauce, sugar, crabmeat, and bean, then use a spoon and the pestle to lightly pound and mix together until the sugar has dissolved. Add the papaya and pound to mis well. Serve with rice and grilled chicken.

title: Papaya and Fish Salad
ingredients: 75 g pickled cabbage, cut into small pieces
120 ml boiled shellfish, cut into small pieces
steps: Finely pound the chiles and garlic in a mortar with a pestle. Add the papaya, bean sprouts, pickled cabbage, shellfish, dried shrimp, fermented rice noodles, cilantro (coriander), tomatoes, roasted peanuts, and lead tree seeds. Season with the salt, fish sauces, and lime juice and mix until thoroughly combined. Serve.

title: Green Papaya Salad
ingredients: 1 yard-long bean, cut into 4 cm lengths
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Pound the chiles and garlic together in a mortar with a pestle. Add the yard-long bean and lightly crush.
Add the tomatoes, sugar, peanuts, dried shrimp, lime juice, lime wedges, and fish sauce. Gently mix until the sugar dissolves.
Add the papaya and mix together. Serve on its own or with grilled chicken.

title: Senna Leaf and Papaya Salad
ingredients: 3-5 red and green bird's eye chiles
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1 salted duck egg, quartered, to garnish
steps: Blanch the senna leaves in a pan of boiling water for 1 minute. Drain and set aside.
Pound the chiles and garlic finely in a mortar. Season with the lime juice, tamarind, sugar, and fish sauce, balancing the dressing to taste sour, salty, and sweet.
Add the senna leaves, dried shrimp, papaya, carrot, tomato, eggplant, and peanuts and mix well. Transfer to a lettuce-lined plate, garnish with the salted egg, and serve.

title: Spicy Blue Crab and Papaya Salad
ingredients: 2 live blue crabs, about 300 g each, cleaned
1 yard-long bean, cut into 5-7.5 cm pieces
1½ teaspoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
raw vegetables, such as yard-long beans and napa (Chinese) cabbage, to serve
steps: Put the crabs in the freezer for 20 minutes, then remove and put them in a large bowl.

Take one crab and place it on a cutting board. Turn the crab onto its back with its legs facing upward. Raise the tail flap and push a small screwdriver or skewer through the hole underneath. Press firmly down on the screwdriver handle until it reaches the other side of the shell. Remove the screwdriver and repeat with the remaining crab.
Remove the crab apron and carapace and rinse until clean. Cut each crab in half vertically, then cut each piece horizontally. Remove the claws, crush them, and set aside.
Blanch the crab pieces and claws in a pan of boiling water for 2-3 minutes, or until cooked, then drain and set aside.

Finely pound the chiles and garlic in a mortar with a pestle. Add the papaya, tomatoes, and yard-long bean and pound again. Add the crab and lightly pound and stir at the same time with the pestle and a spoon.
Add the fish sauce, sugar, and lime juice and mix well. Transfer to a serving plate and sprinkle with the cashew nuts. Serve with raw vegetables.

title: Durian Salad
ingredients: 3 celery stalks, cut into 2.5 cm lengths
2 tablespoons finely sliced red and green bird's eye chiles
steps: Peel the durian, cut the flesh into 4 cm lengths, and cut it again into matchsticks.
For the chili sauce, mix the lime juice, fish sauce, salt, sugar, and chiles in a bowl.
Put the durian, pork, carrot, scallions, and celery in a large bowl. Pour over the chili sauce and mix well. Serve.

title: Spicy Mango and Coconut Salad
ingredients: 1½ tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
300 g sour green mango, peeled and finely sliced
steps: Pound the dried shrimp to fine flakes in a mortar with a pestle and set aside.
Dry-fry the coconut in a wok over low-medium heat, stirring frequently, for about 2 minutes, until golden brown. Let cool.
Stir the coconut milk, salt, sugar, and shrimp paste together in a large bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Add the mango, dried shrimp, toasted coconut, shallots, and chiles and mix well. Transfer to a plate and serve.

title: Mango Salad with Chili Dip
ingredients: 2 x 500 g sour green mangoes, peeled
steps: Slice the mangoes lengthwise into 5 mm-thick slices, then soak in a bowl of cold water for 2-3 minutes, until firm and crunchy.
Mix the chili powder, sugar, and salt in a small bowl. Serve as a dry dip with the mango slices.

title: Spicy Fruit Salad
ingredients: 80 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1 rose apple, cut into 3 cm dice
½ green apple, cut into 3 cm dice
½ tomato, cut into 3 cm dice
steps: Pound the chiles in a mortar with a pestle until crushed.
Add the sugar, fish sauce, and lime juice and mix until the sugar dissolves.
Add the remaining ingredients and gently mix the fruit with the dressing. Serve.

title: Spicy Strawberry Salad
ingredients: 2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Pound the chiles in a mortar with a pestle.
Mix the garlic, lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, dried shrimp, and pounded chiles in a bowl. Add the strawberries and tomato, mix, and serve.

title: Phuket Pineapple Salad
ingredients: 80 g skinless and boneless chicken breast
8 uncooked shrimp, peeled and deveined, with tails intact
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Cut off the pineapple stem, then cut across the top 2-3 cm from the crown and set it aside. Use a long, thin knife to loosen the flesh, then scoop it out to leave a hollow pineapple bowl. Cut 150 g pineapple flesh into 2 cm cubes.
Cook the chicken breast in a pan of boiling water for 2-3 minutes, or until cooked. Remove with a slotted spoon and let cool, then tear into shreds.
Cook the shrimp in another pan of boiling water for 1-2 minutes, or until pink. Drain and set aside.
Dry-fry the coconut in a wok over medium heat for 2-3 minutes, or until light brown. Remove and set aside.
For the dressing, stir all the dressing ingredients together in a large bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Add the pineapple, shrimp, chicken, peanuts, dried shrimp, coconut, and scallions and gently mix until combined.
Spoon into the pineapple bowl, sprinkle with the fried shallots, and serve with lettuce leaves.

title: Spicy Banana Blossom Salad
ingredients: 10 uncooked shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails intact
3-5 red and green bird's-eye chiles, chopped
4 tablespoons Fried Shallots (see p. 64), to garnish
steps: Fill a large bowl with water and add the vinegar. Peel away and discard the outer red petals and the small white flowers from the banana blossom. Cut off the tip and base, split the blossom lengthwise, then cut each half in half again. Put the quarters in the vinegar water.

Peel and clean each layer, discarding the flowers inside. Slice the petals 5 mm thick and return them to the vinegar water. Repeat until all the petals are sliced, then drain, rinse under cold water, and drain again.
Blanch the sliced banana blossom in boiling water for 10-15 seconds. Drain, rinse under cold water, and drain again.
Cook the shrimp in boiling water for 1-2 minutes, then drain.
Mix the chili jam with 3 tablespoons coconut milk. Add the sugar, fish sauce, lime juice, chiles, peanuts, and shallot and mix well.
Add the banana blossom and shrimp and toss well. Garnish with the fried shallots and serve with the quartered egg.

title: Chicken and Banana Blossom Salad
ingredients: 2 skinless, boneless chicken breasts, chopped into bite-size pieces
10 kaffir lime leaves, torn, to garnish
3 lemongrass stalks, finely chopped, to garnish
steps: Fill a large bowl with water and add the vinegar. Peel away and discard the outer red petals and the small white banana flowers. Trim the tip and base of the blossom, quarter it lengthwise, and place the pieces in the vinegar water.
Peel and clean each layer, discarding the flowers inside. Slice the layers 5 mm thick and return them to the vinegar water. Repeat until the whole blossom is prepared.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the garlic and chili paste and stir-fry for 1 minute. Add 750 ml water and bring to a boil.
Add the shallots and chicken, return to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes.

Drain and rinse the banana blossom, then add it to the wok and cook for 5 minutes. Add the sawtooth cilantro, scallions, cilantro, Vietnamese cilantro, galangal, and peppermint and cook for 3 minutes.
Garnish with the kaffir lime leaves and lemongrass and serve.

title: Indian Trumpet Flower Pod Spicy Salad
steps: Dry-fry the flower pod in a wok over medium heat for about 5 minutes, until toasted. Let cool slightly, remove the outer layer, and rinse under cold running water.
Slice the pod into 5 mm pieces. Put it in a bowl with the salt, lime juice, fish sauce, ground toasted rice, scallion, sawtooth cilantro, kaffir lime leaves, and chili powder and toss gently.
Garnish with peppermint leaves and serve.

title: Egg Tofu and Ground Pork Soup
ingredients: 1 bunch cilantro (coriander) leaves, coarsely chopped, to garnish
steps: For the egg tofu, combine the soy milk and salt in a bowl. Add the eggs and whisk gently, avoiding bubbles. Pour into a shallow dish to a depth of about 4 cm. Steam over very low heat for 12-15 minutes, or until firm, then cut into 3 x 3 x 1.5 cm pieces. The egg tofu can be refrigerated for 2-3 days.
Combine the pork and Saam-Gler in a bowl. Add 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce and mix well, then shape into small balls.

Bring the broth and 475 ml water to a boil in a pan. Add the pork balls and simmer for 2-3 minutes, or until they float. Add the salt and remaining soy sauce, then add the egg tofu and celery and cook for 2 minutes. Garnish with cilantro and serve.

title: Fermented Fish and Jackfruit Soup
ingredients: 1 broiled (grilled) sea bass or sea bream, cut into bite-size pieces
1 kg young jackfruit, peeled and seeded wearing gloves, and cut into 2.5 cm slices
100 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Pound the shallots, garlic, fingerroot, and lemongrass thoroughly in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the broiled (grilled) fish and pound until combined. Bring the coconut milk to a boil in another pan over medium heat, add the pounded fish paste and the fermented fish, return to a boil, and add the pork Return to a boil and add the jackfruit then continue to boil for 5 minutes until cooked. Add the salt, fish sauce, sugar, tamarind, and kaffir lime leaves and stir. Ladle into soup bowls and serve.

title: Mullet Soup
ingredients: 1 piece fresh ginger, about 7 cm, peeled and sliced
1 piece galangal, about 7.5 cm, peeled and sliced
1 gray mullet or red snapper, about 500 g, cleaned, descaled, and cut into 5 cm pieces
75 ml mangrove palm vinegar, white wine vinegar, or Tamarind Puree (see p. 63)
steps: Bring 960 ml water to a boil in a large pan. Add the ginger, galangal, lemongrass, chiles, and shallots, return to a boil, and cook for 5 minutes. Carefully add the fish and cook for another 5 minutes. Season with the vinegar and salt. Ladle into soup bowls and serve.

title: Spicy-and-Sour Mackerel Soup
ingredients: 400-500 g horse mackerel, cleaned and descaled
10 green and red bird's-eye chiles, sliced
steps: Bring the broth to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the salt, lemongrass, garlic, and kaffir lime leaves and boil for 2-3 minutes.
Add the fish sauce and lime juice, stir, and increase the heat to high. Add the mackerel and return to a boil without stirring.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and cook for another 2-3 minutes. Add the chiles and cilantro and stir. Ladle into soup bowls and serve hot.

title: Sweet-and-Sour Mackerel Soup
ingredients: 5 small whole mackerel, cleaned and descaled
1 x 2.5 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and julienned
steps: Pound the cilantro roots, salt, shrimp paste, and shallots together in a mortar with a pestle.
Bring the broth or water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the pounded mixture, stir, and return to a boil.
Add the tamarind, sugar, and fish sauce and return to a boil. Add the mackerel and cook for about 10 minutes.
Add the ginger and scallions and stir. Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the dried chiles, and serve.

title: Sea Bass Soup with Cardamom Shoots
ingredients: 500 g sea bass fillet, cut into 4 cm pieces
200 g Siam cardamom shoots, cut into 4 cm lengths
steps: Bring a large pan of water to a boil. Add the sea bass, cardamom shoots, and salacca (snake fruit).
Return to a boil and add the kaffir lime leaves, fish sauce, lime juice, chiles, and cilantro. Cook for 3-4 minutes.
Ladle into soup bowls and serve.

title: Sea Bass in Herb Soup
ingredients: 1 teaspoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
500 g sea bass fillets, cut into bite-size chunks
steps: Bring 475 ml water to a boil in a large pan. Add the fish sauce, shrimp paste, shallots, and garlic and return to a boil.
Add the tamarind sauce and sugar and return to a boil. Add the sea bass and cook for 3-5 minutes.
Remove from the heat and add the sweet basil, star gooseberry, and hairy basil leaves. Ladle into soup bowls and serve.

title: Sea Bass and Rice Soup
ingredients: 1 x 300 g sea bass, cleaned, filleted, and cut into 3-4 cm slices, bones reserved
5 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and julienned
steps: Soak the shiitake mushrooms in warm water for 15 minutes. Squeeze dry, cut into quarters, and set aside.
Bring the chicken broth and 350 ml water to a boil in a large pan over high heat. Add the galangal, garlic, black pepper, and fish bones and boil for 4-5 minutes without stirring.
Strain through a fine strainer into a clean pan. Return to a boil over medium heat, add the soy sauce, fish sauce, and shiitake mushrooms, and stir.
Return to a boil, add the sea bass, and cook for 2 minutes without stirring, or until the fish is cooked. Add the rice and celery and boil for another 1-2 minutes.
Ladle into soup bowls, garnish with fried garlic, scallions, cilantro, and ginger, and serve.

title: Spicy-and-Sour Soup with Egg Noodles
ingredients: 100 g squid, halved and tentacles removed
4 uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined, tails intact
steps: Rinse the sea bass and pat dry. Put it in a pan with enough water to cover by about 1 inch (2.5 cm) and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 2-3 minutes, until cooked, then drain.
Cook the noodles in boiling water for 1 minute, or according to the package directions. Drain, transfer to a serving bowl, and set aside.

Put the galangal, kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, shallots, mushrooms, tomatoes, squid, shrimp, and cooked fish in a large pan. Add the Chili Jam, salt, lime juice, fish sauce, and milk. Pour in the chicken broth, bring to a simmer, and cook for about 3 minutes, until hot. Pour over the noodles, garnish with cilantro, and serve.

title: Spicy Snakehead Fish and Lotus Stem Soup
ingredients: 3 lemongrass stalks, cut into 2.5 cm pieces
800 g snakehead fish or catfish, cleaned, descaled, and cut into 2.5 cm pieces
200 g peeled and sliced lotus stem
4-6 dried red chiles, seeded and chopped
2 sawtooth cilantro (coriander) sprigs, chopped, to garnish
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, shallots, tamarind, and salt and return to a boil.
Add the fish and lotus stem and cook for about 8 minutes, then remove from the heat.
Add the fish sauce, lemon juice, and chiles. Ladle into soup bowls, garnish with sawtooth cilantro, and serve.

title: Spicy Vegetable Soup
ingredients: 100 g chayote shoots or young spinach
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles, garlic, shallots, and salt in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and mix to combine.
Bring the broth to a boil in a large pan over medium heat, add the chili paste, and stir until dissolved. Add the dried fish and return to a boil.

Reduce the heat and simmer for 5-7 minutes, until the fish softens. Add the chayote shoots or spinach and the tomatoes and simmer, stirring occasionally, for another 3-4 minutes. Ladle into bowls and serve.

title: Salmon Sour Soup
ingredients: 2 x 40 g salmon fillets, cut into 1 cm-thick slices
1 x 5 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and julienned
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
2 scallions (spring onions), cut into 2 cm lengths
4 dried red chiles, seeded, to garnish
steps: For the paste, pound the black peppercorns, shallots, and cilantro roots in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and mix until thoroughly combined.
Bring the broth to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the paste and crushed shallots and boil for 1-2 minutes.
Add the salmon and ginger, return to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Add the tamarind, sugar, and fish sauce, followed by the scallions. Ladle into a soup bowl, garnish with the dried chiles, and serve.

title: Very Spicy Papaya and Young Coconut Soup
ingredients: 600 g mixed fruit, such as young papaya, young coconut meat, ripe banana, pineapple, and pickled bamboo
1 kg sea bass, mullet, or king mackerel fillets, cut into 2.5-5 cm pieces
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1 garlic bulb, cloves separated and chopped
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the dried and fresh chiles, turmeric, garlic, and shallots in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and mix until thoroughly combined.
Bring the water to a boil in a large pan. Add the chili paste and lime juice and return to a boil, then add all the fruit.
Return to a boil, add the fish, and cook for 5 minutes. Season with the salt and sugar, ladle into soup bowls, and serve.

title: Spicy Vegetable and Fish Soup
ingredients: 500 g whole snakehead fish, cleaned, skinned, head and bones removed, and cut into 5 cm pieces
100 g pumpkin, cut into 2.5 cm slices
200 g angled gourd, peeled, halved, and cut into 2 cm-thick slices
10-15 young Ceylon spinach or ordinary spinach leaves
steps: For the chili paste, pound the chiles, salt, peppercorns, fingerroot, shallots, and shrimp paste together thoroughly in a mortar with a pestle. Add the fish and pound again until smooth. Set aside.

Bring the chicken broth (stock) to a boil in a pan over high heat. Add the chili paste and fish sauce and return to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium, add the pumpkin and baby corn, and return to a boil for 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms, angled gourd, Ceylon spinach, ivy gourd leaves, if using, and basil. Serve.

title: Spicy-and-Sour Tilapia Soup
ingredients: 2 lemongrass stalks, coarsely crushed and cut into 5 cm lengths
600 g tilapia, cleaned, filleted, and cut into bite-size pieces
10-15 red and green bird's-eye chiles, pounded
steps: Bring the broth and salt to a boil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Add the galangal, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, shallots, and garlic and boil for about 2 minutes.
Add the fish sauce, lime juice, and tomatoes and return to a boil.
Add the tilapia and cook for 3-4 minutes without stirring, until cooked.
Stir in the chiles and cilantro, ladle into bowls, and serve.

title: Spicy Eel Soup
ingredients: 3 lemongrass stalks, diagonally sliced into 4 cm lengths
300 g eel, cleaned and cut into 5 cm lengths
steps: Bring the broth and 475 ml water to a boil in a large pan.
Add the fingerroot, kaffir lime leaves, galangal, lemongrass, garlic, shallots, and chile powder and return to a boil.
Add the eel and return to a boil. Add the fish sauce and tamarind puree and boil for 7-10 minutes, until the eel is tender.
Stir in the basil, if using. Ladle into bowls and serve.

title: Spicy Shrimp Soup
ingredients: 3-7 lemongrass stalks, diagonally sliced into 3 cm lengths
12 uncooked jumbo shrimp, peeled and deveined
3 scallions, cut into 4 cm lengths, to garnish
steps: Pour the broth and 475 ml water into a large pan, add the salt, and bring to a boil over medium heat.
Add the galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and lemongrass and boil for 1-2 minutes.
Add the onion and tomatoes and return to a boil. Add the mushrooms and shrimp and boil for about 1 minute, until the shrimp are cooked.
Add the lime juice, chiles, sugar, fish sauce, and shallots and stir. Ladle into bowls, garnish with cilantro and scallions, and serve.

title: Melinjo Leaf and Shrimp in Coconut Milk Soup
ingredients: 1 handful melinjo leaves or young spinach
4-5 uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined, tails intact
steps: Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a large pan. Add the shrimp paste, sugar, and salt, stir, and return to a boil.
Add the melinjo leaves and shrimp and return to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 2 minutes, or until the shrimp are cooked. Ladle into soup bowls and serve.

title: Spicy Vegetable Soup with Shrimp
ingredients: 200 g uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined, tails intact
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles, fingerroot, peppercorns, and shallots in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and dried shrimp and mix until combined.
Bring 475 ml water and the chili paste to a simmer in a pan over low heat. Add the fish sauce, salt, and sugar and stir well.
Add the shrimp, pumpkin, angled loofah, watermelons, waxy corn, bottle gourd, and dried shrimp. Stir well and cook for 7-10 minutes. Add the lemon basil leaves and serve.

title: Dried Squid, Pork Rib, and Radish Soup
ingredients: 2 × 30 g dried squid, sliced crosswise into 2 cm-wide pieces
400 g soft-bone pork ribs, cleaned and chopped into 4 cm pieces
400 g daikon (mooli) radish, peeled, halved lengthwise, and cut crosswise into 2 cm-thick pieces
3 scallions (spring onions), chopped into 4 cm lengths
steps: Soak the dried squid in water for 10 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Bring 950 ml water, the salt, peppercorns, and cilantro roots to a boil over medium heat. Add the pork ribs and boil for 4-5 minutes, then add the daikon and boil for another 4-5 minutes.
Add the soy sauce and soaked squid. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, until the pork is tender.
Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the cilantro and scallions, and serve.

title: Stuffed Squid Soup
ingredients: 200-250 g small squid, cleaned, with tentacles removed and reserved
steps: Pound the garlic and peppercorns to a smooth paste. Transfer to a large bowl, add the pork and 1 teaspoon soy sauce, and mix well. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 10-15 minutes.
Stuff the pork mixture into the squid cavities, then lightly score each squid once or twice.
Pour the broth and 350 ml water into a large pan. Add the cilantro root and salt and bring to a boil over medium heat. Add the stuffed squid and tentacles and cook for 8-10 minutes, or until cooked.
Add the remaining soy sauce and Chinese celery and stir a few times. Remove from the heat, ladle into soup bowls, and serve.

title: Fish Noodle Soup
steps: Soak the noodles in water for 10 minutes, then drain and blanch in boiling water for 1 minute, or prepare according to the package directions. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the fish balls in boiling water for 2 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.
For the soup, combine the broth, cilantro roots, garlic, peppercorns, salt, soy sauce, and sugar in a pan. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Divide the noodles and bean sprouts among serving bowls. Pour about 300 ml soup into each bowl and top with the fish balls, fish cake, scallions, cilantro, and Fried Garlic. Serve.

title: Spicy Buffalo Meat Soup
ingredients: 1¼ kg buffalo meat or beef brisket, diced
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles, peppercorns, shallots, garlic, lemongrass, galangal, and coriander seeds in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and pound again until combined.
Pour the water into a large pan, add the chili paste, and stir until dissolved. Bring to a boil over medium heat, add the buffalo or beef, and return to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 20 minutes. Add the lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves and cook for another 10 minutes.
Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the cilantro, scallions, and sawtooth cilantro, and serve.

title: Oxtail Soup
ingredients: 2 kg oxtail, cut into 2.5-5 cm pieces
7 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and sliced
steps: Put the cardamom pods, bay leaves, cilantro roots, garlic, and peppercorns into a herb infuser and set aside.

Bring 3 liters water to a boil over high heat. Add the oxtail and boil for 20-30 minutes, skimming away any scum. Add the herb infuser and cinnamon, reduce the heat to low, and simmer for 2 hours, or until the oxtail is tender.
Remove the oxtail and set aside. Strain the soup through cheesecloth into a clean pan and bring it back to a boil over medium heat, adding more water if necessary.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the onion and ginger and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until softened. Transfer to the soup, add the tomatoes, and cook for another 30 minutes.
Ladle into serving bowls and season with the fish sauce and lime juice. Garnish with the chiles, fried shallots, celery, scallions, cilantro, and lime wedges and serve.

title: Clear Soup with Pork Balls and Noodles
prepTime: 10 minutes, plus soaking and marrating times
steps: Soak the noodles in a bowl of water for 5 minutes, or according to package directions. Drain, cut into short lengths, and set aside.
Mix the pork, 1 tablespoon sugar, and the soy sauce in a large bowl. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 10-15 minutes. Add the noodles, mix together, shape into small balls, and set aside.
Bring the chicken broth to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the fish sauce and remaining sugar, then add the pork balls.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 4-5 minutes, or until the pork balls float to the surface. Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the cilantro leaves, and serve.

title: Pork and Anise Soup with Rice Noodles
ingredients: 700 g pork shoulder, cut into 3 cm cubes
4 pieces rock sugar or ½ tablespoon granulated sugar
40 g chopped scallions (spring onions) and cilantro (coriander)
steps: To make the broth (stock) put the cinnamon stick, star anise, garlic, peppercorns and Cilantro (coriander) roots into an herb infuser.

Bring the pork broth, herb infuser, and pickled garlic to a boil in a large pan over high heat. Add the pork, salt, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar. Return to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 1½ hours or until the pork is tender. Soak the vermicelli in a bowl of water for 10 minutes, then drain and blanch in a pan of boiling water for 1 minute or prepare according to package directions, until cooked. Drain.

Divide the vermicelli, fried garlic oil, cooked pork, and bean sprouts among serving bowls. Pour 350 ml of the broth into each bowl and garnish with the radish, scallions (spring onions), and cilantro (coriander). Serve.

title: Red Sauce Noodle Soup
ingredients: 1 daikon (mooli) radish, cut diagonally into 1 cm-thick slices
100 g water spinach, cut into 2.5 cm pieces
8 pieces cooked squid, cut into 2.5 cm pieces
steps: Bring the pork stock to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the cilantro roots, daikon, and salt and return to a boil. Boil for 5 minutes, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for another 5 minutes.
For the red sauce, put all its ingredients in a food processor with 75 ml water and process until smooth. Set aside.
For the pickled chiles, process all their ingredients in a food processor until smooth. Set aside.
Blanch the water spinach and rice noodles in boiling water for 1 minute, or prepare the noodles according to the package directions, then drain.

Divide the water spinach, noodles, squid, pig's blood curd, fish balls, tofu, red sauce, and pickled chiles among serving bowls. Pour 250 ml pork stock into each bowl, place a fried wonton on top, and serve.

title: Noodle Soup with Roasted Pork and Wontons
ingredients: 2 Chinese fish cakes, cut into 2 cm pieces
2 tablespoons chopped salted dried cabbage leaves
50 g finely chopped scallions (spring onions) and cilantro (coriander), to garnish
steps: For the roasted pork, combine the pork, Saam-Gler, oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, five-spice powder, and food coloring in a bowl. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator overnight, or for at least 2 hours.
Preheat the oven to 325°F/160°C. Put the pork in a roasting pan and roast for 45-55 minutes, or until cooked through. Let cool, then slice.

For the wontons, combine the pork, Saam-Gler, oyster sauce, soy sauce, and sugar in a bowl. Put 1 teaspoon of filling in the center of each wrapper, dampen the edges, and fold into a triangle. Cook the wontons in boiling water for 2-3 minutes, or until they float. Drain and drizzle with a little oil.
For the soup, bring the broth to a boil with the cilantro roots, garlic, peppercorns, salt, soy sauce, and daikon. Reduce the heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes.
Soak the rice noodles in water for 10 minutes, then blanch for about 1 minute, or cook according to the package directions. Drain. Blanch the ground pork for 2-3 minutes and drain.

Divide the noodles, roasted pork, wontons, blanched pork, Fried Garlic, fish cakes, peanuts, cabbage, and radish among six bowls. Add about 250 ml hot soup to each bowl. Season with fish sauce and sugar to taste, garnish with the scallion and cilantro mixture, and serve.

title: Pork Noodle Soup
ingredients: 200 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
140 g diagonally sliced yard-long beans, cut into 2 cm lengths
steps: Soak the dried noodles in a bowl of water for 10 minutes, or according to package directions, until soft. Drain and set aside.

Bring a medium pan of water to a boil over medium heat. Add the pork loin, reduce the heat to a simmer, and cook for 8-10 minutes until cooked. Remove with a slotted spoon, drain in a colander, and let cool.
Return the pan of boiling water to the heat, add the pork liver, and cook for about 2 minutes until cooked. Drain, let cool, thinly slice, and cover.
Bring 75 ml water to a boil in a small pan over medium heat. Add the ground pork and stir for 1-2 minutes or until cooked. Drain and set aside, reserving the cooking water.
Heat the sugar and 120 ml water in another small pan over medium heat and stir until the sugar has dissolved and become syrupy. Set aside.
Blanch the yard-long beans in a pan of boiling water for 1 minute, then drain and set aside.

For the soup, put the cilantro roots, garlic, and black peppercorns in a cheesecloth herb bag. Pour the broth into a large pan, add the bag, and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 2-3 minutes.
For the sauce, mix the fish sauce, lime juice, peanuts, chili flakes, 1½ tablespoons sugar syrup, 1½ tablespoons ground pork, and the reserved cooking water in a bowl.
Cook the noodles in boiling water for 1 minute, or according to package directions, until soft. Drain and divide among serving bowls. Drizzle over the fried garlic oil and stir to combine.
Pour a little sauce and 350 ml soup into each bowl. Add the pork liver, sliced pork, eggs, yard-long beans, lettuce, scallion, and cilantro, then serve.

title: Spicy Pork Soup with Straw Mushrooms
ingredients: 800 g pork short ribs, cut into bite-size pieces
15 red and green bird's eye chiles pounded
steps: Bring 1.2 liters water and the pork ribs to a boil in a large pan over medium heat, then reduce the heat and simmer for 40 minutes. Remove any scum with a slotted spoon. Drain and set aside.

Heat the broth (stock) in a pan over medium heat. Add the lemongrass, mushrooms, boiled meat, chiles, fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and cilantro (coriander). Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the fried shallots and chili flakes, and serve.

title: Spicy Pork and Madan Leaf Soup
ingredients: 1 kg boneless pork leg, cut into bite-size pieces
120 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1.5 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped
1 garlic bulb, cloves separated and chopped
steps: For the chile paste, dry-fry the galangal, shallots, garlic, lemongrass, and cilantro root in a wok over medium heat for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Transfer to a mortar and pound with the dried chiles, salt, and shrimp paste.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chile paste and sauté for 1 minute.
Add the pork, fish sauce, and sugar and mix well. Transfer to a pan, add the coconut milk, and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for about 10 minutes, until the pork softens. Add the madan leaves and return to a boil. Ladle into bowls and serve.

title: Roasted Duck Noodle Soup
ingredients: 1 kg whole duck, cleaned and without giblets
1¼ tablespoons black salted soybeans, finely pounded
1 small cinnamon stick, broken into small pieces
steps: Preheat the oven to 300°F/150°C/Gas Mark 2.
Rinse the duck in cold water and pat dry. Rub it all over with the salt flakes and leave for 30 minutes. Rinse off the salt, pat dry, and set aside.

Pound the ginger, garlic, and cilantro roots until smooth. Mix with the five-spice powder, salted soybeans, salt, liquor or brandy, and sugar. Put the mixture inside the duck and place the duck on a roasting tray.

For the honey sauce, mix the honey, thick soy sauce, and 75 ml water. Brush the duck all over 2-3 times, then roast for about 1¾ hours, or until cooked, brushing with more sauce every 30 minutes. Cover with foil and rest for at least 15 minutes. Remove the drumsticks, carve the meat, and slice it into strips.

For the soup, heat the broth over medium heat. Put the star anise, cinnamon, garlic, cilantro roots, and black pepper in a spice bag and add it to the broth. Boil for 5 minutes. Season with soy sauce, salt, sugar, and dark soy sauce. Reduce the heat and simmer for 2-3 minutes.

Divide the noodles, bean sprouts, scallions, fried garlic, and duck among bowls. Pour about 250 ml soup into each bowl. Season to taste with vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, and chili flakes, if using, and serve.

title: Chicken and Coconut Soup
ingredients: 300 g black-skinned chicken breast or boneless chicken thigh, cut into 3 × 4 cm pieces
2 whole young coconuts, opened at the top and drained, with tops reserved as lids
4 dried red bird's-eye chiles, seeded, to garnish
steps: Bring the chicken broth and salt to a boil over medium heat.
Pound the cilantro root, shallot, lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves to a paste. Add it to the pan and boil for 1-2 minutes.
Add the chicken and boil for 3-4 minutes, or until cooked. Add the young coconut flesh, fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and coconut milk and cook for another 2 minutes.
Add the chopped chiles and cilantro. Ladle the soup into the whole young coconuts, garnish with Chili Jam oil and the dried chiles, and serve.

title: Spicy Chicken and Taro Soup
ingredients: 300 g chicken, either half a whole chicken or boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
200 g taro, peeled and cut into 3 cm dice
20 g chopped scallions (spring onions), to garnish
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles, peppercorns, garlic, shallots, and lemongrass to a smooth paste. Add the shrimp paste and mix to combine.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chili paste and cook for 1 minute, or until fragrant. Add the chicken and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes.
Pour in the broth and bring to a boil. Add the taro and salt, reduce the heat to medium-low, and simmer for 4-5 minutes, or until the taro is tender.
Remove from the heat, ladle into soup bowls, garnish with the scallions and cilantro, and serve.

title: Pickled Lime
ingredients: 1 winter melon, peeled, seeded, and cut into 7 x 3 cm pieces
steps: Soak: the shiitake mushrooms in a bowl of hot water for 15 minutes, then squeeze to drain, slice into bite-size pieces, and set aside. Bring the broth (stock) and 750 ml water to a boil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken, cilantro (coriander) root, and salt and return to a boil. Remove any scum with a slotted spoon. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes. Add the pickled lime juice, pickled limes. and shiitake mushrooms, then simmer again for 10 minutes. Add the winter melon and soy sauce and continue to simmer for another 20 minutes or until the chicken and winter melon are tender. Stir gently. Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with white pepper, and serve.

title: Sour-and-spicy Chicken Soup with Tamarind Leaves
ingredients: 2 lemongrass stalks, cut into 4 cm diagonal slices
1 whole 400 g chicken, chopped with the bone into small pieces
steps: Bring the broth (stock) and salt to a boil over high heat in a large pan. Add the galangal lemongrass, and shallots and boil for 1 minute. Had the chicken and return to a boil. Remove any scum with a slotted spoon. Reduce the heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes until cooked and tender. Add the fish sauce, kaffir lime leaves young tamarind leaves, tomatoes, and chiles Ladle into soup bowls and serve.

title: Daylily and Shiitake Mushroom Soup
ingredients: 250 g pork short ribs, cut into bite-size pieces
steps: Bring 1.2 liters water to a boil over medium heat. Add the pork ribs, white pepper, garlic, and cilantro roots and return to a boil. Skim, reduce the heat, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until tender.
Meanwhile, soak the daylily in water for 15-20 minutes. Rinse it 4-5 times under cold running water and squeeze dry. Discard the coarse stems and tie each daylily into a knot.
Add the daylily, shiitake mushrooms, and goji berries to the pan and simmer for about 10 minutes, or until the daylily has softened. Season to taste, ladle into bowls, and serve.

title: Shiitake and Stinkhorn Mushroom Soup
steps: Bring 1 liter water to a boil over medium heat. Add the pork ribs and return to a boil. Skim, reduce the heat, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until tender.

Meanwhile, soak the shiitake and stinkhorn mushrooms separately in hot water for about 15 minutes. Squeeze the softened shiitakes dry and cut into bite-size pieces. Rinse the stinkhorns to remove any dirt, squeeze dry, and cut into bite-size pieces.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the mushrooms and sauté for 1-2 minutes, or until dry. Season with some of the soy sauce, then remove from the heat.
When the pork-rib broth is clear, add the goji berries, red dates, salt, black pepper, and remaining soy sauce. When the ribs are tender, add the mushrooms. Ladle into bowls and serve.

title: Bitter Gourd and Pork Rib Soup
steps: Trim the ends from the bitter gourd. Halve it lengthwise and scrape out the seeds and white fiber, then halve each piece lengthwise again and cut crosswise into 5 cm lengths.
Dissolve 1 tablespoon salt in 475 ml water. Add the bitter gourd and soak for 15-30 minutes, then drain and rinse.

Pour 950 ml water into a large pan. Add the garlic, cilantro roots, peppercorns, and remaining 1 teaspoon salt and bring to a boil over high heat. Add the pork ribs and soy sauce and boil for 4-5 minutes.

Add the bitter gourd and boil for another 10 minutes without stirring, skimming any scum. Reduce the heat, cover, and cook for another 50-60 minutes, or until the pork is tender. Garnish with cilantro and serve.

title: Pork and Bottle Gourd Soup
ingredients: 400 g pork tenderloin or short ribs, sliced
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add the pork, bottle gourd, sugar, and salt and cook for about 30 minutes.
Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the scallions and cilantro, and serve.

title: Chinese Cabbage Soup
ingredients: 300 g pork side (belly), cut into 2 cm-thick slices
250 g choy sum (Chinese flowering cabbage), cut into 6 cm strips
steps: Preheat the broiler (grill) to medium.
Pound the shallots, garlic, and shrimp paste in a mortar with a pestle to a fine paste.
Place the soybean sheet on a broiler pan and broil for about 2 minutes, until fragrant and dark brown. Let cool, then add it to the mortar and pound until ground.
Bring the water to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the pork and salt and boil for 20-30 minutes, until softened, skimming away any scum.
Add the paste, ground soybean sheet, tamarind, fish sauce, sugar, and cabbage and continue boiling for 4-5 minutes, until the cabbage is soft.
Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the fried garlic and roasted chiles, and serve.

title: Spicy Soup with Chinese Mustard Greens
steps: Pound the chiles, shallots, garlic, and salt together in a mortar with a pestle. Place the soybean sheet on the broiler (grill) pan and broil (grill) for about 2 minutes until fragrant and garlic brown. Let cool, then add to the mortar and pound with the pestle until ground. Bring 475 ml water to a boil in a pan over medium heat, add the Chinese mustard greens, and cook for 3-4 minutes And the chile and shallot mixture, stir, and simmer for 2-3 minutes Ladle into in soup bowls, sprinkle with the scallions spring onions), and serve.

title: Spicy Catfish and Snake Gourd Curry
ingredients: 300 g catfish, cleaned, head removed, and cut into 2.5 cm-thick pieces
230 g snake gourd or zucchini (courgette), cut into 2.5 cm-thick slices
a handful of wild bitter gourd leaves or other bitter green leaves
a handful of sweet basil leaves
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378) or Glutinous Rice (see p. 378)
steps: For the chili paste, soak the chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop. Pound the chiles, shallots, lemongrass, and salt in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Set aside.

Bring the broth to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the chili paste and boil for 1 minute. Add the fish and ground toasted rice and return to a boil, then season with the fermented fish sauce and fish sauce.

Add the snake gourd or zucchini, both kinds of eggplant, wild bitter gourd leaves, and scallions. Stir gently and boil for 3-5 minutes, or until the vegetables soften. Add the basil, stir again, and remove from the heat. Serve with rice.

title: Spicy Catfish and Jackfruit Curry
ingredients: 300 g young jackfruit, peeled and seeded wearing gloves, and cut into 2.5 cm slices
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles and the remaining chili paste ingredients in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Set aside.

Bring 475 ml water to a boil in a large pan, add the chili paste and jackfruit, and cook for 3-4 minutes or until the jackfruit has softened. Add the catfish and cook for another 3-4 minutes, then add the tomatoes, tamarind, fermented fish sauce, and sugar and stir gently. Remove from the heat and sprinkle with the chopped cilantro (coriander) and scallions (spring onions). Serve.

title: Spicy Catfish and Tree Basil Curry
ingredients: 500 g catfish, head removed and cut into 2 cm-thick pieces
2 handfuls of tree basil or holy basil leaves, chopped
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the chili paste, and cook for 1-2 minutes or until fragrant. Add the coconut milk and bring to a boil. Add the fish, cook for 4 minutes, then add the chiles, fish sauce, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Stir and cook for another 1-2 minutes or until the fish is fully flavored. Add the tree basil, stir a couple times, then serve.

title: Fried Sheatfish Curry
ingredients: 1 x 300 g small white sheatfish, cleaned, gutted
2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
2-3 orange spur chiles, finely sliced diagonally
steps: Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the fish for 8-10 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Set aside. Bring the coconut milk to boil in a clean wok over medium heat and add the chili paste. Stir for 2 minutes or until thoroughly combined and the coconut milk has thickened. Season with the fish sauce, sugar, and evaporated milk if using. Stir until the sugar has dissolved. Add the fish and cook for 1-2 minutes or until full-favored. Add the chiles and most of the basil leaves. Stir 3-4 times and remove from the heat. Garnish with the remaining basil leaves and serve.

title: Spicy Catfish and Bamboo Shoot Curry
ingredients: 200 g sour and salty pickled bamboo shoots, rinsed and coarsely chopped
1 x 300 g catfish, cleaned and chopped into 2 cm-thick pieces
5 red and green bird's eye chiles, chopped
steps: For the paste, pound the chiles, garlic, lemongrass, shallots, turmeric, and salt thoroughly in a mortar with a pestle. Add the fermented fish and pound until thoroughly combined. Set aside.

Bring the broth (stock) and 475 ml water to a boil in a pan over high heat. Add the bamboo shoots and boil for 4-5 minutes to allow the pickled bamboo to flavor the stock. Add the fish sauce andi fish and cook for another 4-5 minutes. Transfer to a serving bowl and sprinkle with the cilantro (coriander) and scallions (spring onions). Serve.

title: Sour Sea Bass and Salacca Curry
ingredients: 3 garlic bulbs, cloves separated and halved
1 × 1 kg sea bass, cleaned, filleted, and cut into 5 cm pieces
50 g red and green bird's-eye chiles, coarsely chopped
steps: Bring 1 liter water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the shallots, garlic, salacca (snake fruit), and shrimp paste, return to a boil, then add the fish and cook for about 3 minutes. Remove from the heat, add the chiles and mint, and stir. Season with fish sauce and serve.

title: Sour-and-Spicy Sea Bass Curry
ingredients: 1 × 300 g sea bass, cleaned, descaled, and cut into 2 cm-thick pieces
5 slices dried asam gelugor, washed, or 2-3 tablespoons lime juice
200 g heart of palm, cut into 5 cm strips, or cauliflower florets
20 dried red chiles, for the chili paste
1 teaspoon salt, for the chili paste
10 g garlic cloves, for the chili paste
1 × 5 cm piece long turmeric root, for the chili paste
1½ teaspoons shrimp paste, for the chili paste
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.

Pound the chiles, salt, garlic, turmeric, and shrimp paste in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add about 2 tablespoons water and pound with a pestle until smooth. Set aside. Bring the broth (stock) to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the chili paste and boil for another 2 minutes. Add the sea bass, increase the heat to high, and return to a boil without stirring. Reduce the heat to medium and boil for another 2 minutes. Gently remove the fish from the pan and set aside.

Add the asam gelugor, fish sauce, and tamarind to the pan. Reduce the heat to low-medium and simmer for 5-7 minutes until the som khaek fully releases its sourness. Increase the heat back to medium, add the heart of palm or cauliflower, and boil for 2 minutes for the heart of palm or 3 minutes for the cauliflower until softened. Return the fish to the pan and boil for another 1 minute. Serve.

title: Jungle Fish Curry
ingredients: 90 g sliced yard-long beans or green beans, cut into 3 cm lengths
1 ×300 g sea bass or sea bream fillet, cut into 5 cm-thick slices
1 handful sweet basil leaves, plus extra to garnish
2.5 cm piece fresh galangal, peeled and finely chopped
1 teaspoon finely chopped kaffir lime zest
steps: For the chili paste, soak the chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.

Pound the chiles and salt in a mortar with a pestle until the chiles are fine flakes. Add the lemongrass and pound until smooth. Add the galangal and kaffir lime zest and pound thoroughly. Add the black peppercorns, garlic, and shallot and pound again, then add the cilantro (coriander) root and pound until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and pound until thoroughly combined and a smooth paste. Set aside. Bring 250 ml water and the chicken broth (stock) to a boil in a pan over high heat. Add 3 tablespoons of the chili paste, stir, and boil for 2-3 minutes. Add both eggplants (aubergines), the beans and baby corn, then reduce the heat to medium and boil for 3-4 minutes. Add the fish sauce, sugar, fingerroots, and finger chiles and stir a couple times. Gently add the fish and cook for 2-3 minutes, without stirring, until the fish is cooked. Add the basil and stir. Serve garnished with a few basil leaves.

title: Fish Curry in Banana Leaf
ingredients: 300 g Asian knifefish, bronze featherback, or sea bass fillet
50 g kaffir lime leaves, finely sliced
raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumber, Chinese leaves, carrots, and yard-long beans
steps: Before cooking, check that the charcoal is glowing white-hot, or preheat a gas grill (barbecue) to 300°F/150°C.
Bring 475 ml water to a boil in a large pan over high heat. Add the fermented fish sauce, stir, then set aside and keep warm.

Pound half the sliced shallot in a mortar with a pestle. Add the fish and pound until smooth. Gradually pour in the warm fermented-fish water, stirring continuously. Gradually add the ground toasted rice and chili powder and mix well. Add the kaffir lime leaves, cilantro, scallions, and remaining shallot and stir until thoroughly combined.

Lay the banana leaves on a work surface. Put the fish curry in the center and flatten it slightly to make it easy to wrap. Cover with the sides of the leaf, fold over the ends, and secure with toothpicks.
Grill the banana-leaf package over low heat for 10-15 minutes, or until cooked. Unwrap and serve with rice and raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Dry Fish Curry
ingredients: 1 kg whisker sheatfish, red snapper, or red mullet, cleaned and tails removed
950 ml vegetable oil, for deep-frying, plus 60 ml
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles, shallot, garlic, galangal, fingerroot, and lemongrass in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and salt and pound again until thoroughly combined.

Cut each fish crosswise into 3 pieces. Heat the deep-frying oil in a wok or deep fryer to 340°F/170°C and fry the fish for about 7 minutes, until golden brown and crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Heat the remaining 60 ml oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the chili paste and stir-fry for about 3 minutes, until fragrant.
Carefully add 120 ml water, then season with the fish sauce, sugar, and white pepper. Add the fried fish, stir, and cook for another 3-4 minutes. Garnish with the kaffir lime zest and serve.

title: Spicy Dried Fish and Vegetable Curry
ingredients: 50 g dried smoked snakehead fish fillet, broken into small pieces
200 g choy sum (Chinese flowering cabbage), chopped into 5 cm pieces
1 handful of fresh dill, coarsely chopped
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.

Pound the chiles, garlic, salt, and shallots in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Set aside. Bring the broth (stock) and salt to a boil in a pan over high heat. Add the chili paste and boil for 1-2 minutes. Add the dried fish and bail for another 3 minutes or until the fish has softened. Add the yard-long beans, chay sum, and fermented fish sauce and boil for another 4-5 minutes or until the vegetables have softened. Add the dill and stir. Serve.

title: Spicy Fish Ball Curry with Rice Vermicelli
ingredients: 2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
2 dried garcinia or 1 tablespoon Tamarind Puree (see p. 63)
raw or steamed vegetables, such as yard long beans, bean sprouts, shredded lettuce, and cucumbers, to serve
2 tablespoons dried bird's eye chiles, soaked
5-8 dried red chiles, seeded and soaked
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles, salt, lemongrass, galangal. shallots, garlic, and turmeric together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and boiled fish meat and pound 1o a paste.

Heat the coconut milk in a pan over medium- low heat. Add the pounded fish mixture, stir, and bring to a boil. Boil for 3-4 minutes, then add the fish balls and season with the fish sauce, sugar, and dried garcinia or tamarind. Reduce the heat to low, then add the coconut cream and simmer for 3 minutes. Remove from the heat and transfer the curry to a large serving bowl. Place the rice vermicelli on a serving plate and garnish with hard-boiled eggs. Serve with the spicy curry and raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Crab Curry with Betel Leaves
