ingredients: 1½ teaspoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1 red spur chile, seeded and finely sliced lengthwise, to serve
7 large dried red chiles, for the red curry paste
10 dried bird's-eye chiles, for the red curry paste
1 cilantro root, for the red curry paste
1½ tablespoons thinly sliced lemongrass, for the red curry paste
1½ tablespoons thinly sliced galangal, for the red curry paste
4 shallots, chopped, for the red curry paste
5 garlic cloves, for the red curry paste
1½ teaspoons thinly sliced kaffir lime zest, for the red curry paste
½ teaspoon salt, for the red curry paste
½ teaspoon ground white pepper, for the red curry paste
1½ tablespoons roasted ground black pepper, for the red curry paste
1 teaspoon roasted cumin seeds, for the red curry paste
1 teaspoon roasted coriander seeds, for the red curry paste
1 × 3 cm piece fresh turmeric, peeled and chopped, for the red curry paste
½ teaspoon shrimp paste, for the red curry paste
steps: Soak the vermicelli in water for 5 minutes, or according to the package directions. Drain and set aside.

For the red curry paste, soak both kinds of dried chile in warm water for 15 minutes, until rehydrated. Drain and chop. Pound the chiles with the remaining curry-paste ingredients in a mortar until smooth.

Bring a pan of water to a boil. Add the vermicelli and cook for 1-2 minutes. Drain, rinse under cold water, and leave in a sieve to drain completely. Roll the vermicelli into small bundles and arrange them on a serving plate.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Add 3 tablespoons of the curry paste and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
Gradually pour in the coconut milk and bring to a boil. Season with the fish sauce, sugar, and kaffir lime leaves. Add the sliced betel leaves and cook for 1-2 minutes.
Add the crabmeat and stir gently for 1 minute.
Ladle the curry into serving bowls. Place each vermicelli bundle on a betel leaf and top with a cilantro leaf and two strips of chile.

title: Fish Curry with Fermented Rice Noodles
ingredients: 700 g snakehead fish, catfish, or sea bass fillet
300 g finely sliced yard long beans
steps: Put the fish in a steamer and steam for 5-7 minutes or until cooked. Remove from the steamer and remove and discard the skin. Pound the fish and chili paste in a mortar with a pestle until combined. Set aside. Bring the coconut milk to boil in a large pan over medium heat, add the chili paste mixture, and stir until thoroughly combined. Return to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for about 2 minutes. Season with the fish sauce, add the kaffir leaves, and simmer for another 5 minutes or until full-flavored. Remove from the heat and set aside.
Divide the noodles among serving bowls and pour 175 ml of the curry into each bowl. Top with the bean sprouts yard-long beans, lemongrass, and cucumber and serve.

title: Spicy Fish Curry Bites
ingredients: 1 tablespoon finely sliced kaffir lime leaves
1 red spur chile, cut into rings
steps: Put the fish meat, curry paste, fish sauce, and beaten egg in a large bowl and mix well, then while stirring, slowly pour in the coconut milk and stir until smooth.
Pour the mixture into a khanom krok pan or pancake puff pan, sprinkle with the kaffir lime leaves and chiles, then cover with the lids and put the pan over medium heat. Cook for 3-5 minutes. Serve.

title: Red Curry with Clams and Pineapple
ingredients: 500 g live Atlantic surf clams, cleaned, or 300 g clam meat
2 pineapples, peeled, cored, and cut into 2 cm pieces
2 tablespoons finely shredded kaffir lime leaves
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
5 dried bird's-eye chiles, seeded, for the chili paste
4 dried red spur chiles, seeded, for the chili paste
½ teaspoon salt, for the chili paste
3 thin slices galangal, chopped, for the chili paste
2 lemongrass stalks, finely chopped, for the chili paste
2 small shallots, chopped, for the chili paste
2-3 garlic cloves, for the chili paste
1 teaspoon shrimp paste, for the chili paste
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.

Pound the chiles and salt in a mortar with a pestle until fine flakes. Gradually add the galangal, lemongrass, shallots, and garlic and pound until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and pound again until smooth and thoroughly combined. Set aside.

Put the clams in a wok or pan, cover with a lid, then steam over medium heat for 2 minutes or until the clam shells have opened and the clams begin to cook. Discard any clams that are still closed Let cool, then open the clams and remove the meat and set aside. Discard the shells.

Bring half the coconut milk to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add 2 tablespoons of the chili paste, stir, and mix until the chili paste has dissolved and combined with the coconut milk. Boil for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until fragrant and the oil from the coconut milk has separated. Pour in the remaining coconut milk and return to a boil. Add the pineapple and cook for 5-7 minutes or until the pineapple has softened. Add the clam meat, fish sauce, kaffir lime leaves, and sugar, then gently stir and cook for another 2 minutes or until the sugar has dissolved. Serve.

title: Blue Crab and Coconut Milk Curry
ingredients: 2 x 300 g live blue crabs, cleaned
1½ teaspoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
Raw or steamed vegetables, such as sliced cucumber and round eggplants (aubergines), to serve
steps: Put the crabs in the freezer for 20 minutes, then transfer them to a large bowl.

Working with one crab at a time, place it on a cutting board with its back down and legs facing upward. Raise the tail flap and push a small screwdriver or skewer through the hole underneath until it reaches the other side of the shell. Repeat with the second crab.
Remove the aprons and carapaces and rinse the crabs clean. Cut each crab in half vertically, then halve each piece horizontally. Remove and crush the claws.
Bring half the coconut milk to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the chili paste and stir continuously for 2-3 minutes, until fragrant.

Add the crab pieces, claws, and broth and boil for 2 minutes. Add the fish sauce, sugar, and remaining coconut milk, reduce the heat slightly, and boil gently for another 2-3 minutes, until the crab is cooked. Serve with rice and vegetables.

title: Stir-Fried Blue Crab Curry
ingredients: 2 x 300 g live blue crabs, cleaned
6 scallions, diagonally sliced into 4 cm lengths
100 g Chinese celery, cut into 4 cm lengths
steps: Put the crabs in the freezer for 20 minutes. Working with one crab at a time, place it on its back, raise the tail flap, and push a small screwdriver or skewer through the opening until it reaches the other side of the shell.
Remove the aprons and carapaces and rinse the crabs clean. Cut each crab in half vertically, then halve each piece horizontally. Remove and crush the claws.
Blanch the crab pieces and claws in boiling water for 2 minutes, until cooked, then drain.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the garlic and stir-fry for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the crab, increase the heat to medium-high, and stir-fry for 1 minute. Add the egg and stir-fry for about 10 seconds, until cooked.
Add the soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar, curry powder, broth or water, scallions, and celery. Stir-fry for another 1-2 minutes, until thoroughly mixed, and serve.

title: Shrimp and Vegetable Yellow Curry
ingredients: 4 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
2 tablespoons Fried Shallots (see p. 84), to garnish
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
steps: Bring 350 ml coconut milk to a boil in a wok over medium heat. Add the curry paste, stir, and cook for 3-4 minutes or until fragrant and the texture has thickened. Add the fish sauce, sugar, tamarind, tomatoes, onion, 2 tablespoons water and the remaining coconut milk, and return to a boil. Reduce the heat slightly and cook for 2-3 minutes or until the tomatoes and onion have softened. Add the shrimp (prawns) and cook for another 3-4 minutes or until the shrimp are cooked. Add the snow peas (mangetout) and cook for 1 minute. Sprinkle with the fried shallots and serve with rice.

title: Spicy Coconut Milk Curry (Made from Field Crab)
ingredients: 75 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1 kg cooked rice noodles, to serve
1 garlic bulb, cloves separated and chopped
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles, black pepper, garlic, shallots, turmeric, galangal, and lemongrass in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and pound again until smooth.
Pound the field crabs in the mortar to release their juices, then strain through a colander or sieve into a bowl and reserve the liquid.
Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a large pan. Add the chili paste and return to a boil.
Add the crab liquid, tamarind, sugar, and kaffir lime leaves, then season to taste with salt. Serve with the rice noodles.

title: Spicy-and-Sour Curry with Shrimp and Acacia Leaf Omelet
ingredients: 4 tablespoons Kaeng Som Chili Paste (see p. 36)
12 uncooked jumbo shrimp (king prawns), peeled and deveined, with tails still intact
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
For the deep-fried acacia leaf omelet
steps: For the deep-fried acacia leaf omelet, rinse the acacia twigs and pick only the leaves and young stems.
Put the beaten eggs and acacia leaves and stems in a bowl and mix well with a fork.

Heat the oil for deep-frying in a large wok over medium heat. When fully heated, carefully pour in the acacia leaf mixture and cook for about 3 minutes on both sides or until golden brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Cut into 2.5 cm-square pieces and set aside.

Bring the broth (stock) to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the chili paste, and stir until the paste has dissolved. Return to a boil for 2-3 minutes, then season with the fish sauce, tamarind, sugar, and lime juice, if using. Return to a boil then add the acacia leaf omelet and shrimp (prawns). Cook for another 2-3 minutes or until the shrimp are cooked. Remove from the heat and ladle into serving bowls. Serve with rice.

title: Spicy-and-Sweet Curry
ingredients: 200 g raw shrimp, peeled, deveined, and ground
1½ teaspoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
5 dried red spur chiles, for the chili paste
2 tablespoons vegetable oil, for the chili paste
5 garlic cloves, chopped, for the chili paste
5 shallots, chopped, for the chili paste
½ teaspoon salt, for the chili paste
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried spur chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, until rehydrated. Drain, chop, and set aside.
Toast the mung beans in a wok over medium heat for 5-6 minutes, until lightly browned and fragrant. Process them into fine flakes.

Heat the chili-paste oil in a wok over medium heat. Sauté the soaked chiles for 30 seconds, until fragrant and beginning to brown, then drain and set aside. Dry-fry the garlic and shallots for 5-6 minutes, until browned and fragrant.
Pound the sautéed chiles and salt in a mortar until smooth. Add the toasted garlic and shallots and pound again to a smooth paste.

Bring 475 ml coconut milk to a boil in a wok or pan over medium heat. Add the chili paste and sauté for 5-6 minutes, until the coconut oil separates. Add the ground shrimp and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until cooked.

Add the peanuts, mung beans, chicken broth, and remaining coconut milk. Season with the fish sauce, sugar, and tamarind. Reduce the heat and simmer for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beans and peanuts are tender and fully flavored.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Fry the whole bird's-eye chiles for 1-2 minutes, until darkened.
Serve the curry with rice vermicelli and top with the fried chiles.

title: Beef Massaman Curry
ingredients: 500 g brisket or chuck beef, cut into 3 cm cubes
4 potatoes, peeled and cut into 4 cm pieces
1 small sweet potato, peeled and cut into 4 cm pieces
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378) or roti
steps: Bring half the coconut milk and 100 ml water to a boil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the beef and return to a boil, Reduce the heat, cover with a lid, and simmer for 50-60 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the curry paste, and stir for 1-2 minutes or until sizzling and fragrant. Gradually add 150 ml coconut milk and stir for 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and set aside.

After the beef has finished simmering, add the paste, onions, peanuts, bay leaves, fish sauce, sugar, tamarind, cinnamon, cardamom pods, and the rest of the coconut milk and put over low-medium heat for 40 minutes. Add the potatoes and sweet potato, then reduce the heat to low, partly cover, and simmer for another 30-40 minutes or until the beef is tender. Serve with rice or roti.

title: Spicy-and-Sour Curry with Shrimp
ingredients: 200 g young watermelon or round zucchini, sliced into 2 cm-thick pieces
100 g yard-long beans, cut into 2.5 cm pieces
400 g raw shrimp, peeled and deveined with tails intact
4 dried red spur chiles, seeded, for the kaeng som paste
½ teaspoon salt, for the kaeng som paste
3 garlic cloves, for the kaeng som paste
3 shallots, chopped, for the kaeng som paste
1 teaspoon shrimp paste, for the kaeng som paste
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
steps: For the paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, until rehydrated. Drain and pound them with the salt until smooth. Add the garlic and shallots and pound again, then add the shrimp paste and pound until combined.
Bring the broth, 475 ml water, and the paste to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the vegetables and boil for 3 minutes.
Season with the fish sauce, sugar, and tamarind. Add the shrimp and boil for 1-2 minutes, until just cooked.
Adjust with fish sauce, tamarind, and sugar so the curry tastes sweet, sour, and salty. Serve with jasmine rice.

title: Dry Beef Curry
ingredients: 400 g beef shank or rump, cut into bite-size pieces
1 teaspoon ground roasted cumin and coriander seeds
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
1 red spur chile, thinly sliced diagonally
a handful of sweet basil leaves
steps: For the curry paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.

Pound the chiles and salt in a mortar with the pestle until fine flakes form. Add the lemongrass, galangal, kaffir zest, shallots, garlic, cilantro (coriander) root, peppercorns, ground coriander, ground cumin, ground cardamom, and pound again until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and pound until combined Set aside.

Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add 1½ tablespoons curry paste and sauté for 1 minute or until fragrant. Add half the coconut milk, stir, and cook for 1-2 minutes or until the coconut milk thickens. Add the beef and cook for 4-5 minutes or until the beef is cooked. Add the sugar, fish sauce, ground cumin and coriander seeds, and the rest of the coconut milk and stir until combined. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for another 4-5 minutes or until fully flavored. Add a swirl of coconut cream, garnish with the chile, kaffir lime leaves, and basil and serve with rice.

title: Beef and Coconut Milk Curry
ingredients: 5 red spur chiles, sliced diagonally lengthwise
300 g water spinach, finely sliced and blanched
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the curry paste and sauté for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add 250 ml coconut milk and cook for 2-3 minutes, until the mixture thickens and the coconut oil separates and rises to the surface.
Add the beef and stir for about 4 minutes. Add 475 ml water and bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the remaining coconut milk, season with the fish sauce and sugar, and cook for another 5 minutes.
Add the eggplants and chiles, bring to a boil, and cook for 5 minutes. Add the basil, stir, and remove from the heat.
Serve with the rice vermicelli, bean sprouts, water spinach, and hard-boiled eggs.

title: Spicy Beef and Vegetable Curry
ingredients: 300 g chuck beef, thinly sliced into bite-size pieces
steps: For the chile paste, pound the dried chiles, salt, shallots, garlic, lemongrass, galangal, long pepper, Sichuan peppercorns, coriander seeds, and dill seeds in a mortar until smooth.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the chile paste and sauté for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the beef, sliced galangal, lemongrass, and cilantro roots and stir-fry for 2 minutes, until the beef starts to cook.
Add the broth, fermented fish sauce, and fish sauce and simmer for 30 minutes, until the beef is tender.
Add the kaffir lime leaves, dill, skunk-vine tips, chile, and scallions and cook for another 1-2 minutes. Serve.

title: Beef Curry with Noodles
ingredients: 2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
15 g peanuts, roasted and coarsely pounded
100 g extra-firm tofu, cut into small cubes
4 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and sliced
steps: Soak the rice vermicelli in a bowl of water for 10 minutes or according to package directions then drain and set aside.

Meanwhile, for the curry paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop Dry-fry the garlic and ginger in a wok over medium heat for 5 minutes or until fragrant and brown. Set aside.

Pound the drained chiles and salt in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the lemongrass and galangal and continue to pound until thoroughly combined. Add the roasted garlic and ginger and pound until mixed well. Add the shallots and continue to pound, then add the spices and shrimp paste and pound to a smooth paste. Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat, add the curry paste, and saute for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Remove from the heat and set aside. Bring 950 ml water and half the coconut milk to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the beef and return to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 40 minutes.
Add the remaining coconut milk and the broth (stock), and return to a boil. Add the fried chili paste, and season with the salt and sugar. Boil for about 5 minutes, then remove from the heat.

Cook the vermicelli in a pan of boiling water for 2 minutes or until soft. Drain and divide among serving bowls. Add 350 ml of the curried soup and 3-4 slices of beef to each serving bowl. Top with the salted turnips, bean sprouts, peanuts, tofu, fried shallots, and egg. Garnish with the cilantro (coriander) and scallions (spring onions) and serve.

title: Leftover Curry with Noodles
ingredients: 90 g yard-long beans, cut into 3 cm lengths
150 g glass noodles, soaked and cut into 5 cm lengths
steps: For the chile paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles and salt in a mortar. Add the lemongrass, garlic, galangal, and shallot and pound until smooth.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chile paste and sauté for 1 minute, until sizzling and fragrant.
Add the Hunglei curry and cook for 1 minute. Add the pea eggplants and yard-long beans and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the bamboo shoots and cook for 30 seconds. Add the noodles and fish sauce and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the ivy gourd leaves, kaffir lime leaves, cilantro, basil, and sugar and continue stirring for another minute, until thoroughly combined. Serve.

title: Spicy Pork Rib and Mushroom Curry
steps: For the curry paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.

Pound the chiles, shallots, garlic, and shrimp paste in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Set aside. Bring the broth (stock) 475 ml water, and the salt to a boil in a large pan over high heat. Add the ribs and return to a boil. Remove any scum on the surface, Reduce the heat to low, cover the pan, and simmer for 30 minutes or until the ribs are tender.

Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat, add the curry paste, and sauté for 1 minute or until fragrant. Add the paste to the broth, then season with the fish sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar and cook for another 3-4 minutes. Add the acacia leaves, betel leaves, and mushrooms and simmer for 1 minute or until softened. Add the cilantro (coriander), stir, and serve.

title: Hunglei Curry
ingredients: 200 g pork shoulder, cut into 2 cm pieces
250 g pork belly, cut into 2 cm pieces
15 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
4 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and finely julienned
Steamed Jasmine Rice or Glutinous Rice (see p. 378), to serve
1½ teaspoons Hunglei or ordinary curry powder
steps: For the chile paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, then drain and chop.

Pound the chiles and salt in a mortar. Add the galangal and lemongrass and pound thoroughly. Add the garlic and shallots and pound to a paste, then add the shrimp paste and curry powder and pound until combined.
Mix both cuts of pork with the chile paste and pineapple. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.
Heat the oil in a pan or casserole over medium heat. Add the marinated pork and sauté for 3-4 minutes, until fragrant.
Add 600 ml water, increase the heat, and boil for 10 minutes. Add the fish sauce, tamarind puree, sugar, peanuts, ginger, tomatoes, and garlic.
Partly cover, reduce the heat to medium-low, and simmer for 30-35 minutes, until the pork is tender and the liquid has reduced by half. Serve with rice.

title: Fermented Fish and Bamboo Shoot Curry
ingredients: 200 g canned bamboo shoots, cut into 2 cm dice
1½ teaspoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Pound the lemongrass, galangal, shallots fingerroots, garlic, and shrimp paste together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Set aside.

Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the paste and boil for 3-4 minutes or until fragrant. Add the pork side (belly), dried fish, and bamboo shoots, then boil for 5 minutes or until the pork is cooked through. Season with the fermented fish sauce, sugar, and salt and cook for another 2 minutes or until the bamboo shoots are fully flavored. Add the kaffir lime leaves and chopped chile and stir, then serve.

title: Pork and Cow Tree Leaf Curry
ingredients: 1 kg pork shoulder joint with fat, cut into bite-size pieces
225 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
500 g cow tree leaves or tamarind leaves
1 x 7 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped
1 garlic bulb, cloves separated and chopped
steps: Mix the pork, sugar, salt, and soy sauce in a large bowl. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 15 minutes.
For the chili paste, pound all its ingredients together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth.
Heat the oil in a large wok over medium heat. Add the chili paste and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the pork and stir-fry for about 5 minutes, stirring continuously. Pour in the broth, bring to a boil, and boil for 10 minutes.
Reduce the heat to low, add the cow tree leaves, tamarind, and fish sauce, and simmer for 20-30 minutes, until the pork is tender. Serve.

title: Pork Curry with Siam Cardamom Shoots
ingredients: 150 g thinly sliced Siam cardamom shoots or fresh ginger
300 g pork tenderloin or loin steak, thinly sliced
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
steps: Soak the cardamom shoots in a bowl of water for 1-2 minutes, then drain and set aside.

Bring half the coconut milk to a boil in a pan over medium heal. Add the chili paste and stir for 4-5 minutes or until fragrant and the coconut milk has thickened. Add the pork and cardamom shoots or ginger and cook for about 5 minutes or until the pork is cooked. Add the remaining coconut milk and season with the fish sauce, salt, sugar, and kaffir lime leaves. Return to a boil for 3-4 minutes, then serve with rice.

title: Spicy Dry Pork Curry
ingredients: 1½ teaspoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
50 g dried red bird's-eye chiles, for the chili paste
100 g fresh red chiles, chopped, for the chili paste
1 tablespoon black peppercorns, for the chili paste
5-7 lemongrass stalks, chopped, for the chili paste
1 × 4 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped, for the chili paste
3 tablespoons turmeric, for the chili paste
1 garlic bulb, cloves separated and chopped, for the chili paste
2 shallots, chopped, for the chili paste
Zest of 1 kaffir lime, for the chili paste
1-2 teaspoons salt, for the chili paste
1 tablespoon shrimp paste, for the chili paste
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.

Pound the rehydrated and fresh chiles, the peppercorns, lemongrass, galangal, turmeric, garlic, shallots, kaffir lime vest, and salt in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and pound again until thoroughly combined. Set aside.

Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chili paste and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes or until fragrant. Add the pork and stir-fry for about 10 minutes or until dry. Season with the fish sauce and sugar, stir, and add the kaffir lime leaves and green peppercorns. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes. Serve.

title: Roasted Duck Curry
ingredients: ¼ teaspoon ground roasted cumin seeds
½ teaspoon ground roasted coriander seeds
1 red spur chile, diagonally sliced, to garnish
steps: Pound the garlic and cilantro (coriander) root in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the curry paste, pound again until thoroughly combined, and set aside.

Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat, add the paste, and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes or until fragrant. Gradually add 9s 150 ml coconut milk and bring to a boil. Add the pineapple, tomatoes, duck, grapes, and remaining coconut milk and stir. Add both ground seeds, the kaffir lime leaf, and red chile, reduce the heat, and simmer for about 3 minutes, Season with the fish sauce and sugar, add the basil leaves, and stir. Garnish with the sliced red chile and a swirl of coconut cream. Serve.

title: Roasted Duck Curry with Lychee
ingredients: 2½ tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
100 g cubed pineapple, cut into 3 cm cubes
10 lychees or rambutans, peeled and pitted
1 red spur chile, finely sliced, to garnish
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
steps: Put the duck breast in a shallow dish and rub the soy sauce all over the meat, then let marinate for 5-10 minutes.

Preheat the broiler (grill) to high. Place the duck breast on the broiler (grill) rack and broil (grill) for about 7-8 minutes on each side until the skin is brown. Remove and slice the duck into 1 cm thick pieces. Set aside.

Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the curry paste, and sauté for 1-2 minutes until sizzling and fragrant. Pour in the coconut milk, bring to a boil, and boil for 2-3 minutes. Add the duck and broth (stock) and boil for another 3-4 minutes, then add the fish sauce sugar, round and pea eggplants (aubergines), pineapple, kaffir lime leaves, and lychees or rambutans. Boil for another 4-5 minutes, then garnish with basil leaves and the red chile and serve with rice.

title: Chicken Curry with Herbs
ingredients: 700 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into small pieces
½ tablespoon chopped kaffir lime leaves
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the curry paste and sauté for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry for 4-5 minutes. Carefully pour in the water and cook for another 10 minutes, until the chicken is cooked. Season with the salt.
Add the cardamom shoots and pea eggplants and cook for 2 minutes. Add the kaffir lime leaves and both chiles and cook for another 2 minutes.
Fill a small bowl to the rim with steamed rice and invert it in the middle of a serving plate. Serve with the curry.

title: Green Chicken Curry
ingredients: 400 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into 3 cm cubes
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
100 g round eggplants (aubergines), cut into quarters
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over low-medium heat, add the curry paste, and stir-fry for about 2 minutes until sizzling and fragrant. Add the chicken and cook for 1-2 minutes. Pour in half the coconut milk, stir well, then increase the heat to medium and cook for 2-3 minutes. Add the remaining coconut milk, the fish sauce, and sugar and stir again. Add both eggplants (aubergines), then cover the wok and let boil for 4-5 minutes until the eggplants are cooked. Add the basil leaves and chile, stir for 30 seconds, then transfer to a serving bowl. Garnish with basil leaves and sliced chiles and serve with rice.

title: Spicy Chicken Curry
ingredients: 500 g chicken thighs, boned and cut into small pieces
1 x 4 cm piece galangal, peeled and sliced
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
steps: Bring the broth to a boil in a large pan. Add the chili paste and return to a boil for 2-3 minutes.
Add the chicken and boil for another 4-5 minutes.
Add the galangal, fish sauce, sugar, and salt and return to a boil for 5-8 minutes, until the chicken is cooked and fully flavored.
Add the kaffir lime leaves and pennywort or watercress and cook for another minute. Serve with rice.

title: Spicy Chicken Curry and Young Banana
ingredients: Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
20 red and green bird's-eye chiles, chopped
steps: For the chili paste, pound all its ingredients together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth.
Dissolve the salt in the water. Wash the peeled bananas in the salt water, then cut them into 3 cm-thick slices.
Heat the coconut cream in a wok over medium heat. Add the chili paste, chicken, bananas, and coconut milk and simmer for about 10 minutes, until the chicken and bananas are cooked.
Season with the fish sauce and sugar, garnish with the chile and basil, and serve with rice.

title: Chicken and Bitter Gourd Curry Soup with Noodles
steps: Soak the dried noodles in a bowl of water for 10 minutes or prepare according to package directions. Drain and set aside.

Cook the chicken in a pan of boiling water over medium heat for 4-5 minutes or until cooked. Remove with a slotted spoon and shred into bite-size pieces with a fork. Set aside. For the curry soup, bring the broth (stock) to a boil in a large pan over medium heat and add the remaining ingredients except for the bitter gourd and boil for about 5 minutes. Add the bitter gourd, return to a boil, and cook for another 5 minutes. Reduce the heat to low and let simmer for 30 minutes.

Blanch the bean sprouts in a pan of boiling water for 1-2 minutes, then drain, add to the noodles, and divide among serving bowls. Add the shredded chicken, pork blood curd, cilantro (coriander), and scallions (spring onions), then pour the soup into the bowls and serve.

title: Spicy Chicken Curry with Bamboo Shoots
ingredients: 4-5 orange and red spur chiles, chopped
200 g boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-size pieces
1 red spur chile, diagonally sliced, to garnish
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
steps: Pound the chiles and garlic together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the chile-garlic mixture, and saute for 1 minute or until fragrant. Add the chicken and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes or until the chicken is cooked. Add the bamboo shoots and stir-fry for another 1 minute. Season with the fish sauce, sugar, and kaffir lime leaves and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until thoroughly combined, Garnish with the basil leaves and sliced red chile, and serve with rice.

title: Chicken Curry with Yellow Glutinous Rice
prepTime: 15–30 minutes, plus soaking and marinating time
ingredients: 500 g boneless chicken thigh, cut into 4 cm pieces
3 tablespoons Fried Shallots (see p. 64), plus their oil, to garnish
steps: Soak the glutinous rice in water with the turmeric overnight, then drain. Wrap the rice in cheesecloth and steam for 30-35 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until cooked and translucent. Keep covered.
For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Preheat the broiler to medium. Broil the soybean sheet for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant and dark brown, then let cool.
Pound the chiles and salt in a mortar with a pestle. Add the soybean sheet, lemongrass, shallots, garlic, and shrimp paste and pound until smooth.
Mix the chicken with the chili paste, cover, and marinate in the refrigerator for 15-30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chicken and cook for 6-7 minutes, until it begins to brown. Carefully add the water, tomatoes, and salt and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 40-50 minutes, until the chicken is tender and the liquid has reduced by one-third.
Pour the fried shallot oil over the yellow glutinous rice, sprinkle with the fried shallots, and serve with the curry.

title: Green Curry with Silkworm Pupae
ingredients: 2 long eggplants (aubergines), sliced into 2.5 cm pieces
steps: Blanch the silkworm pupae in a pan of boiling water for 1 minute. Drain, transfer to a heatproof bowl, add the fish sauce, and marinate for 10 minutes.
Bring the coconut milk to a boil over medium heat, add the curry paste, and return to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for about 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the pupae and eggplants and return to a boil. Cook for 5-7 minutes. Add the chile, basil, and kaffir lime leaves, stir, and serve.

title: Sour Horse Mango Curry
ingredients: 2 x T 200 g mackerel, sliced into bite-size pieces
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the dried chiles, salt, shallots, and the shrimp paste in a mortar with a pestle until smooth, then set aside.
Dissolve the salt in 475 ml water. Soak the horse mangoes in the salt water for 5 minutes, then drain.

Bring 750 ml water to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the paste, stir, and return to a boil. Add the mackerel and horse mango and cook for 6-8 minutes. Add the sugar and stir until dissolved. Serve.

title: Corn Curry in Banana Leaves
ingredients: 40 g grated fresh coconut or dry unsweetened desiccated coconut
steps: Preheat a charcoal or gas grill to 200°C.
Pound the fingerroot in a mortar. Add the curry paste and pound until smooth, then add the corn, coconut, and salt and pound until the mixture becomes sticky.
Layer the banana leaves back to back with their shiny sides facing outward. Put the curry mixture in the center and flatten it slightly. Fold in the sides and ends and secure with a toothpick.
Grill over low heat for 8 minutes on each side, until cooked. Unwrap and serve.

title: Steamed Mushroom Curry in Banana Leaves
ingredients: 150 g mushrooms, such as white beach, cleaned and stems removed
2 banana leaf sheets, about 8 x 9 inches/20 x 23 cm
steps: Mix the mushrooms, egg, lemongrass, basil leaves, chiles, and shallot together in a bowl. Add the fish sauce and fermented fish sauce and mix again.

Place the 2 banana leaf sheets back to back on a work surface with the shiny surface face outward on both sides. Put the mushroom mixture in the center of the banana leaf sheets and flatten the mixture slightly to make it easy to wrap. Cover the curry with the sides of the sheets, fold over the ends, and secure with a toothpick Steam the banana-leaf package in a steamer over medium heat for 15 minutes or until cooked. Unwrap and serve.

title: Coconut Curry with Wax Gourd and Noodles
ingredients: 300 g wax gourd, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Soak the noodles in water for 10 minutes, or prepare according to package directions, then drain.
Pound the shallots, peppercorns, salt, and shrimp paste in a mortar until smooth.
Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the paste and boil for about 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the wax gourd and sugar and cook for 12 minutes, until the gourd is tender and flavored.
Add the drained noodles and cook for another 1-2 minutes, until soft. Serve.

title: Spicy-and-Sour Curry with Durian and Shrimp
ingredients: 2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
300 g durian flesh, cut into bite-size pieces
200 g uncooked shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails intact
10 fresh red and green bird's-eye chiles
steps: For the curry paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, then drain and chop.
Pound the rehydrated and fresh chiles with the shallots and turmeric until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and salt and pound until combined.
Bring 600 ml water to a boil over medium-high heat. Add the curry paste, sugar, fish sauce, tamarind puree, lime juice, durian, and shrimp.
Return to a boil and cook for 10 minutes. Serve.

title: Durian Massaman Curry
ingredients: 500 g boneless chicken, cut into 5 cm pieces
3 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
Pickled ginger, pickled cucumber, and salad greens, to serve
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop. Pound with the remaining chili paste ingredients in a mortar until smooth.
Dry-fry the peanuts, coriander, tree basil, cloves, cardamom, and cinnamon in a wok for 1 minute, until fragrant. Set aside.
Bring the coconut milk to a simmer in a clean wok over low heat, stirring continuously, until grainy.
Add the chili paste and stir for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant. Add the chicken, roasted spices, fish sauce, bay leaves, tamarind, and sugar and cook for 20-25 minutes.
Add the durian and cook for 5 minutes. Serve with pickled ginger, pickled cucumber, and salad greens.

title: Spicy Taro Stem Curry
ingredients: 1 × 800 g snakehead fish, cleaned and descaled
1 kg fresh taro stems, washed and cut into 5 cm pieces
300 g pork belly, cut into 2.5 cm pieces
2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
25 g ground dried red chiles, for the chili paste
1 × 4 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped, for the chili paste
1 garlic bulb, cloves separated and chopped, for the chili paste
1 shallot, chopped, for the chili paste
40 g chopped fingerroot, for the chili paste
20 g chopped lemongrass, for the chili paste
steps: Preheat the boiler (grill) to medium-high, place the fish on the broiler (grill) rack, and broil (grill) for 10-12 minutes on each side. Remove the meat and discard the skin and bones. Set aside.

For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop. Pound the chiles, galangal, garlic, shallot, fingerroot, and lemongrass in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the grilled fish meat and pound again, then set aside.
Bring a large pan of water to a boil over medium heat. Add the taro stems and boil for 5-7 minutes or until softened. Drain, squeeze to remove any excess liquid, and set aside.

Bring the coconut milk, chili paste, and fermented fish to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the pork and return to a boil. Add the taro stems, reduce the heat, and simmer for 5 minutes or until cooked. Add the fish sauce, sugar, tamarind, and kaffir lime leaves and serve.

title: Spicy Banana Blossom Curry
ingredients: 2 x 400 g mackerel, cleaned, filleted, and sliced into bite-size pieces
steps: For the chilli paste, pound all the ingredients together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth Set aside To clean and prepare banana blossom, pour 475 ml water into a large bowl, add the salt, and stir until dissolved. Peel away and discard the outer red petals from the banana blossom and also the small white strips of banana flower. Cut off the tip and the end of the blossom, then cut the blossom crosswise into thin slices. Put the slices into the bowl of water and let soak for 10 minutes, then drain and set aside.

Bring a large pan of water to a boil over medium heat, add the chili paste and banana blossom, stir, and return to a boil. Add the mackerel, then return to a boil and cook for about 3 minutes. Add the sweet basil leaves and stir. Serve.

title: Sweet Taro Stem Curry
ingredients: 3 taro stems, washed, peeled, and cut into large pieces
steps: Preheat a charcoal or gas grill to 200°C, or preheat an indoor broiler to medium. Grill or broil the pork for 7-8 minutes on each side, until cooked. Slice into bite-size pieces.
Boil the taro stems for 5-7 minutes, until softened. Drain and squeeze out any excess liquid.
Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chili paste and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the pork and season with the sugar, tamarind, fish sauce, and fermented fish sauce. Return to a boil.
Add the taro stems and the acacia leaves, if using. Return to a boil and cook for about 5 minutes. Serve.

title: Grilled Marinated Beef
ingredients: 1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Mix all the ingredients together in a large bowl, cover with plastic wrap (clingfilm), and let marinate in the refrigerator for 1 hour.

Before you begin cooking, check that your charcoal is glowing white hot, or your gas grill (barbecue) is preheated to 400°F/200°C Grill the beef over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side or until cooked. Serve with rice and barbecue sauce.

title: Grilled Squid
ingredients: Seafood Dipping Sauce (see p. 58), to serve
steps: Preheat a charcoal or gas grill to 200°C, or preheat an indoor broiler to high.
Score 3-4 cuts across the squid body without cutting all the way through.
Grill over high heat for 6-7 minutes on each side. If broiling, position the rack about 10 cm from the heat and broil for 6-7 minutes on each side.
Slice the squid into small rings and serve with Seafood Dipping Sauce.

title: Grilled Trevally Fish
ingredients: 1 x 650 g trevally, kingfish, or sea bream, cleaned and descaled
2½ tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
3 red and green bird's-eye chiles, chopped
steps: Prepare a charcoal or gas grill for 350°F/180°C, or preheat an indoor broiler to medium.
For the dipping sauce, bring the tamarind and sugar to a boil in a pan over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Let cool, then add the chiles, shallots, and salt.
Rub the fish with salt and place it in the center of the banana leaf. Fold the sides and ends over the fish and secure with toothpicks.
Grill over medium heat for 7-8 minutes on each side, until cooked. If broiling, position the rack about 10 cm from the heat and broil for 7-8 minutes on each side, turning occasionally.
Unwrap the fish and serve with the dipping sauce.

title: Grilled Tilapia with Spicy Dips
ingredients: 2-3 lemongrass stalks, chopped and lightly pounded
raw vegetables, such as cabbage, lettuce, galangal, ginger, garlic, and round eggplant, to serve
fresh herbs, such as dill and cilantro (coriander), to serve
For the spicy fermented fish dip
2 garlic bulbs, cloves separated and peeled
steps: To make the fermented fish dip, dry-fry the shallots, garlic, galangal, and lemongrass in a wok for 2-3 minutes or until fragrant. Let cool slightly, then peel. Transfer to a mortar, add the chili flakes, and finely pound with a pestle. Add the fermented fish, then pound thoroughly until combined. Set aside.
For the spicy seafood dip, finely pound the chiles, garlic, and salt together in a mortar with a pestle. Add the fish sauce and sugar and stir Set aside.
For the spicy tamarind dip, finely pound the chiles, garlic, and salt together in a mortar with a pestle. Add the tamarind and sugar and stir Set aside.

Before you begin cooking, check that your charcoal is glowing white hot, or your gas grill (barbecue) is preheated to 400°F/200°C. Alternatively, use a conventional indoor broiler (grill) preheated to medium. Stuff the lemongrass into the fish cavity and rub both sides of the fish with the salt.

Grill the fish over medium heat for about 10 minutes on each side or until cooked. If using an indoor broiler, put the broiler (grill) rack 10 cm away from the heat source, then place the fish on the rack and broil (grill) for about 10 minutes on each side or until cooked.
Serve with the spicy dips, vegetables, and fresh herbs.

title: Grilled Snakehead Fish
ingredients: Seafood Dipping Sauce (see p. 58), to serve
Raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumber, napa cabbage, and yard-long beans, to serve
steps: Preheat a charcoal or gas grill to 200°C, or preheat an indoor broiler to medium.
Mix the salt and flour in a bowl.
Stuff the lemongrass into the fish's mouth, then rub the fish all over with the salt mixture.
Grill over medium heat for 15 minutes on each side, until cooked. If broiling, place the fish on a broiler rack and cook over medium heat for 15 minutes on each side.
Serve with seafood dipping sauce and raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Grilled Snakehead Fish in Bamboo
ingredients: 4 cm piece turmeric root, peeled and chopped
2 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped
500 g snakehead fish, cleaned and descaled
Tomato Chili Sauce (see p. 64), Barbecue Sauce (see p. 63), or Seafood Dipping Sauce (see p. 58)
raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumber, napa cabbage, and small bitter gourd
steps: Heat a charcoal or gas grill to 400°F/200°C, or preheat the oven to 325°F/160°C/Gas Mark 3.
Soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, then drain and chop. Pound the chiles, turmeric, galangal, shallots, lemongrass, and salt until smooth. Rub the paste over the whole fish.
Push the basil into the bamboo, followed by the fish. Roast on the grill or in the oven for about 30 minutes, rotating the bamboo regularly.
Remove from the heat, break open the bamboo, and serve with a sauce and raw or steamed vegetables.

title: Catfish and Neem with Sweet Sauce
ingredients: 2 lemongrass stalks, finely sliced and pounded
10-15 dried red chiles, fried, to serve
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
4½ tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Score the fish 2-3 times on each side.
Mix the lemongrass, black pepper, cilantro roots, and soy sauce. Rub the mixture over the fish and inside its cavity.

Prepare a grill for 400°F/200°C. Cook the fish over medium heat for 10-15 minutes on each side. Alternatively, broil it 7 cm from a medium-high heat source for 13-15 minutes on each side, until the skin is dry and brown and the fish is cooked.
For the sauce, combine the sugar, tamarind, fish sauce, salt, and 1-2 tablespoons water in a wok over medium heat. Stir for 4-5 minutes, until thickened, then add the fried shallots.
Blanch the neem in hot water 2-3 times, then drain and refresh in cold water.
Serve portions of neem, fish, fried chile, and sweet sauce together with rice.

title: Grilled Beef with Peppermint Leaves
steps: Put the tenderloin steak (beef fillet) and all the remaining ingredients, except the oil and peppermint leaves, in a large bowl and mix well. Cover with plastic wrap (clingfilm) and let marinate for in the refrigerator for 15 minutes. Brush a grill pan (griddle) with oil and put over medium heat. Add the marinated beef and grill for 4-5 minutes on each side. Let rest for about 2 minutes, then slice into bite-size pieces Garnish with peppermint leaves and serve.

title: Grilled Pork with Black Pepper
ingredients: 500 g pork shoulder, cut into 1 cm pieces
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
Barbecue Sauce (see p. 63) or Seafood Dipping Sauce (see p. 58), to serve
steps: Pound the garlic, peppercorns, and cilantro (coriander) root together in a mortar with a pestle. Transfer to a bowl, add the remaining ingredients, and mix well. Cover with plastic wrap (clingfilm) and let marinate in the refrigerator for 2 hours.

Before you begin cooking, check that your charcoal is glowing white hot, or your gas grill (barbecue) is preheated to 350°F/180°C. Cook the marinated pork over medium heat for 6-7 minutes on each side or until cooked. Alternatively, use a conventional indoor broiler (grill) preheated to medium. Put the broiler (grill) rack 10 cm away from the heat source, then place the pork on the rack, with a tray underneath, and broil (grill) for 6-7 minutes on each side or until cooked. Serve with rice and a sauce on the side.

title: Spicy Thai-Style Sausage
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles and salt in a mortar with a pestle. Add the lemongrass, turmeric, garlic, and shallot and pound until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and pound until thoroughly combined.
Turn the casings inside out and soak in the water mixed with 1½ tablespoons salt for about 10 minutes. Drain and turn right-side out.
Mix the pork and chili paste in a large bowl. Add both cilantro, scallions, kaffir lime leaves, and the remaining teaspoon salt and mix well.
Prepare a grill for 400°F/200°C, or preheat an indoor broiler to medium-high.
Fill the casings with the pork mixture using a sausage funnel, tie both ends, and prick the sausages with a toothpick.
Grill over medium heat for 15-18 minutes on each side, until browned and cooked. If broiling, position the rack 10 cm from the heat and broil for about 15 minutes on each side.
Slice diagonally and serve with glutinous rice.

title: Grilled Pork with Spicy Fish Sauce
ingredients: ½ teaspoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: For the spicy fish sauce, bring the tamarind, sugar, fish sauce, toasted rice, and chili flakes to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Sprinkle with the cilantro (coriander) and transfer to a sauceboat.
Put the sliced pork in a large bowl, add the soy sauce, oil, and oyster sauce, mix, and let marinate in the refrigerator.

Before you begin cooking, check that your charcoal is glowing white hot, or your gas grill (barbecue) is preheated to 400°F/200°C. Grill the pork over medium heat for 4-5 minutes on each side or until cooked. Serve with the spicy fish sauce.

title: Spicy Grilled Pork Brain
ingredients: 2 banana leaves, about 8 x 9 inches/20 x 23 cm
15 dried red bird's eye chiles, chopped
steps: For the chili paste, soak the chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles, shallots, garlic, lemongrass, galangal, turmeric, and salt in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and pound until combined.
Put the chili paste and pork brains in a large bowl and mix until thoroughly combined. Add the sawtooth cilantro (coriander) and scallions (spring onions) and mix again. Set aside.

Lay the 2 banana leaves on a work surface Spoon 100 g of the pork mixture into the center of each leaf, wrap into a square shape, and secure with a bamboo pin or toothpick. Before you begin cooking, check that your charcoal is glowing white hot, or your gas grill! (barbecue) is preheated to 325°F/160°C. Grill the package over low heat for 30-40 minutes turning occasionally to prevent it from burning Unwrap and serve.

title: Grilled Chicken
prepTime: 2 hours, plus marinating and standing time
ingredients: 1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Mix the garlic, salt, black pepper, sugar, and soy sauce in a large bowl. Add the chicken and massage with the seasoning. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 2 hours, or for at least 30 minutes.

Bring the chicken to room temperature for 30 minutes. Heat a charcoal grill until white hot or preheat a gas grill to 300°F/150°C. Grill over low-medium heat for about 20 minutes on each side, or until cooked.
Alternatively, preheat an indoor broiler to low-medium, place the rack about 10 cm from the heat with a tray underneath, and broil the chicken for about 20 minutes on each side. Serve with rice.

title: Spicy Grilled Pork Salad
ingredients: 400 g pork loin, about 1 cm thick
steps: Preheat a charcoal or gas grill to 200°C, or preheat an indoor broiler to medium.
Grill or broil the pork for 7-8 minutes on each side, until cooked. Slice it into bite-size pieces and arrange on a serving plate.
Mix the fish sauce, lime juice, chili flakes, and ground toasted rice in a bowl. Add the shallot, scallions, and sawtooth cilantro and mix thoroughly.
Spoon the dressing over the pork and serve.

title: Duck with Tamarind Sauce
ingredients: 2 cups (16 fl oz/475 mil) vegetable oil
3 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the kale leaves, and fry for 1 minute or until the kale starts to become crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Put the duck, soy sauce, white pepper, and five-spice powder in a bowl and mix well. Cover with plastic wrap (clingfilm) and let marinate in the refrigerator for 20 minutes. Preheat a grill pan (griddle) over high heat. Place the duck, skin side down, in the pan, then reduce the heat to low and grill for 7 minutes or until brown and crispy. Turn over and grill for 10 minutes. Remove and set aside.
For the sauce, heat the sugar, tamarind, soy sauce, and 1 tablespoon water together in a pan over medium-low heat. Cook for 5-6 minutes or until thickened. Set aside.

Carve the duck breast into 1 cm-thick pieces and place on a serving plate with the pieces overlapping in a fan shape. Put the crispy kale to one side of the duck and pour over the sauce. Sprinkle with the fried garlic, fried shallots, roasted chile, and cilantro (coriander) leaves and serve.

title: Grilled Pork Salad
ingredients: 400 g skinless pork neck, fillet, or shoulder
10 dried red chiles, seeded and chopped
Raw vegetables, such as carrots, cucumbers, and Chinese greens, to serve
steps: Preheat a charcoal or gas grill to 160°C, or preheat an indoor broiler to medium-low.
Rub the soy sauce over the pork, cover, and marinate for 15 minutes.
Grill the pork over medium-low heat for 15-20 minutes on each side, until browned and cooked. If broiling, position the rack about 10 cm from the heat and broil for 15-20 minutes on each side.
Shred the cooked pork with a fork, then pound it briefly in a mortar.
Transfer the pork to a bowl. Add the garlic, shallots, lemongrass, chiles, lemon juice, and fish sauce and mix well.
Serve with glutinous rice and raw vegetables.

title: Stewed Pork Side
ingredients: 500 g pork side (belly), cut into 5 cm cubes
120 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
475 ml water, plus more if needed
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
steps: Heat the oil in a pan or casserole over medium heat. Add the saam-gler and sauté for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook for about 4 minutes, until golden brown.
Add the water, sugar, both soy sauces, five-spice powder, and black pepper. Mix well and return to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the eggs and partially cover with a lid. Simmer for 1 hour, until the pork is tender, stirring occasionally and adding water if needed to prevent the meat from drying out. Serve with rice.

title: Stewed Pork with Peanuts and Dried Bamboo Shoots
ingredients: 1 kg pork side (belly), diced with the fat
200 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1 medium garlic bulb, cloves separated and chopped
1 x 12.5 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped
steps: Soak the bamboo shoots in water for 15 minutes, then drain. Cut into 7.5 cm segments.
Cook the peanuts in boiling water for about 5 minutes, until soft, then drain.
For the chili paste, pound all its ingredients together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chili paste and stir-fry for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the pork, peanuts, bamboo shoots, sugar, and fish sauce and stir-fry for 5-6 minutes, until cooked. Serve.

title: Steamed Sea Bass with Spicy Lime Sauce
ingredients: 1 × 800 g whole sea bass, cleaned and filleted
3-4 red and green bird's-eye chiles, chopped, for the sauce
4 garlic cloves, chopped, for the sauce
1½ teaspoons chopped cilantro root, for the sauce
60 ml chicken broth, for the sauce
3 tablespoons fish sauce, for the sauce
2 tablespoons lime juice, for the sauce
1 tablespoon granulated sugar, for the sauce
1 small handful cilantro sprigs, to garnish
3 red bird's-eye chiles, sliced, to garnish
steps: For the sauce, pound the chiles, garlic, and cilantro (coriander) root in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Transfer to a bowl. Add the chicken broth (stock), fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and 60 ml water and stir until thoroughly combined. Place one of the fillets, skin side down, in a deep plate. Cover with the galangal and half the lemongrass, then put the remaining fillet on top, skin side up. Arrange the kaffir lime leaves and the remaining lemongrass around the fillets. Steam in a steamer for 5-7 minutes, then pour over the sauce and steam for another 5 minutes or until the fish is cooked through. Transfer to a shallow serving bowl. Garnish with sliced lime, cilantro (coriander) sprigs, and chile and serve.

title: Steamed Tilapia with Spicy Tomato Dip
ingredients: 2-3 lemongrass stalks, chopped and lightly pounded
10 kaffir lime leaves, plus a few extra
Raw vegetables, such as cabbage, snake gourd, and napa cabbage, to serve
Vegetable hummingbird and Chinese mustard flowers, coarsely chopped, to serve
steps: For the dip, roast the tomato, chiles, and shallots in a dry skillet over low heat for 2-3 minutes, until fragrant.
Lightly pound the chiles and shallots in a mortar. Add the tomato and pound again, then mix in the salt and tamarind puree. Sprinkle with cilantro.
Score the tilapia 2-3 times on both sides. Stuff the lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves into the cavity.
Season both sides generously with sea salt and tuck a few extra kaffir lime leaves into the score marks.
Steam the fish for about 20 minutes. In a separate steamer, steam the vegetables and flowers for about 10 minutes.
Serve the fish with the vegetables, flowers, and spicy tomato dip.

title: Steamed Catfish in Banana Leaf
ingredients: Banana leaves, cut into circles about 20 cm in diameter
250 g snakehead fish fillet, cut into 2.5 cm cubes
15 g finely sliced kaffir lime leaves
15 g finely sliced great morinda leaves or sweet basil leaves
1 red spur chile, finely sliced lengthwise, to garnish
steps: For each cup, place 2 banana-leaf circles back to back, shiny sides facing outward. Fold up a 5 cm section and fold it in on itself to form a corner; secure with a toothpick. Repeat to make 4 corners.
Whisk the coconut cream and curry paste in a large bowl until the paste dissolves. Add the eggs, oyster sauce, fish sauce, and sugar and whisk until combined.
Add the fish, kaffir lime leaves, and morinda or basil leaves and mix gently.
Fill the banana cups with the mixture, making sure each contains at least 4-5 pieces of fish.
Steam over medium-high heat for 20-25 minutes, until the mixture has set and feels firm. Garnish each cup with red chile and serve.

title: Steamed Fish with Pumpkin and Herbs
ingredients: 2 lemongrass stalks, halved crosswise and crushed
200 g pumpkin wedge, cut into 3-4 pieces
1 handful basil or Greek basil, to garnish
Spicy Tomato Dip (see p. 54) or Seafood Dipping Sauce (see p. 58), to serve
steps: Rinse the fish in cold water, pat dry with paper towels, then rub the whole fish with the salt and set aside, Coarsely pound the shallots, garlic, black peppercorns, and cilantro (coriander) root together in a mortar with a pestle. Add the soy sauce and stuff the mixture inside the fish cavity. Put the lemongrass and galangal in the center of a large heatproof plate, then place the fish on the top. Arrange the pumpkin around the fish and steam in a steamer for about 15 minutes or until the fish is cooked. Garnish with the basil and serve with rice and spicy tomato dip or seafood sauce.

title: Steamed Egg with Shrimp and Coconut Milk
ingredients: 1 tablespoon salted tiny freshwater shrimp or 1½ teaspoons shrimp paste mixed with 1 tablespoon water
red and green bird's eye chiles, sliced, to garnish
steps: Beat the eggs and coconut milk in a large bowl, then add the shrimp and shallot and beat again until thoroughly combined. Let sit for about 2 minutes to let the air bubbles dissipate. Pour the mixture into small heatproof cups and steam in a steamer over medium heat for 15-20 minutes or until cooked. To see if the eggs are cooked, push a skewer through the center-only clear water should come out. Sprinkle with the chiles and serve.

title: Steamed Egg with Shrimp and Mushrooms
steps: Soak the mushrooms in a bowl of boiling water for 15 minutes, then drain, slice, and set aside. Pour the broth (stock) or water into a large bowl, add the eggs, mushrooms, shrimp, fish sauce, and soy sauce, and beat until thoroughly combined. Let sit for about 2 minutes to let the air bubbles dissipate.

Pour the mixture into a small heatproof bowl and steam in a steamer over medium heat for 15-20 minutes or until cooked. To see if the eggs are cooked, push a skewer through the center-only clear water should come out. Serve sprinkled with the carrot, onion, and scallion (spring onion).

title: Stuffed Mangrove Trumpet Tree Flowers
ingredients: 4 lemongrass stalks, sliced 50 g bird's eye chiles
500 g clown featherback or flounder fillet, finely chopped
30 g kaffir lime leaves, finely sliced, plus whole ones to garnish
20 mangrove trumpet tree flowers or zucchini (courgette) flowers
steps: Put the glutinous (sticky) rice in a large bowl, add 120 ml water, and let soak for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Drain and reserve the rice water.

Pound the lemongrass, chiles, salt, and glutinous rice water in a mortar with a pestle. Add the fish, pork, and fermented fish sauce and pound thoroughly. Add the dill and kaffir lime leaves, then pound again until smooth. Spoon the paste into the flowers and place on cheesecloth (muslin) in a steamer. Steam for about 30 minutes. Serve garnished with kaffir lime leaves.

title: Stuffed Squid with Garlic and Pepper
ingredients: 400 g small squid, cleaned, with tentacles intact
steps: Mix the ground (minced) pork with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, the salt, sugar, and 1½ teaspoons Saam-Gler in a large bowl until thoroughly combined. Stuff the squid with the pork mixture until three-quarters full. Thread the sides of the squid together, using a toothpick or skewer. Steam the stuffed squid in a steamer over medium heat for 10-12 minutes or until cooked. Remove and set aside.

Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the remaining saam-gler, and stir-fry for 1 minute or until fragrant. Add the steamed squid and remaining soy sauce, then stir-fry for another 1-2 minutes or until the squid is well coated with the saam-gler. Serve sprinkled with the cilantro (coriander).

title: Steamed Pork Patties with Salted Egg
steps: Finely pound the cilantro (coriander) root, garlic, and white peppercorns together in a mortar with a pestle. Put the ground (minced) pork, salted egg whites, soy sauce, sesame oil, and the cilantro root paste in a large bowl and mix well. Mold the pork mixture into flat round patties, 10 cm in diameter. Lightly press a piece of salted egg yolk into the center of each patty. Arrange the patties in a shallow dish and steam in a steamer for 15-20 minutes over medium heat until cooked. Serve.

title: Sweet Boiled Mackerel
ingredients: 5-7.5 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and pounded
2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Bring a large pan of water to a boil, then add all the ingredients, reduce the heat to low, and simmer for 20 minutes. Serve hot or cold.

title: Bilimbi with Dipping Sauce
ingredients: 80 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: For the dipping sauce, put the shrimp paste, sugar, and 120 ml water in a pan over medium heat, stir, and cook for 3-4 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool. Add the chiles and shallots, stir well, then transfer to a small serving bowl.
Arrange the sliced bilimbi on a serving plate and serve with the dipping sauce on the side.

title: Slow-Cooked Mackerel
ingredients: 2.5 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped
10 cm piece sugar cane, quartered lengthwise
300 g pork side (belly), cut into 1 cm dice
1 kg horse mackerel, cleaned and heads removed
Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
steps: Put the galangal, lemongrass, and half the sugar cane in a large, deep pan. Place the pork and mackerel on top and add enough water to cover the fish. Do not stir from this point.

Pound the shallot, garlic, and salt and add to the pan with the sugar, fish sauce, and soy sauce. Put the remaining sugar cane on top of the fish and bring to a boil over medium heat. Cook for 30 minutes and skim.

Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 3-4 hours, or until the fish is cooked and its bones have softened. Add more water if the liquid dries out and stir gently only if necessary. Serve with rice.

title: Sweet Boiled Shrimp
ingredients: Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve
steps: Bring 120 ml water to a boil in a large pan, add the shrimp (prawns), sugar, and salt, and mix well. Reduce the heat and simmer for 7-8 minutes or until the water has evaporated. Let cool, then serve with the rice.

title: Pork and Herb Meatballs
ingredients: 1 x 2 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and finely chopped
steps: Combine the pork, tomatoes, shallots, both cilantro, garlic, ginger, lemongrass, scallions, turmeric, and salt in a large bowl.
With damp hands, roll the mixture into 5 cm-diameter balls.
Heat a layer of oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Sauté the meatballs in batches for 6-7 minutes, until well browned all over.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve with glutinous rice.

title: Sea Snails with Dipping Sauce
ingredients: 1 kg dog conch or wing shell sea snails, shells intact and cleaned
Seafood Dipping Sauce (see p. 58), to serve
steps: Mix the water, vinegar, and chiles in a large bowl. Add the snails, soak for about 15 minutes, then drain.
Bring a large pan of water to a boil over medium heat. Add the snails and boil for about 2 minutes, until cooked.
Drain and serve with the seafood dipping sauce.

title: Squid with Lime
ingredients: 10-15 red and green bird's-eye chiles, chopped
2 squid, about 12.5 cm long, cleaned and cut into 5 mm rings
steps: Pound the garlic and chiles together in a mortar with a pestle. Add the fish sauce and lime juice and mix until combined.
Bring 250 ml water to a boil in a pan, add the squid, and cook for 5 minutes. Add the garlic paste, celery leaves, and cilantro (coriander) and cook for another 2 minutes, then serve.

title: Boiled Chicken with Herbs
ingredients: 1 x 1.3 kg chicken, chopped into pieces
1 x 7 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and chopped
steps: For the paste, pound the galangal, lemongrass, shallots, ginger, cilantro roots, garlic, kaffir lime leaves, salt, black pepper, and soy sauce in a mortar with a pestle until smooth.
Coat the chicken thoroughly with the paste, then place it in a large pan or in the top of a double boiler.

Bring 2-3 liters water to a boil in a slightly larger pan or in the bottom of the double boiler. Place the pan containing the chicken above it, cover, and steam for 1 hour, until the chicken is cooked.
Transfer to a serving plate, sprinkle with the cilantro leaves and sweet basil, and serve.

title: Spiced Ivy Gourd and Egg
ingredients: 200 g ivy gourd leaves or Chinese kale
steps: Soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop. Pound the chiles, shallots, and shrimp paste in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Bring 250 ml water to a boil in a pan over medium heat, add the chili paste and return to a boil. Add the ivy gourd leaves, reduce the heat, and simmer for 1-2 minutes Break the eggs into the mixture and beat with a fork. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat. Season with the fish sauce and serve.

title: Pumpkin in Coconut Milk
ingredients: 1 kg Thai pumpkin, peeled and seeded
225 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Cut the pumpkin into 1 x 2.5 cm sticks, rinse under cold running water, and set aside.
Bring the coconut milk and pumpkin sticks to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for about 10 minutes, until the pumpkin has softened.
Add both sugars and the salt and return to a boil. Add the coconut cream, bring back to a boil, then remove from the heat and serve.

title: Water Spinach with Shrimp and Tofu
ingredients: 150 g extra-firm tofu, cut into cubes
8 raw freshwater shrimp, heads and tails intact
3-5 dried red chiles, finely pounded, for the sauce
2 garlic cloves, finely pounded, for the sauce
3 tablespoons white vinegar, for the sauce
3 tablespoons granulated sugar, for the sauce
3 tablespoons fish sauce, for the sauce
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Stir-fry the tofu for 5-7 minutes, until golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Add the shrimp to the wok and stir-fry for about 2 minutes, until pink. Remove and set aside.
Put all the sauce ingredients in a pan over medium heat and simmer until thick.
Blanch the water spinach in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain.
Arrange the cucumber on a serving plate and cover with the water spinach. Drizzle with the sauce and sprinkle with the sesame seeds, peanuts, and fried garlic. Top with the tofu and shrimp and serve.

title: Fried Mackerel with Spicy Shrimp Dip
ingredients: Lettuce, wilted spinach, bok choy, or other leafy greens, to serve
2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
Red bird's-eye chiles, seeded, to garnish
4-8 pea eggplants, broiled whole, to garnish
steps: For the dip, pound the chiles and garlic in a mortar until smooth. Add the sugar, shrimp paste, and fish sauce and pound until combined.
Mix in the dried shrimp and lime juice. Transfer to a serving bowl and garnish with the red chiles and pea eggplants.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Fry the mackerel until browned and the skin is crisp, turning to cook both sides.
Drain, transfer to a plate, and serve with the spicy shrimp dip and leafy greens.

title: Spicy Gourami Salad
ingredients: 3 gourami, filleted and each cut into 3 pieces
5 red and green bird's eye chiles, chopped
2 cilantro (coriander) sprigs, leaves only, to garnish
steps: Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the fish for 8-10 minutes or until golden and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Mix the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, chiles, and shallots together in a bowl until the sugar has dissolved. Add the deep-fried fish and mix well. Serve garnished with the cilantro (coriander).

title: Fried Sea Bass
ingredients: 80 g green sour mango, peeled and julienned
1 × 500 g whole sea bass or red snapper, cleaned and descaled
4-5 red and green bird's-eye chiles, chopped
1 tablespoon fish sauce, for the topping
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar, for the topping
steps: Put the mango, carrot, shallots, fish sauce lime juice, and superfine (caster) sugar in a large bowl and mix well. Set aside.

Butterfly the fish by cutting the fish lengthwise down the middle to the backbone, without cutting all the way through, then open out to create a butterfly fillet, leaving the head and bones intact. Pat dry with paper towels.

Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the sea bass for 15 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Set aside 1 tablespoon of the oil.
For the fish topping, put the fish sauce and sugar in a small bowl and mix until the sugar has dissolved.

Heat the reserved oil in a wok over medium heat, add the fish sauce and palm sugar mixture, and heat for 1 minute or until it starts sizzling. Pour the sizzling mixture over the fish and top with the mango and carrot. Serve.

title: Spicy Fried Sea Bass
ingredients: 1 x 800 g whole sea bass, cleaned and descaled
1 liter vegetable oil, for deep-frying, plus 2 tablespoons
steps: Place the fish on a cutting board and score it 2-3 times on both sides with a sharp knife. Set aside.

Heat the deep-frying oil in a large wok or deep fryer to 180°C. Deep-fry the sea bass for 10-12 minutes on each side, until golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and set aside.
Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons oil in the same wok over medium heat. Add the garlic, chiles, sugar, fish sauce, and 1 tablespoon water. Stir-fry for 1 minute, until the sugar has dissolved.
Spoon the sauce into a bowl and serve with the fried sea bass.

title: Deep-Fried Sea Bass on Betel Leaves
ingredients: 1 x 400 g whole sea bass, cleaned and filleted, skin on and bones reserved
3 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
4 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and diced
steps: Cut the sea bass fillets into 2 cm cubes. Toss the cubes with the flour, then coat the reserved fish bones with the remaining flour.
Heat the oil to 180°C. Deep-fry the fish cubes for 3-4 minutes, until golden, then drain on paper towels.
Deep-fry the fish bones for 3 minutes on each side, until golden and crisp, then drain.
For the sauce, stir the fish sauce and sugar in a small pan over low-medium heat for 2-3 minutes, until the sugar dissolves. Let cool.
Mix the peanuts, ginger, lime, shallot, chiles, lemongrass, and sauce in a bowl.
Arrange the fried bones on a serving plate and place the fish cubes on top. Spoon over the peanut mixture and sprinkle with fried shallots.
To serve, wrap bite-size portions in betel leaves and eat whole.

title: Fried Sea Bass with Three-Flavored Sauce
ingredients: 1 x 800 g sea bass or sea bream, cleaned and descaled
3 red spur chiles, seeded and finely pounded
50 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
3 bell peppers, 1 each red, green, and orange, halved, seeded, and diced, to garnish
1 red chile, sliced into oval shapes, to garnish
steps: Place the fish on a cutting board. Using a sharp knife, score it 2-3 times on both sides. Sprinkle the flour over both sides and set aside.

Heat the oil for deep-frying to 180°C, or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the fish for 10-12 minutes on each side, until golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and set aside.
Put 2 tablespoons of the frying oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and pounded chiles and sauté for about 30 seconds, or until fragrant.

Stir in the chicken broth and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat, add the sugar, tamarind, fish sauce, and salt, and simmer for 3-4 minutes, until reduced and beginning to caramelize. Stir in the basil leaves.
Place the fish on a serving plate, pour over the sauce, garnish with the diced bell peppers and sliced chile, and serve.

title: Fried Sheatfish with Garlic and Peppercorns
ingredients: 1 × 500 g sheatfish, cleaned, head removed, and cut into 1 cm-thick slices
steps: Pound the unpeeled garlic in a mortar with a pestle, then set aside. Put the peppercorns, salt, and fish slices in a bowl, mix well, and set aside.

Heat the oil for deep-frying in a large wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the fish for 8-10 minutes, then remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Deep-fry the pounded garlic in the wok for 1 minute or until golden, then remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. To serve, crumble the deep-fried garlic over the fish.

title: Deep-Fried Sea Bass with Chili Sauce
ingredients: 1 x 800 g sea bass, cleaned and descaled
2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Place the fish on a cutting board and score it 2-3 times on both sides with a sharp knife. Season with the black pepper and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wok or deep fryer to 180°C. Deep-fry the fish for 10-12 minutes, until golden brown and crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Bring the broth to a boil in a pan. Add the sugar and salt and stir, then add the chiles and garlic and cook for 3 minutes. Season with the lime juice.
Place the fish on a serving plate, pour over the sauce, garnish with the cilantro, and serve.

title: Fried Whisker Sheatfish in Garlic and Pepper
ingredients: 4 whisker sheatfish, cleaned and tails removed
1 garlic bulb, cloves separated and coarsely pounded
steps: Place the fish on a cutting (chopping) board, and using a sharp knife, score each fish 2-3 times on both sides.
Put the soy sauce and black pepper into a shallow dish, add the fish, and coat in the mixture.

Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the coated fish for 8-10 minutes or until golden brown, then remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.

Deep-fry the garlic for 1 minute or until golden brown and crispy, then remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Place the fish on a serving plate, sprinkle with the deep-fried garlic, and serve.

title: Deep-Fried Tilapia with Vegetables
ingredients: 1 x 800 g tilapia, cleaned and descaled
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1 tablespoon finely sliced kaffir lime leaves
1 tablespoon black and white sesame seeds
80 g roasted chile paste (Nam Prik Pao)
steps: Score the fish 2-3 times on both sides.
Heat the oil to 180°C. Deep-fry the fish for 12-15 minutes on each side, until golden and crisp, then drain on paper towels.
For the sauce, mix the tamarind puree, sugar, chiles, chili jam, and fish sauce in a large bowl.
Add the mango, carrot, peppercorns, kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, betel leaf, shallots, sesame seeds, and roasted chile paste and mix until combined.
Place the fish on a serving plate, pour over the sauce, and serve.

title: Fried Snakehead Fish
prepTime: 20 minutes, plus marinating and drying time
ingredients: Tomato Chili Sauce (see p. 84), to serve
steps: Butterfly each fish by cutting lengthwise down the middle to the backbone without cutting all the way through. Open it into a butterfly fillet, leaving the head and bones intact, and pat dry with paper towels.
Rub the fish with the salt. Place on a large plate, cover, and marinate in the refrigerator for 2-3 hours.
Rinse thoroughly, drain, wrap in cheesecloth, and sun-dry for 1-2 hours. Alternatively, heat the oven to 60°C and dry the fish for 1½-2 hours.
Heat the oil in a deep, heavy pan or deep fryer to 180°C. Cut the fish into pieces and deep-fry for 10-15 minutes, until golden.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and serve with glutinous rice and tomato chili sauce.

title: Fish Cakes
ingredients: 300 g skinless spotted featherback, cod, or salmon fillets, ground (minced)
½ tablespoon Red Curry Paste (see p. 38)
1 tablespoon thinly sliced kaffir lime leaves
steps: Mix the fish and curry paste together by hand in a bowl until thoroughly combined.
Add the egg, sugar, fish sauce, cornstarch, and salt and mix well. Add the beans and kaffir lime leaves and continue mixing until the mixture is firm and sticky.
Cover and chill in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.
Dampen your hands and shape the mixture into 20-25 round cakes, about 5 cm in diameter and 7-8 mm thick.
Heat the oil in a wok or deep fryer to 180°C. Deep-fry the fish cakes in batches for 3-4 minutes, until golden brown.
