Strain through cheesecloth into a bowl, reserving the broth. Separate the fish meat and set aside.
Pound the cooked chiles, garlic, galangal, lemongrass, fingerroot, and shallots together in a mortar. Add the fish meat and pound until combined.
Return the broth to the pan and bring to a boil over medium heat. Add the pounded paste, fish sauce, sugar, and fish balls and boil for 2-3 minutes.
Add the scallions and cook for about 2 minutes, then remove from the heat.
Divide the noodles and fish balls among serving bowls and pour over the broth. Top with the bean sprouts, basil, yard-long beans, water mimosa, chile flakes, and eggs.

title: Fried Noodles
ingredients: 300 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1 kg blue crabs, stir-fried and cut into small pieces (see p. 338)
500 g uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined
2 garlic bulbs, cloves separated and chopped
200 g chopped Chinese chives, to serve
1½ cucumbers, peeled and sliced lengthwise into chunks, to serve
steps: Soak the noodles in water for 10 minutes, or according to the package directions, until soft. Drain, rinse, and set aside.
For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in hot water for 15 minutes, until rehydrated. Drain and chop.
Pound the chiles, shallots, garlic, and salt together in a mortar until smooth.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chili paste and stir-fry for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the tamarind and sugar and simmer for about 3 minutes, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Add the crab pieces and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the shrimp, noodles, and a few snipped chives. Reduce the heat to low and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Serve with the remaining chives, cucumber, and bean sprouts.

title: Stewed Beef Noodles
ingredients: 1 tablespoon sliced Chinese celery (cut into 1-inch 2.5 cm slices)
2 kg beef sirloin, cut into 3 cm pieces
steps: Soak the noodles in a bowl of water for 10 minutes, or according to package directions, until soft, then drain, rinse, and set aside. To make the beef broth (stock), bring 2 liters water to a boil in a large pan. Add all the ingredients and return to a boil. Use a slotted spoon to remove any scum. Cover with a lid, reduce the heat to low, and simmer for 1-2 hours until the beef is tender. Remove the beef from the pan and set aside Blanch the rice noodles and bean sprouts in a pan of boiling water for 1 minute, then drain and divide among serving bowls. Add the lettuce, Chinese celery, scallions (spring onions), cilantro (coriander), and 50 g stewed beef. Add 1 ladleful of beef broth to each bowl and serve.

title: Rice Noodles with Pork and Gravy
ingredients: 250 g pork tenderloin or shoulder, thinly sliced
200 g Chinese broccoli, cut into 2-inch 5 cm-long pieces
steps: Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the rice noodles and dark soy sauce and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until the noodles have softened. Remove from the wok and set aside.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in the wok over medium-high heat, add the garlic, and quickly stir-fry for 1 minute or until fragrant. Add the pork and stir-fry for 1 minute. Add the broth (stock) and bring to a boil. Season with the soy sauce, salt, sugar, and salted soybeans and return to a boil. Dissolve the tapioca flour in 50 ml water and slowly add to the wok, stirring continuously, until the mixture has thickened into a gravy. Add the broccoli and cook for about 2 minutes or until the broccoli is tender.
Transfer the noodles to a deep serving plate or bowl and pour the gravy, pork, and vegetables over the noodles. Serve.

title: Rice Noodles with Shredded Chicken
ingredients: 2 skinless, boneless chicken breasts, cut in half lengthwise
1 kg fresh rice noodles or 400 g dried rice noodles
1 bunch of cilantro (coriander), half the stems removed
steps: Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the chicken and salt, reduce the heat to low-medium, and simmer for 10 minutes. Remove from the heat and let the chicken cool in the pan for 10 minutes. Remove the chicken with a slotted spoon and transfer to a cutting (chopping) board. Use a fork to shred the chicken, then return to the pan and set aside. Cook the noodles according to the package directions, If using dried noodles, first soak them in a bowl of water for 10 minutes, or according to package directions, until soft. Drain and rinse under cold water, then leave in the strainer (sieve) to drain completely. Use your hand or a fork to roll the vermicelli into small rolls and place on a serving plate To serve, divide the rolls of noodles among serving plates and top with 2-3 tablespoons of the chili jam and 3-4 tablespoons of the chicken and coconut milk. Serve with the cilantro (coriander), cucumber slices, and lettuce leaves.

title: Fried Rice Noodles with Chicken
ingredients: 200 g skinless, boneless chicken breast, sliced
1 tablespoon finely chopped sweet preserved turnip
steps: Put the chicken, ground white pepper, sesame oil, and 1 teaspoon soy sauce in a bowl, mix well, and let stand for 10~15 minutes.

Separate the strips of noodles from each other. If the noodles have been kept in the refrigerator, wrap them in cheesecloth (muslin) and steam in a steamer for 2-3 minutes until warmed through. Alternatively, heat in a microwave for 1 minute. Set aside.

Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a wok over low- medium heat, add the garlic and preserved turnip, and stir-fry for 10 seconds or until fragrant. Add the chicken, increase the heat to medium, and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until cooked. Add the noodles and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, then season with 2 teaspoons soy sauce, the oyster sauce, and sugar. Stir until combined, then move to one side of the wok.

Add 1 tablespoon oil, break in the eggs, and let the egg whites become lightly cooked before scrambling. When the eggs are cooked halfway, mix with the noodles and stir-fry for about 1 minute or until the eggs are fully cooked. Add the bean sprouts and stir-fry for 20 seconds. Remove from the heat Let cool for 1 minute, then add the lettuce and scallions (spring onions) and stir. Serve.

title: Rice Vermicelli with Pineapple and Coconut Milk
ingredients: 1 kg fresh rice vermicelli or 400 g dried rice vermicelli
10 red and green bird's-eye chiles, chopped
25 g chopped fresh ginger, to serve
10 cloves garlic, thinly sliced, to serve
steps: Cook the vermicelli according to the package directions. If using dried vermicelli, first soak it in water for 10 minutes, until soft. Drain, rinse under cold water, and leave in a strainer to drain completely.
Process the dried shrimp in a food processor into fine flakes and set aside.
For the chili sauce, combine the chiles, fish sauce, and lime slices in a small serving bowl and set aside.
Simmer the coconut milk, sugar, and salt in a pan over low-medium heat for 2-3 minutes, until the sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from the heat.
Divide the vermicelli among serving bowls and pour over the coconut milk mixture.
Top with the ginger, garlic, dried-shrimp flakes, diced pineapple, and chili sauce.

title: Corn in Coconut Milk
ingredients: 100 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a pan over medium heat.
Add the sugar and salt and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add the corn, stir gently, and return to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 4-5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Serve hot or cold.

title: Corn with Young Coconut
ingredients: 80 g shredded fresh coconut, or 40 g dry unsweetened desiccated coconut
steps: If using dried coconut, wrap it in cheesecloth and steam for 10 minutes, until hydrated and softened. Let cool.
Boil the corn for 10-12 minutes, then drain and slice the kernels from the cobs.
Mix the corn and coconut, reserving some coconut for decoration. Add the sugar and salt and stir together. Decorate with the reserved coconut and serve.

title: Corn and Pandan Pudding
ingredients: 1 kg banana leaves, cut into 15 cm circles
steps: Prepare 15-20 banana-leaf cups. For each cup, place 2 banana-leaf circles back to back with the shiny sides facing outward. Fold up about 3 cm of leaf at the edge and fold it inward on itself to form a corner. Secure with a toothpick or staple and repeat to make four corners.
For the filling, combine the mung bean flour, sugar, corn, pandan extract, and 250 ml water in a pan.
Cook over low-medium heat, stirring continuously for 7-8 minutes, until thick and transparent.
Fill each banana-leaf cup with about 1 tablespoon filling, leaving about 5 mm headspace. Set aside.
For the topping, combine the coconut milk, rice flour, salt, and sugar in a pan.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly for 6-7 minutes, until thickened.
Top each filled cup with about ½ tablespoon topping, let cool, and serve.

title: Steamed Rice Flour Topped with Coconut Flesh
ingredients: meat of 2 coconuts, cut into thin strips
steps: Bring 475 ml water and the sugar to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Stir until the sugar has dissolved and the mixture is syrupy, then remove from the heat and let cool. Sprinkle 120 ml water onto the rice flour to dampen it, then sift this wet rice flour through a strainer (sieve) into a bowl. Wrap the powdered rice flour in cheesecloth (muslin) and steam in a steamer for 10 minutes, then transfer to a large bowl and let cool.

Gradually add the cold sugar syrup to the cold steamed rice flour and mix well with a spatula. Mix the coconut flesh and salt together in a bowl, then stir into the rice flour mixture until combined. Transfer to a serving bowl and garnish with jasmine Flowers. Serve.

title: Golden Egg Teardrops
ingredients: 10-12 jasmine flowers or 1¼ teaspoons jasmine essence
steps: To make the jasmine water, bring 950 ml water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Let cool and transfer to a large bowl. Add the jasmine flowers, cover, and let steep overnight. The next day, remove and discard the flowers.
For the syrup, mix the sugar with the jasmine water, or jasmine essence, and pandan leaf in a pan over medium-low heat, then bring to a boil.
Meanwhile, strain the egg yolks through cheesecloth into a bowl. Whisk until thick, smooth, and pale yellow, taking care not to overwhisk. Add the flour and gently fold until well mixed.
When the syrup starts boiling, remove and discard the pandan leaf.

Use the narrow grooved handle of a noodle spoon or a teaspoon to scrape ½ teaspoon egg mixture onto another spoon, then use your thumb to push the mixture into the boiling syrup. Repeat, keeping the syrup boiling, until all the mixture is used or there is no room on the surface. The egg mixture should form teardrops.
Cook the teardrops in the syrup for 4-5 minutes, then remove them with a slotted spoon and transfer to a bowl.
Pour about 120 ml syrup over the egg teardrops. Let cool, then remove the teardrops from the syrup with a slotted spoon and serve.

title: Coconut Custard with Fried Shallots
ingredients: 1.5 kg jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
13 duck eggs or 15 hen eggs, beaten
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F/180°C/Gas Mark 4. Grease a 30 cm square baking pan. Mix the coconut milk, flour, sugar, and eggs together in a bowl until thoroughly combined. Pour the mixture into a pan and cook over medium heat for 7 minutes, stirring frequently. Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan and bake for 15 minutes or until golden brown. Sprinkle with the fried shallots, cut into squares, and serve.

title: Job's Tears and Young Coconut Porridge
ingredients: 215 g Job's tear seeds (Chinese pearl barley)
steps: Rinse and soak the Job's tear seeds in a bowl of water overnight. The next day, drain and rinse. Transfer to a large pan, add 950 ml water, cover with a lid, and cook over low heat for about 1 hour or until cooked. Drain and rinse the Job's tears again and return to the pan. Add the coconut water and bring to a boil over medium heat. Add the sliced coconut, sugar, and half the salt, and stir until the sugar and salt have dissolved Dissolve the cornstarch (cornflour) and the arrowroot starch in 60 ml water. Stir half of the mixture into the pan and cook until thick. Remove from the heat.

Bring the coconut cream to a boil in another pan over medium heat. Add the remaining salt and stir for about 2 minutes or until the salt has dissolved. Add the rest of the cornstarch mixture and stir until thickened. Remove from the heat.
Put the Job's tears into small serving bowls and pour over the coconut cream. Serve.

title: Sweet Glutinous Rice with Dried Shrimp
ingredients: 1 kg banana leaves, cut into 15 cm circles
steps: Pound the turmeric in a large mortar. Add 2 liters water, mix, then strain through cheesecloth into a large bowl and discard the residue.
Add the rice to the turmeric water, cover, and soak overnight or for at least 3 hours.
Wrap the soaked rice in cheesecloth and steam for 30-35 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until cooked and translucent.
Prepare banana-leaf cups by placing two leaf circles back to back, shiny sides outward. Fold and secure four corners with toothpicks or staples.
Bring the coconut milk to a boil over low-medium heat. Add the salt and sugar and stir until dissolved.
Add the rice and cook for 3-4 minutes, until thoroughly combined. Remove from the heat, cover, and rest for 10 minutes.
For the topping, dry-fry the coconut in a wok over medium heat for 1-2 minutes, stirring continuously, until it begins to color.
Add the dried shrimp, sugar, and fried shallots and stir until combined.
Spoon the rice into the banana-leaf cups, sprinkle with the topping, and serve.

title: Caramel
ingredients: 1 kg jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Soak the rice in a large bowl of water overnight or for at least 3 hours. Wash and drain. Wrap the rice in cheesecloth (muslin) and steam in a steamer for 30-35 minutes, stirring the rice every 10 minutes until cooked through. The rice will look transparent when cooked. Mix the rice flour with the steamed rice in another pan, then add the coconut milk and sugar and cook over low heat for 2-3 hours or until sticky. Let cool in a casserole dish, then cut into 4 cm squares and serve.

title: Sweet Coconut Balls
ingredients: ½ teaspoon salt, plus extra for rolling
300 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
880 g shredded fresh coconut, plus 40 g for rolling
steps: Mix the flour, coconut milk, and salt in a bowl, then knead by hand until the dough is sticky. Cover with plastic wrap and set aside.
Bring the sugar to a simmer in a wok over low heat for 2-3 minutes, until softened. Add 80 g shredded coconut and stir-fry until dry. Remove from the heat.

Spread the remaining coconut and a little salt on a plate. Roll out the dough and cut small circles with a cookie cutter. Put a teaspoon of filling in the center of each circle and mold the dough around it to form a ball.
Bring a large pan of water to a boil. Carefully add the balls and cook for 4-5 minutes, until they float. Drain, roll in the salted shredded coconut, and serve.

title: Black Beans in Coconut Milk
ingredients: 15 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Soak the beans in a bowl of water for 2 hours, then drain, rinse, and put into a pan. Pour in enough water to cover and bring to a boil over medium heat. Boil for 50-60 minutes or until softened. Drain and transfer to a clean pan. Add the coconut milk and 75 ml water and bring to a boil over medium heat. When the mixture is boiling, add both sugars and the salt and stir until the sugars have dissolved. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 30 minutes or until the beans are fully flavored. Remove from the heat and serve.

title: Coconut Rice Balls
steps: Mix the cooked rice, three-quarters of the coconut, the sugar, and salt together in a large bowl.
Scoop out a teaspoon of the mixture, roll it into a ball, and place on a plate. Repeat with the remaining mixture.
Sprinkle with the remaining coconut and serve.

title: Sweet Glutinous Rice with Black Beans
ingredients: 75 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: For the rice, soak the rice in water overnight, or for at least 3 hours. Drain and rinse, then wrap in cheesecloth and steam for 20 minutes.
Pour the coconut milk into a pan, add the salt and granulated sugar, and gradually bring to a boil. Remove from the heat and reserve three-quarters of the sweet coconut milk for topping.
Put the rice and remaining sweet coconut milk into another pan, mix well, cover, and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes. Pour the reserved sweet coconut milk over the rice.
For the beans, rinse them under cold running water, put them in a pan, and cover with 950 ml water. Bring to a boil and cook for about 20 minutes, until soft.
Bring the coconut milk to a boil in another pan over low heat. Add the salt and both sugars and stir, then add the black beans and stir until mixed.
Pour the beans over the rice and serve.

title: Glutinous Rice Roasted in Bamboo
ingredients: bamboo stalks, about 2 inches/S om in diameter, and cut into 30 cm long pieces
steps: Soak the rice in a bowl of water for about 2 hours, then drain and set aside Soak the beans in a bowl of water for 2 hours, then drain, rinse, and put into a pan. Pour in enough water to cover and bring to a boil over medium heat. Reduce the heat and simmer for about 30 minutes. Remove from the heat and mix with the rice. Spoon the mixture into the bamboo stalks until three-quarters full.

Before you begin cooking, check that your charcoal is glowing white hot. Bring the coconut milk, sugar, and salt to a boil over medium heat and stir until the sugar has dissolved. Remove from the heat and carefully pour into the bamboo stalks. Cover with the banana leaf and cook over the charcoal fire for 2½-3 hours. Remove from the heat, carefully split the bamboo stalks open, and serve.

title: Glutinous Rice in Coconut Shell
prepTime: 10 minutes plus soaking time and resting time
ingredients: 50 g cooled black beans or red beans
50 g arrowroot starch or tapioca flour
steps: Soak the rice in a large bowl of cold water overnight or for at least 3 hours. Wash and drain. Wrap the rice in cheesecloth (muslin) and steam in a steamer for 30-35 minutes. stirring the rice every 10 minutes until cooked through. The rice will look transparent when cooked. Set aside.
Heat the coconut milk, sugar, and salt in a pan over medium heat and simmer, stirring, until the sugar has dissolved.

Put the steamed rice into a bowl and add the black or red beans. Sprinkle with half the sweetened coconut milk and stir until thoroughly combined. Let rest for 10 minutes. Open the young coconuts, remove the flesh with a spoon, keeping the shells intact. Set the shells aside. Shred the coconut flesh, add to the rice and bean mixture, and stir until well mixed. Set aside. Preheat the oven to 425°F/220°C/Gas Mark 7.

Mix the starch or flour with the remaining sweetened coconut milk in a pan and simmer over low heat for a few minutes or until thickened. Add the mixture to the rice and coconut mixture, then pour into the coconut shells and bake for 10-15 minutes. Serve.

title: Glutinous Rice in Tiger Grass Leaf
steps: Soak the rice in a bowl of water overnight or for at least 3 hours, then drain, rinse under cold running water, and drain again. Transfer to a bowl and set aside.

Soak the beans in another bowl of water for 2 hours, then drain, rinse, and put into a pan. Pour in enough water to cover and bring to a boil over medium heat. Boil for 50-60 minutes or until softened.

Add the beans to the rice and mix together thoroughly, then add the sugar and salt Lay a tiger grass leaf on a flat work surface. Put a 1 cm mound of the rice and bean mixture into the center of the leaf. Fold the leaf into a triangular shape and secure with a bamboo strip. Repeat until all the filling is used. Bring 3 liters water to a boil in a large pan, add the packages, reduce the heat, and simmer for 30 minutes. Remove the packages with a slotted spoon, let cool slightly, then serve.

title: Sweet Glutinous Rice in Banana Leaf
ingredients: Banana leaves, cut into 18-20 cm-wide strips
steps: Soak the rice in water overnight or for at least 3 hours. Drain, rinse under cold running water, and drain again.
Soak the beans in a separate bowl of water for 2 hours. Drain, rinse, and place in a pan with enough water to cover.
Bring the beans to a boil over medium heat and boil for 50-60 minutes, until softened.
Mix the coconut milk, sugar, and salt in a bowl, then strain through cheesecloth into a clean bowl.
Combine the rice and sweetened coconut milk in a wok over medium heat. Stir continuously for about 10 minutes, until the rice begins to cook. Remove from the heat.
Peel the bananas and cut each in half lengthwise.
Lay a banana leaf on a flat work surface. Put 1 tablespoon rice and 10 black beans in the center. Cover with 2 banana halves and top with another spoonful of rice.
Fold the leaf around the filling and secure with string to form a package. Repeat until all the filling is used.
Steam the packages for 40-45 minutes, then serve.

title: Crispy Stuffed Buns
ingredients: 100 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
150 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: For the filling, soak the mung beans in water for 2 hours.
For the dough, mix the flours together. Gradually add 120-175 ml water and knead until a dough forms. Add the coconut and sugar and knead until sticky enough to shape.

Drain the mung beans, wrap them in cheesecloth, and steam for 25 minutes, or until cooked. Melt the sugar in a wok over low heat for 2-3 minutes. Add the coconut and mung beans and cook until dry enough to shape into 2.5 cm balls.
Roll the dough to 2 mm thick and cut into 6 cm circles. Put a ball of filling in the center of each circle and enclose it with the dough.
Heat the oil for deep-frying to 350°F/180°C. Fry the buns in batches for 7-8 minutes, or until crisp and golden. Drain on paper towels and serve.

title: Sugar-Coated Stuffed Dough Balls
prepTime: 10–15 minutes, plus soaking and resting time
ingredients: 1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: For the filling, soak the mung beans in a bowl of water for 30 minutes. Drain, rinse, and drain again. Wrap the mung beans in cheesecloth (muslin) and steam over medium heat for 20 minutes, or until cooked. Remove from the cheesecloth and let cool. Process the mung beans in a food processor and set aside.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the shallot and stir-fry for 1 minute, or until softened. Add the mung beans, sugar, salt, and white pepper, reduce the heat to medium-low, then stir until the sugar has dissolved and the mixture is thoroughly combined. Remove from the heat and set aside.

To make the dough, mix the rice flour, glutinous rice flour, and salt together in a large bowl. Add the sugar and crumble it into the flour mixture. Gradually pour in the coconut milk and 120 ml water, a little at a time, crumbling and mixing the flour mixture into the liquid with your other hand. Keep kneading until a smooth dough forms, adding a little more water if it is too dry. Cover with plastic wrap and rest for 20 minutes.
When the filling is cool, roll portions just under a tablespoon each into balls. Divide the dough into small portions and roll these into balls as well.

Working with one dough ball at a time, flatten it with your thumb from the center outward to form a circle about 3 mm thick and 6 cm in diameter. Put a ball of filling in the middle, wrap the dough around it, and squeeze and tap the seam closed. Gently roll into a ball and repeat with the remaining dough and filling.

Heat the oil for deep-frying to 180°C (350°F), or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the dough balls in batches for about 8 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.

Bring the superfine sugar and 120 ml water to a boil in a clean wok over medium heat. Boil for about 2½ minutes, or until thickened. Remove from the heat, immediately add the fried dough balls, and stir until coated in the sugar syrup. Remove with a slotted spoon, let cool slightly, and serve.

title: Mung Bean Porridge with Coconut Milk
steps: Soak the mung beans in a bowl of water for 2 hours, then drain and rinse. Put the beans in cheesecloth (muslin) and steam in a steamer for 25 minutes or until cooked. Set aside.
Mix the coconut cream, rice flour, and salt together in a pan and cook over low heat for 3-4 minutes or until thickened. Set aside.

Bring 750 ml water to a boil in another pan. Add the sugar and stir until dissolved. Mix the tapioca flour, arrowroot flour, and 0 ml water together in a bowl. Continue to stir the sugar mixture in the pan and gradually pour in the flour mixture. Stir and cook for 1-2 minutes or until thickened. Add the mung beans, then stir and cook for another 3-4 minutes or until the mung beans are fully flavored. Transfer to serving bowls, pour over the coconut cream mixture, and serve.

title: Sweet Mung Bean Packages
ingredients: 45 g shredded fresh or dry unsweetened (desiccated) coconut
steps: Soak the mung beans in a bowl of water for 2 hours, then drain and rinse. Wrap the beans and coconut in separate pieces of cheesecloth and steam for 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, mix the sugar, salt, and sesame seeds together in a small bowl and set aside.
Mix the flour and 250 ml water in a bowl until a dough forms. Knead until soft and smooth. Pinch off pieces and shape into small balls.

Bring a large pan of water to a boil. Add the dough balls one by one and boil for 5 minutes, or until cooked and floating. Remove with a slotted spoon and transfer to a large bowl. Add a small amount of water to prevent them sticking together.

Spread the steamed mung beans and coconut on separate plates. Flatten each dough ball into a 1 cm-thick patty. Place 1-2 teaspoons mung beans in the center and wrap the edges over the filling to form an oval package.

Squeeze the edges to seal, roll in the steamed mung beans, and place on a serving plate. Repeat with the remaining patties. Cover with the steamed coconut, sprinkle with the sugar and sesame mixture, and serve.

title: Colorful Mung Bean Noodles in Coconut Milk
ingredients: 195 g mung bean starch (mung bean flour)
225 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
Thai scented dessert candle, for smoking
steps: Divide the mung bean starch (flour) into 3 equal portions to make sa-lim noodles in different colors. For the green noodles, mix 65 g starch, the pandan juice, and 250 ml water together until thoroughly combined. For red noodles, mix 65 g starch, the red food coloring, and 600 ml water together until thoroughly combined. For white noodles, mix 85 g starch and 600 ml water together until thoroughly combined Fill a large pan with cold water and set aside. Heat the first portion of starch in a separate pan over low heat for 7-9 minutes, stirring until translucent and shiny. When cooked pour the mixture into a sa-lim mold or a potato ricer and slowly press the mixture through the mold, letting it drop into the pan of cold water The mixture should resemble noodles. Let soak in the cold water for at least 10 minutes then drain and wrap in cheesecloth (muslin). Transfer to a plate and set aside. Repeat with the second and third starch portions. Heat the sugars, salt, and coconut milk in another pan over low heat, stirring, for about 5 minutes or until the sugars have dissolved.

Place the candle in a small bowl on a plate. Light both ends of the candle and let stand for 2 minutes, Blow out the candle and wait until the black smoke disappears and you can smell the aroma, then quickly put the candle still in the bowl on a plate into the pan of coconut milk syrup, cover with a lid, and let smoke for 10-15 minutes. This process can be repeated as many as 5-6 times for a more intense aroma. The candle can be used again if there is still some left after the dessert has been scented.
To serve, divide the different color mung bean noodles among serving bowls, pour the aromatic coconut milk over them, and add ice cubes.

title: Mung Bean Custard with Fried Shallots
ingredients: 10 shallots, halved lengthwise and finely sliced
225 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Soak the mung beans in a bowl of water for 2 hours, then drain and rinse. Put the beans in cheesecloth (muslin) and steam in a steamer for 25 minutes or until cooked. Pound the beans in a mortar with a pestle until fine, then transfer to a bowl and set aside.

For the crispy shallots, heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the shallots, and fry for 10-12 minutes or until golden brown. Set aside and reserve 2 tablespoons of the fried oil Preheat the oven to 400°F/200°C/Gas Mark 6. Grease a 30 cm round baking pan with butter or oil. Beat the eggs in a large bowl, then add the sugar, salt, and rice flour and mix well until the sugar has dissolved. Add the coconut milk, all but 1 tablespoon of the crispy shallots, and the reserved fried oil and mix well. Pour into the bowl containing the mung beans and mix well. Heat the mixture in a pan over low heat for about 5 minutes stirring continuously until smooth. Pour the mixture into the greased pan. Bake for 30 minutes or until the mixture has risen and turned golden brown on top. Let cool slightly, then remove from the pan and sprinkle with the reserved crispy shallots. Serve.

title: Mung Bean Pudding with Ginkgo
steps: Soak the mung beans in water for 2 hours, then drain and rinse.
Bring 750 ml water to a boil in a pan. Add the mung beans and cook for 15 minutes, until softened.
Add the sugar and ginkgo nuts and cook for another 10 minutes.
Remove from the heat and transfer to a serving bowl.
Bring the coconut cream and salt to a boil in another pan over low-medium heat. Pour over the mung bean pudding and serve.

title: Tapioca Balls in Coconut Milk
ingredients: 120 g tapioca flour, plus extra for coating
steps: Sift the tapioca flour and rice flour into a bowl. Add about 120 ml tepid water and stir until a dough forms.
Let cool, knead, then pinch off small pieces and roll into balls. Press each ball on a krong krang or gnocchi press, or with a fork. Coat lightly in tapioca flour to prevent sticking.
Bring 2 liters water to a boil in a large pan. Add the tapioca balls and cook for 3 minutes, until transparent.
Remove with a slotted spoon and place in a large bowl of cold water for 4-5 minutes. Transfer to a plate and set aside.
Bring the sugar, salt, and coconut cream to a boil in another pan, stirring occasionally.
Add the tapioca balls and cook for 4-5 minutes.
Transfer to serving bowls, sprinkle with the sesame seeds, and serve.

title: Tapioca Dessert with Peanuts
ingredients: 225 g packed soft light brown sugar
steps: Grease a shallow square baking pan with oil.
Mix the flours and 475 ml water together in a large bowl.
Pour the batter into a pan and simmer over low heat for 10 minutes, stirring frequently.
Transfer to the greased baking pan and let cool. Cut into 2.5 cm squares and place on a serving plate.
For the syrup, combine the sugar and 120 ml water in a pan over medium heat and simmer, stirring, for 5 minutes, or until syrupy.
Pour the syrup over the squares, sprinkle with the ground peanuts, and serve.

title: Dried Rice Balls
ingredients: 300 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Put the sugar and jasmine water in a bowl and mix well. Transfer to a pan and put over medium heat. Stir continuously for 3-5 minutes until the sugar mixture begins to thicken. Add the shredded coconut and stir continuously until all the sugar has been absorbed and the coconut has become sticky. Remove from the heat and let cool.
Spread the rice out on a plate. Use a tablespoon or damp hands to shape the cold coconut mixture into bite-size balls, then roll the balls in the ground rice.

title: Red Glutinous Rice with Sesame Seeds
ingredients: 275 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1 heaping tablespoon white sesame seeds, roasted
banana leaves, cut into 15 cm diameter circles
steps: Soak the rice in a large bowl of cold water overnight or for at least 3 hours. Wash and drain. Wrap the rice in cheesecloth (muslin) and steam in a steamer for 30 minutes, stirring the rice every 10 minutes, until cooked through, Dry the steamed rice and let cool.

Prepare the banana-leaf cups. For each cup, place 2 banana leaf circles back to back with the shiny surface face outward on both sides. From the outside of the circle, fold up 3 cm of banana leal and then fold in on itself to create a corner. Secure with a toothpick or use a stapler. Repeat until there are 4 corners.
Simmer the coconut milk and sugar in a wok over medium heat until it begins to thicken. Add the rice and stir until the rice becomes light, dry, and crispy, about 15-20 minutes.
Carefully spoon the mixture into the banana leaf cups and let cool. Sprinkle with the sesame seeds and serve.

title: Glutinous Rice Balls in Coconut Milk
ingredients: For the green rice flour balls
For the yellow rice flour balls
For the purple rice flour balls
50 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: To make the green rice balls, smash the pandan leaves in a mortar with a pestle, then pound to a paste. Add 250 ml water and instantly squeeze with your hands to get 3 tablespoons thick pand an juice. Mix the glutinous (sticky) rice flour and pandan juice together in a bowl to form a sticky dough, then knead. Gradually add 120 ml water to the dough until no longer sticky. Divide the dough into small portions and roll into balls Set aside.

For the yellow rice balls, steam the pumpkin in a steamer for 3 minutes or until soft, let cool, then pound in a mortar with a pestle. Mix the rice flour and pounded pumpkin together in a bowl, then knead. Gradually add 120 ml water to the dough until no longer sticky. Divide the dough into small portions and roll into balls. Set aside.

For the purple rice balls, steam the taro in a steamer for 3-4 minutes or until soft, let cool, then pound in a mortar with a pestle. Mix the rice flour and the pounded taro in a bowl, then knead. Gradually add 120 ml water to the dough until no longer sticky. Divide the dough into small portions and roll into balls. Set aside. Bring a large pan of water to a boil over medium heat, add the rice balls, and cook for 4-5 minutes or until they float to the surface. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.

For the coconut milk, bring the coconut milk, sugars, salt, pandan leaves, and coconut meat to a boil in a pan. Reduce the heat and cook stirring continuously, for 3-4 minutes. Add the rice flour balls and return to a boil. Remove from the heat and stir in the coconut cream. Serve hot or cold.

title: Ginkgo Nuts and Dates in Longan Syrup
ingredients: 1 packed 225 g soft light brown sugar
steps: Put 3 liters water, the dried longans, dried jujube, and ginkgo in a large pan and bring to a boil over medium heat. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for about 15 minutes, adding more water if necessary. Add the sugar to taste, then transfer to a heatproof serving bowl and serve.

title: Ginkgo Nuts, Taro, and Coconut Dessert
ingredients: water and meat of 2 young coconuts
steps: Bring 2 liters water and the sugar to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the ginkgo nuts and taro, reduce the heat, and simmer for about 15 minutes, until softened. Add the coconut water and meat and continue to simmer for 5 minutes.
Dissolve the tapioca flour in 2 tablespoons water, then gradually pour into the pan, stirring continuously. Bring to a boil, then remove from the heat and set aside.
Bring the coconut cream to a boil in another pan, add the salt, stir, and return to a boil. Remove from the heat.
Put the ginkgo nuts and coconut meat in small serving bowls and pour the coconut cream over them. Serve.

title: Glutinous Rice with Coconut and Black Sesame
ingredients: 5 banana leaves, cut into 5 x 15 cm strips
steps: Soak the rice in a large bowl of water overnight or for at least 3 hours, then drain.
Lay a banana-leaf strip on a flat work surface. Place a little rice at one end, leaving a 1 cm border.
Fold the leaf and filling diagonally to form a triangle. Continue folding into triangles until the end of the leaf is reached, then secure with toothpicks. Repeat with the remaining rice.
Bring 950 ml water to a boil in a large pan. Carefully add the packages, return to a boil, reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 1 hour.
Remove the packages with a slotted spoon, drain, and let cool.
Combine the coconut, sesame seeds, and sugar in a small bowl.
Unwrap the rice packages and discard the leaves. Roll the rice in the coconut, sesame, and sugar mixture, then serve.

title: Sesame and Sugar-Coated Peanuts
steps: Rinse the peanuts in plenty of cold water, then drain and set aside.

Put 120 ml water, the peanuts, and sugar in a wok over medium heat and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer, stirring continuously for about 20 minutes or until thickened. Be careful not to let the sugar boil and caramelize. Remove from the heat and continue stirring until the sugar cools, dries, and coats the peanuts. Sprinkle with the salt, and put the pan back over medium heat. Stir continuously for about 10 minutes until the sugar coating the peanuts starts to melt again. Add the sesame seeds and stir until the peanuts are well coated, then remove from the heat. Transfer to a large tray and use a spatula to separate the peanuts. Let cool, then serve.

title: Coconut Custard in Pumpkin
ingredients: 175 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Remove the top of the Thai pumpkin by cutting around the stem to create a "lid" 8 cm in diameter. Set the lid aside. Scoop out the seeds with a spoon. Set aside.

Whisk the eggs and coconut cream together in a bowl, add the sugar, salt, and pandan leaves. and mix well. Use your hand to squeeze the mixture until the pandan leaves are soft and aromatic and the sugar has dissolved. Strain through cheesecloth (muslin) or a fine strainer (sieve) and pour into the pumpkin. Fill to just under the top of the pumpkin.

Carefully place the pumpkin and its lid (on the side), into a large steamer, at least twice the size of the pumpkin. Steam over medium heat for 35-40 minutes or until the custard is firm and cooked and the pumpkin is soft Let cool slightly, then serve whole with the reserved lid on top.

title: Pumpkin Custard
ingredients: 450 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
350 g peeled, seeded, and sliced pumpkin batons (4 cm long and 1 cm wide)
steps: Beat the eggs in a bowl until lightly foamy.

Mix the coconut milk and sugar together in another bowl until well blended, then pour into the beaten egg and mix well. Strain the mixture through a strainer (sieve) into a 20 cm square baking pan 5 cm deep. Sprinkle with the pumpkin batons and steam in a steamer over high heat for about 20 minutes or until firm. Let cool, then cut the custard into 16 squares and serve.

title: Sweet Potato in Ginger Syrup
ingredients: 3 sweet potatoes, cut into 4 cm cubes
90 g peeled and sliced fresh ginger (3 cm-thick pieces)
steps: Bring 950 ml water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the sugar and salt and return to a boil for 1-2 minutes. Add the sweet potatoes and ginger and continue to boil for another 10-12 minutes. Remove from the heat and let cool for 10 minutes. Serve hot or cold.

title: Pumpkin in Syrup
ingredients: 1.5 kg pumpkin, peeled and cut into bite-size pieces
steps: Soak the pumpkin in the limewater for about 30 minutes, then rinse and drain.
Bring the coconut cream to a boil in a pan over low heat and add the salt. Add the rice flour and stir occasionally until the coconut milk has thickened.

Bring 350 ml water, the sugar, and lime juice to a boil in another pan over medium heal. Boil, stirring occasionally until the sugar has dissolved, then add the pumpkin. Cook for about 10 minutes until the pumpkin is glossy. Transfer to a serving bowl, pour the coconut milk over the top, and serve.

title: Wax Gourd Dessert
ingredients: 280 g peeled and grated wax gourd
225 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
90 g peeled and grated overripe coconut
Banana leaves, cut into 20 cm-wide strips
steps: Put the grated wax gourd in cheesecloth and squeeze into a bowl to remove any excess liquid. Discard the liquid and put the damp wax gourd flesh in a bowl.
Sprinkle with the tapioca flour and mix well. Add the sugar, grated coconut, and salt and mix again. The mixture should be neither too thick nor too dry.

Lay a banana leaf on a work surface. Put 2 tablespoons of the wax gourd mixture in the center. Cover the filling with the sides of the leaf and fold over the ends to make a package. Secure with toothpicks and repeat with the remaining mixture.
Place the packages in a steamer and steam over high heat for 30 minutes, or until cooked. Let cool, then serve.

title: Coconut Cakes with Herbs
steps: For the batter, mix the rice flour with 475 ml tepid water in a bowl.

Mix the coconut milk, salt, sugar, cilantro (coriander), and scallions (spring onions) together in another bowl Coat the khanom krok pan or pancake puff pan with oil and place over medium heat. The pan is ready when a small drop of batter sizzles. Stir the batter and carefully pour a little into the molds until about two-thirds full, then carefully pour the coconut milk mixture on top to fill the molds. Cover with a lid and cook for about 5 minutes before removing the desserts from the molds with a spoon or fork. Serve.

title: Coconut Milk Custard
ingredients: 250 ml unshaken can coconut milk, cream and mill separated
125 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Season the coconut cream with salt. Set aside.
Mix the coconut milk and the rice flour together in a large bowl, add the sugar, and stir well.
Pour the mixture into small talai cups or small heatproof cups or bowls about three-quarters full and steam in a steamer for 10 minutes until cooked.
Pour the coconut cream over the rice mixture and continue to steam for another 10 minutes until the coconut cream is cooked. Serve.

title: Gelatin in Young Coconut
prepTime: 35 minutes plus setting and chilling time
steps: Strain the water through cheesecloth (muslin) and bring to a boil in a pan. Add the gelatin powder, reduce the heat, and simmer for 5 minutes, Pour the coconut water mixture back into the coconuts and let set for 30 minutes. chill in the refrigerator until ready to serve.

title: Fried Bananas
ingredients: 6-8 semi-ripe small bananas, peeled and sliced into 1 cm lengths
steps: Mix the sugar, flours, coconut, coconut milk, sesame seeds, salt, and 60 ml water together in a large bowl until the sugar and flour have dissolved.
Dip the bananas into the batter and make sure they are well coated.
Heat the oil for deep-frying to 180°C (350°F), or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the bananas for 6-7 minutes, or until golden and crisp.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and serve.

title: Tapioca and Young Coconut in Coconut Milk
steps: Bring 1.2 liters water to a boil in a pan over medium-high heat. Put the tapioca pearls in a strainer (sieve) and dip in water, then shake once. Add to the pan of boiling water and cook for about 7 minutes, stirring occasionally until the tapioca pearls are cooked and translucent. Add the sugar and coconut meat and gently stir until the sugar has dissolved, then remove from the heat.
Heat the coconut milk and salt in another pan over low heat for about 5 minutes. Transfer the tapioca to small serving bowls with the coconut milk on the side.

title: Banana with Shredded Coconut and Sesame Seeds
steps: Mix the shredded coconut and salt together in a small bowl and set aside.

Bring a medium pan of water to a boil, add the bananas, and cook for 20 minutes. Drain the bananas in a colander and cool under cold running water, then slice lengthwise. Put the banana slices into the coconut mixture and roll to coat. Place on a serving plate and sprinkle with sesame seeds and sugar. Serve.

title: Bananas in Syrup
steps: Bring a medium pan of water to a boil, add the bananas, reduce the heat, and simmer for 10 minutes until tender. Remove with a slotted spoon and cut into 2.5 cm-thick slices. Set aside.

Bring the sugar and 350 ml water to a boil in another pan and boil for 3-4 minutes, stirring, until the sugar has dissolved. Add the banana pieces, reduce the heat, and cook for 30 minutes or until the syrup thickens and the bananas turn red. Serve.

title: Glutinous Rice, Beans, and Banana in Palm Leaves
ingredients: 10 small ripe bananas, cut lengthwise into 3 slices
steps: Soak the rice in water for about 1 hour, then drain and set aside.
Bring the coconut milk and salt to a boil in a wok or pan over medium heat.
Add the rice and cook, stirring constantly, for about 5 minutes, until dry.
Add the sugar and stir-fry for another 5 minutes. Remove from the heat, add the black beans, and stir. Let cool.
Lay a palm leaf on a work surface. Place 1 tablespoon rice mixture between 2 thin banana slices on the leaf.
Fold the leaf into a package and secure with toothpicks. Repeat until all the filling is used.
Steam the packages for about 40 minutes, until the rice is sticky, then serve.

title: Banana with Shredded Coconut
steps: Spread the shredded coconut in a shallow bowl or plate.
Steam the unpeeled bananas for about 10 minutes, or until soft and tender. Peel and cut into 2.5 cm pieces, then roll in the coconut until coated.
Mix the sugar and salt in a small bowl, sprinkle over the bananas, and serve.

title: Caramelized Bananas
ingredients: 8 semi-ripe small bananas, peeled, or 4 ordinary bananas, halved crosswise
steps: Bring 475 ml water to a boil in a wok over medium heat. Add the sugar, reduce the heat, and simmer for 5 minutes. Add the pandan leaves, return to a boil, and remove from the heat.

Strain the syrup into a pan and discard the pandan. Add the bananas and simmer over medium-low heat for 12-15 minutes on each side, or until glossy and the syrup is absorbed. Sprinkle with lime juice, remove from the heat, and transfer to a serving plate.
Mix the coconut milk, flour, and salt in a small pan over medium-low heat for 2-3 minutes, or until thickened. Drizzle over the bananas and serve immediately.

title: Sweet Banana
ingredients: 10 ripe small bananas, peeled and mashed
200 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Mix the coconut and salt in a small bowl. Reserve half for the garnish.
Mix the bananas, rice flour, sugar, remaining coconut and salt, and coconut milk in a large bowl.
Pour into small heatproof cups or bowls, sprinkle with the reserved coconut, steam for 30 minutes, and serve.

title: Bananas in Coconut Milk
steps: Dry-fry the mung beans in a wok over low heat for 5 minutes until roasted, shaking and stirring to prevent the beans from burning. Meanwhile, bring a small pan of water to a boil, then add the mung beans and cook for 5 minutes.

Bring another pan of water to a boil, add the bananas, and boil for 10 minutes. Drain and transfer to a bowl of cold water for 3-4 minutes. Drain, then cut the bananas in half lengthwise and then into 2.5 cm slices.
Bring the coconut milk to a simmer in a wok over low heat, add the mung beans, and cook for 10 minutes. Add the salt, sugar, and bananas and cook for another 5 minutes. Serve.

title: Jackfruit and Tapioca Threads in Coconut Milk
ingredients: 100 g tapioca flour, plus extra for sprinkling
steps: For the syrup, bring 175 ml water and the sugar to a boil over medium heat. Stir until the sugar dissolves and the mixture becomes syrupy.
Put the tapioca flour in a large bowl and gradually add 100 ml hot water, stirring quickly. Knead for 5 minutes, until a dough forms.
Divide the dough into 3 portions. Color one green and another red, leaving the third uncolored. Knead each portion separately on a lightly floured work surface.
Bring a pan of water to a boil and have a bowl of cold water ready. Roll each portion into a thin sheet, cut into thin threads, and dust with tapioca flour to prevent sticking.
Boil the threads for 3-4 minutes, until transparent. Remove with a slotted spoon and transfer to the cold water.
Bring the coconut milk and salt to a boil in another pan over medium heat, then remove from the heat.
Divide the tapioca threads and jackfruit among bowls. Pour over the coconut milk and sugar syrup, add a few ice cubes, and serve.

title: Rice Pudding with Longans and Butterfly Pea Flowers
ingredients: 1 small handful fresh butterfly pes flowers
steps: Soak the rice in a bowl of water overnight The next day, drain and rinse under cold running water. Bring 750 ml water to a boil in a pan. Add the rice and butterfly pea flowers and cook for about 15 minutes or until the rice is softened. Add the sugar and longans, then remove the pan from the heat and set aside. Bring the coconut cream to a boil in another pan over low-medium heat, then stir in the salt.
Put the rice mixture into a serving bowl and pour the coconut cream over it. Serve.

title: Tapioca with Longan
steps: Bring 1.2 liters water to a boil in a pan over medium-high heat.

Put the tapioca pearls in a strainer (sieve) and dip in water, then shake once. Add to the pan of boiling water and cook for about 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tapioca pearls are cooked and translucent. Remove from the heat and drain. Return to the pan, add the sugar, and longans, and gently stir until the sugar has dissolved. Heat the coconut milk and salt in another pan over low heat for about 5 minutes. Transfer the tapioca and longan mixture to a serving bowl and pour the coconut milk over it. Serve.

title: Glutinous Rice with Mango
prepTime: 10 minutes, plus soaking and standing time
ingredients: 2 ripe mangoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm-wide slices
steps: Soak the rice in a bowl of water for at least 3 hours, or preferably overnight, then rinse and drain.
Soak the mung beans in a bowl of water for 1 hour. Drain and pat dry with paper towels.
Wrap the rice in cheesecloth and steam for 30-35 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes. The rice will look transparent when cooked.
Put the coconut milk, sugar, and salt in a small pan over low-medium heat and stir until the sugar dissolves. Remove from the heat and set aside, reserving about 75 ml for the topping.
Toast the mung beans in a dry skillet over low-medium heat, stirring frequently, for 5 minutes, or until dark yellow and completely dry.
Transfer the cooked rice to a bowl and add the sweet coconut milk. Mix well, cover, and let stand for 10-15 minutes.
Top the sweet rice with the toasted mung beans and serve with the mango slices and reserved coconut milk.

title: Mangosteen in Syrup
steps: Bring 950 ml water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the sugar and salt and return to a boil for 1-2 minutes or until the sugar has dissolved. Add the mangosteen and continue to boil over low heat until softened. Remove from the heat and let cool. Transfer to a bowl, cover with plastic wrap (clingfilm), and let marinate in the refrigerator for 24 hours.
Remove the mangosteen from the refrigerator, add crushed ice, and serve cold.

title: Pandan Leaf Noodles in Coconut Milk Syrup
ingredients: 250 ml limewater (see p. 509) or club soda (soda water)
225 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Blend the pandan leaves with 750 ml water until thoroughly combined. Strain through a very fine sieve or cheesecloth and reserve the extract.
Mix the flours together, then gradually stir in the limewater or club soda until a dough forms. Knead for 4-5 minutes, then add the pandan extract and mix until smooth.

Prepare a large bowl of ice-cold water. Cook the flour mixture in a nonstick pan or wok over medium heat for 6-7 minutes, stirring until it begins to thicken. Reduce the heat and stir for another 4-5 minutes, until thick, dark green, glossy, and syrupy. Adjust with a little water if necessary.
Transfer the mixture to a potato ricer and press the strands into the ice water. Leave for 5-7 minutes, or until firm, then transfer to a clean bowl with a slotted spoon.
For the syrup, heat the coconut milk, sugar, and salt over low heat for about 5 minutes, or until the sugar dissolves. Remove from the heat and cool.
Divide the pandan noodles among bowls, pour over the cooled coconut milk syrup, top with ice cubes, and serve.

title: Candied Sugar Palm Fruit
steps: Rinse the sugar palm fruit and scrub its skin with the shredded banana leaf to remove its grease, then rinse again under cold running water.
Mix the ground alum and 1 liter water together in a large bowl. Soak the sugar palm fruit in the alum water for 30 minutes, then remove and rinse under cold running water.
Bring a pan of water to a boil, add the sugar palm fruit, and boil for 5 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.

To prepare the sugar syrup, mix 5 liters water and 600 g of the sugar together in a pan and bring to a boil. Add the sugar palm fruit, reduce the heat, and simmer over medium heat for 1-2 hours. Add more water if necessary. Gradually add the remaining sugar until the fruit has absorbed the sugar and become shiny. Let cool, then serve the candied fruit on the whole banana leaf.

title: Muskmelon in Coconut Milk
ingredients: 225 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1 muskmelon or cantaloupe, peeled, seeded, and cut into bite-size pieces
steps: Heat the coconut milk in a pan over low heat. Add the sugar and salt and stir continuously until it reaches a gentle boil. Remove from the heat and let cool.
Put about I cubes of muskmelon or cantaloupe into a serving bowl. Add the coconut milk syrup and some crushed ice cubes and serve.

title: Pandan Pudding
ingredients: 250 ml limewater (see p. 508) or club soda
75 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Grease a baking sheet with oil and set aside.
Put the pandan leaves and 250 ml water in a food processor and blend until smooth.
Mix the flours together in a wok or pan, then gradually add the limewater or club soda, stirring constantly.
Add the pandan juice and stir until smooth. Add both sugars and stir until thoroughly combined.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture begins to cook. Reduce the heat slightly and continue stirring for 7-8 minutes in total, until shiny, solid, and dark green.
Pour onto the prepared baking sheet and spread evenly with a spatula. Let cool.
Cut into 6 cm squares, remove from the tray, sprinkle with the grated coconut, and serve.

title: Pandan and Coconut Milk Gelatin
prepTime: 8 minutes, plus setting and chilling time
steps: To make the coconut gelatin (jelly), heat the coconut milk in a pan to 104-122°F/40-50°C, then add the gelatin powder. Stir until the gelatin melts, then add the salt. Stir and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat, add the sugar, and stir until the sugar has dissolved. Fill a shallow tray halfway with the mixture and let cool at room temperature for about 25 minutes. To make the pandan gelatin, heat 750 ml water in a pan to 104-122°F/ 40-50°C and add the gelatin powder. Stir until the gelatin melts, then bring to a boil over low heat and continue to stir. Reduce the heat, add the sugar, and stir until the sugar has dissolved. Pour in the pandan juice and stir to combine When the coconut gelatin starts to set, pour the pandan gelatin on top, and set aside at room temperature for about 25 minutes or until set, then chill in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes or until firm. To serve, cut the gelatin into squares with a serrated knife and transfer to serving plates.

title: Crispy Fried Whole Fish with Roasted Chile and Garlic Sauce
ingredients: 35 g long red chile, finely chopped
steps: Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 180°C, or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the snapper for 7 minutes, until golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and place on a serving plate.
Heat the sunflower oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the shallots and stir-fry for 5 minutes, until fragrant and reduced by about half. Add the garlic and stir-fry for 3-5 minutes, until soft.

Add the chile and stir for 1 minute, then add the broth, cherry tomatoes, tamarind puree, fish sauce, and sugar. Stir briefly and pour over the fish. Garnish with the chiles and kaffir lime leaves and serve.

title: Green Papaya Salad
ingredients: 2 tablespoons grated jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: Shred the green papaya and immediately soak it in iced water for 5 minutes. Drain and refrigerate until ready to use.
Pound the sugar, garlic, and chiles in a mortar until almost paste-like, using a large spoon to scoop and toss the mixture.
Add the green beans, peanuts, and dried shrimp and pound until lightly flattened and crushed.
Add the tomatoes and gently crush them so the juices release without completely breaking them down.
Add the fish sauce and lime juice and pound and toss until the sugar dissolves.
Add the shredded papaya, toss until well mixed, and serve.

title: Beef Satay
steps: Put the lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, sugar, and spices in a blender and process until smooth. Transfer to a bowl, add the coconut milk, and mix well.
Add the beef to the marinade and turn until well coated. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 2 hours.
Preheat the broiler (grill). Thread the marinated beef onto skewers and broil for 5 minutes on each side, until cooked. Serve.

title: Spaghetti with Pork, Chile, and Basil
ingredients: 25 g holy or sweet basil leaves
steps: Put the chiles and garlic in a mortar and crush with a pestle.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the crushed garlic and chile and stir-fry for 1 minute, or until golden brown.
Add the pork and stir-fry for about 5 minutes, until cooked. Season with the fish sauce, soy sauce, and sugar, then toss to mix well.
Add the cooked spaghetti, basil, and kaffir lime leaves and serve.

title: Stir-Fried Rice Noodles with Northern Thailand Chili Paste
ingredients: 10 dried chiles, or fewer for a milder dish
steps: Soak the noodles in water for about 10 minutes, or according to the package directions, until soft. Drain and set aside.
Blend the dried chiles, shallots, and garlic until smooth.
Heat the oil in a skillet over high heat for 10 seconds. Add the chile mixture and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes. Add the chicken and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until cooked through.

Add the cherry tomatoes, shrimp paste, sugar, and fish sauce and stir to combine. Pat the noodles with paper towels to remove excess moisture, add them to the pan, and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes, until soft.
Garnish with the cilantro and scallion and serve.

title: Thai Calamari
ingredients: 200 g squid, cut into small strips
1 teaspoon chopped green and red bell pepper
steps: Blend the lemongrass and cilantro roots until combined, then transfer to a bowl.
Mix the cornstarch, egg yolk, and salt in another bowl to make a batter. Add the squid to the lemongrass mixture and stir until coated.
Heat the oil for deep-frying to 180°C. Dip the coated squid into the batter, then deep-fry in batches for 2-3 minutes, until crisp and golden. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.

For the garnish, heat 1 teaspoon oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the bell pepper, onion, chiles, lemongrass, and lime leaves and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes. Place the squid on a serving plate, garnish with the stir-fried vegetables, and serve.

title: Charcoal Grilled Blowfish Tails with Seafood Nam Prik
ingredients: 1 tablespoon chopped cilantro (coriander) leaves and stems
2½ teaspoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar, softened in a microwave
steps: Blend all the marinade ingredients until smooth. Pour into a bowl, add the blowfish tails, cover, and marinate for at least 45 minutes.
For the dipping sauce, mix the garlic, cilantro, chiles, and softened sugar in a bowl. Add the lime juice, vinegar, fish sauce, olive oil, lime zest, and salt and whisk until thoroughly combined.

Heat a charcoal grill until the coals are glowing white, or preheat a gas grill to 190°C. Grill the fish over medium-high heat for about 4 minutes on each side, until lightly charred and cooked through. Serve with the seafood dipping sauce.

title: Coconut Sundae with Palm Sugar Whipped Cream and Sweet and Salty Peanuts
ingredients: 4 tablespoons freshly grated coconut meat, toasted
For the palm sugar whipped cream
85 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
steps: For the whipped cream, briefly microwave the palm sugar in a heatproof bowl to melt it. Gently warm the cream over low heat, then whisk in the melted sugar. Remove from the heat, cool quickly, and whip to soft peaks.
For the candied peanuts, bring 950 ml water and 800 g of the sugar to a boil over medium heat. Add the peanuts and boil for 4 minutes. Drain, then toss in the remaining sugar.

Heat the oil for deep-frying to 180°C. Shake the excess sugar from the peanuts and deep-fry for 2 minutes, or until golden. Remove with a slotted spoon, spread in a single layer on a baking sheet, and season with flaky sea salt.
To assemble, place a scoop of coconut ice cream in each dish. Top with the whipped cream, toasted coconut, and candied peanuts. Decorate with a wafer and serve.

title: Broiled Beef Salad with Mangosteen and Chili Mint Dressing
ingredients: 1½ teaspoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
Fresh fruits and vegetables, such as cabbage, mint sprigs, green beans, and small purple apple eggplants, to serve
steps: For the dressing, pound the garlic, mint, chiles, and shrimp paste to a very fine paste. Add both sugars and fish sauce to taste, followed by the lime juice and coconut cream. The dressing should be hot, sour, salty, pleasantly sweet, and strongly fragrant with mint.
Preheat the broiler (grill) to high. Broil the beef for 3-5 minutes on both sides, or until medium-rare. Let rest, then slice.

Put the mint, cilantro, shallots, lemongrass, and mangosteen in a bowl. Add a generous amount of dressing and toss lightly. Add the beef, drizzle over a little more dressing, and finish with the kaffir lime leaves. Serve with the fruits, vegetables, and a sprig of mint.

title: Stir-Fried Pork with Santol
ingredients: 1½ teaspoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
4 red and green chiles, seeded and sliced lengthwise
steps: For the paste, pound the cilantro roots, chiles, shallots, garlic, and shrimp paste to a coarse paste.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-low heat. Add the paste and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the pork, increase the heat slightly, and cook for 1-2 minutes, until almost cooked. Season with the sugar and a little fish sauce, then add enough broth to loosen the mixture.

Add the santol, kaffir lime leaves, and chiles and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until the sauce is thick enough to coat. Finish with lime juice. It should taste hot, sour, and equally sweet and salty; adjust the seasoning and serve.

title: "Yam" Meringue with Beef Tartare and Herbs
origin: Henrik Yde-Andersen, Sra Bua by Kiin Kiin
ingredients: 200 g very fresh beef tenderloin or mignon fillet, finely chopped
steps: Beat the egg whites in a large bowl, slowly adding the confectioners' sugar, fish sauce, and lime juice until the mixture has balanced sweet-and-sour flavor and forms stiff peaks.
Process the chile in a small food processor or spice grinder until smooth, then fold it into the meringue. Set aside.
For the tartare, combine the fish sauce and beef in a bowl. Cover and marinate for 5 minutes.
Arrange the meringue in a bowl, add the beef to one side, sprinkle with the shallot and herbs, and serve.
